3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktassa tu vaitālo mahākāleśvarasthitaḥ ..
śivaṃ manasi saṃsthāpya rājñānamidamabravīt..
vikramādityabhūpāla śṛṇu gāthāṃ manoramām ..
vārāṇasī purī ramyā maheśo yatra tiṣṭhati .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्तस्स तु वैतालो महाकालेश्वरस्थितः ॥
शिवं मनसि संस्थाप्य राज्ञानमिदमब्रवीत्॥
विक्रमादित्यभूपाल शृणु गाथां मनोरमाम् ॥
वाराणसी पुरी रम्या महेशो यत्र तिष्ठति ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Thus addressed, that vetāla, remaining at Mahākāleśvara, / fixed Śiva in his mind and spoke thus to the king: / 'O King Vikramāditya, hear a charming tale! / There is the lovely city of Vārāṇasī, where Maheśa resides, 2

3.2.s:
cāturvarṇyaprajā yatra pratāpamukuṭo nṛpaḥ ..
mahādevī ca mahiṣī dharmajñasya mahīpateḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यप्रजा यत्र प्रतापमुकुटो नृपः ॥
महादेवी च महिषी धर्मज्ञस्य महीपतेः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: where the subjects belong to the four classes, and where Pratāpamukuṭa was king, / and Mahādevī was the chief queen of that earth-ruler who knew righteousness. 3

3.2.s:
tatputro vajramukuṭo maṃtriṇaḥ sutavallabhāḥ ..
ṣoḍaśābde'tha saṃprāpte hayārūḍho vanaṃ gataḥ ..4..
3.2.d:
तत्पुत्रो वज्रमुकुटो मंत्रिणः सुतवल्लभाः ॥
षोडशाब्देऽथ संप्राप्ते हयारूढो वनं गतः ॥4॥
3.2.m: His son was Vajramukuṭa, whose companions were ministers' sons. / When he attained his sixteenth year, he mounted a horse and went to the forest. 4

3.2.s:
amātyatanayaścaiva buddhidakṣa iti śrutaḥ ..
hayārūḍho gataḥ sārdhaṃ samānavayasā vane ..5..
3.2.d:
अमात्यतनयश्चैव बुद्धिदक्ष इति श्रुतः ॥
हयारूढो गतः सार्धं समानवयसा वने ॥5॥
3.2.m: And the minister's son, known by the name of Buddhidakṣa, / mounted a horse and went into the forest together with his peer in age. 5

3.2.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā vipinaṃ ramyaṃ mṛgapakṣisamanvitam ..
mumoda vajamukuṭaḥ kāmāśayavaśaṃ gataḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
स दृष्ट्वा विपिनं रम्यं मृगपक्षिसमन्वितम् ॥
मुमोद वजमुकुटः कामाशयवशं गतः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Beholding the lovely forest filled with deer and birds, / Vajramukuṭa rejoiced, falling under the sway of amorous desire. 6

3.2.s:
tatra divyaṃ saro ramyaṃ nānāpakṣinināditam ..
tasya kūle śivasthānaṃ munivṛṃdaiḥ prapūjitam .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
तत्र दिव्यं सरो रम्यं नानापक्षिनिनादितम् ॥
तस्य कूले शिवस्थानं मुनिवृंदैः प्रपूजितम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: There was a divine, delightful lake resounding with the cries of various birds; / on its bank was a shrine of Śiva, worshipped by hosts of sages. 7

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā tatra gatau vīrau paramānaṃdamāpatuḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare bhūpa karaṇāṭakabhūpateḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा तत्र गतौ वीरौ परमानंदमापतुः ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे भूप करणाटकभूपतेः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: Beholding it, the two heroes went there and experienced supreme bliss. / In the meantime, O king, the daughter of the king of Karṇāṭaka, 8

3.2.s:
daṃtavaktrasya tanayā nāmnā padmāvatī matā ..
kāmadevaṃ namaskṛtya kāminī kāmarūpiṇī ..9..
3.2.d:
दंतवक्त्रस्य तनया नाम्ना पद्मावती मता ॥
कामदेवं नमस्कृत्य कामिनी कामरूपिणी ॥9॥
3.2.m: the daughter of Dantavaktra, known by the name of Padmāvatī, / having bowed to the god of love, that passionate maiden capable of changing form at will, 9

3.2.s:
cikrīḍa sakhibhiḥ krīḍāṃ saromadhye manoharā ..
tadā tu vajramukuṭo mandirādāgato bahiḥ .. 3.2.1.10 ..
3.2.d:
चिक्रीड सखिभिः क्रीडां सरोमध्ये मनोहरा ॥
तदा तु वज्रमुकुटो मन्दिरादागतो बहिः ॥ 3.2.1.10 ॥
3.2.m: played games in the middle of the lake together with her female friends, captivating to behold. / Just then, Vajramukuṭa emerged from the temple. 10

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā padmāvatīṃ bālāṃ tulyarūpaguṇānvitām..
mūrcchitaḥ patito bhūmau sā dṛṣṭvā tu mumoha vai .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा पद्मावतीं बालां तुल्यरूपगुणान्विताम्॥
मूर्च्छितः पतितो भूमौ सा दृष्ट्वा तु मुमोह वै ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: Beholding the maiden Padmāvatī, endowed with beauty and virtues equal to his own, / he fell unconscious to the ground; and she, on seeing him, was truly infatuated. 11

3.2.s:
prabuddho vajramukuṭo māṃ pāhi śivaśaṃkara ..
ityuktvā bhūpatanayaḥ punarbālāṃ dadarśa ha .. 12
3.2.d:
प्रबुद्धो वज्रमुकुटो मां पाहि शिवशंकर ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भूपतनयः पुनर्बालां ददर्श ह ॥ 12
3.2.m: Awakening, Vajramukuṭa cried out, "Save me, Śiva Śaṅkara!" / Having said this, the prince looked upon the maiden once more. 12

3.2.s:
śirasaḥ padmakusumaṃ sā gṛhītvā tu karṇayoḥ ..
kṛtvā cakhāna daśanaiḥ pādayordadhatī punaḥ .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
शिरसः पद्मकुसुमं सा गृहीत्वा तु कर्णयोः ॥
कृत्वा चखान दशनैः पादयोर्दधती पुनः ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Taking a lotus flower from her head, she placed it to her ears, / bit it with her teeth, and then set it at her feet. 13

3.2.s:
punargṛhītvā tatpuṣpaṃ hṛdaye saṃpraveśitam ..
iti bhāvaṃ ca sā kṛtvā''libhiḥ sārdhaṃ yayau gṛham .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
पुनर्गृहीत्वा तत्पुष्पं हृदये संप्रवेशितम् ॥
इति भावं च सा कृत्वा'ऽलिभिः सार्धं ययौ गृहम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: Taking that flower again, she placed it against her heart; / having thus conveyed her sentiment, she went home together with her female companions. 14

3.2.s:
tīrthārthaṃ ca samaṃ pitrā saṃprāptā girijāvane ..
tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ sa nṛpo mārabāṇena pīḍitaḥ .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
तीर्थार्थं च समं पित्रा संप्राप्ता गिरिजावने ॥
तस्यां गतायां स नृपो मारबाणेन पीडितः ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: She had arrived at the forest of Girijā together with her father for the sake of pilgrimage. / When she had gone, the prince was afflicted by the arrows of Love. 15

3.2.s:
mahatīṃ mānasīṃ pīḍāṃ prāptavānmohamāgataḥ ..
unmādīva tato bhūtvā khādyapānavivarjitaḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
महतीं मानसीं पीडां प्राप्तवान्मोहमागतः ॥
उन्मादीव ततो भूत्वा खाद्यपानविवर्जितः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: He suffered immense mental agony and fell into a swoon; / then, becoming like one mad, he abstained from food and drink. 16

3.2.s:
dhyātvā padmāvatīṃ bālāṃ maunavratamacīkarat ..
tadā kolāhalo jātaḥ pratāpamukuṭāṃtike .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
ध्यात्वा पद्मावतीं बालां मौनव्रतमचीकरत् ॥
तदा कोलाहलो जातः प्रतापमुकुटांतिके ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: Meditating upon the maiden Padmāvatī, he undertook a vow of silence. / Then an uproar arose in the presence of King Pratāpamukuṭa. 17

3.2.s:
kumāraḥ kāṃ daśāṃ prāpta iti hāheti sarvataḥ ..
tridināṃte maṃtrisuto buddhi dakṣo viśāradaḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
कुमारः कां दशां प्राप्त इति हाहेति सर्वतः ॥
त्रिदिनांते मंत्रिसुतो बुद्धि दक्षो विशारदः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: "What condition has the prince fallen into?"—thus cries of distress resounded everywhere. / At the end of three days, the minister's son, the clever Buddhidakṣa, 18

3.2.s:
abravīdvajramukuṭaṃ satyaṃ kathaya bhūpate ..
sa āha kāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ yathā jātaṃ sarovare .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
अब्रवीद्वज्रमुकुटं सत्यं कथय भूपते ॥
स आह कारणं सर्वं यथा जातं सरोवरे ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: said to Vajramukuṭa: "O prince, speak the truth!" / He related the whole cause just as it had happened at the lake. 19

3.2.s:
tacchrutvā buddhidakṣaśca vihasyāha mahīpatim ..
mahākaṣṭena sā devī mitratvaṃ hi gamiṣyati .. 3.2.1.20 ..
3.2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा बुद्धिदक्षश्च विहस्याह महीपतिम् ॥
महाकष्टेन सा देवी मित्रत्वं हि गमिष्यति ॥ 3.2.1.20 ॥
3.2.m: Having heard that, Buddhidakṣa smiled and said to the prince: / "That lady can indeed be attained with great effort. 20

3.2.s:
karaṇāṭakabhūpasya daṃtavaktrasya sā sutā ..
padmāvatīti vikhyātā dadhatī tvāṃ svamānase .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
करणाटकभूपस्य दंतवक्त्रस्य सा सुता ॥
पद्मावतीति विख्याता दधती त्वां स्वमानसे ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: She is the daughter of Dantavaktra, the king of Karṇāṭaka, / celebrated as Padmāvatī, and she holds you in her heart. 21

3.2.s:
puṣpabhāvena jñātvāhaṃ tvāṃ nayāmi tadaṃtike ..
ityuktvā tasya pitaraṃ pratāpamukuṭaṃ prati .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
पुष्पभावेन ज्ञात्वाहं त्वां नयामि तदंतिके ॥
इत्युक्त्वा तस्य पितरं प्रतापमुकुटं प्रति ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: Having understood this through the gesture with the flower, I will lead you into her presence." / Having spoken thus, he addressed his father, Pratāpamukuṭa: 22

3.2.s:
āhājñāṃ dehi bhūpāla yāsyehaṃ kāraṇāṭake ..
tvatsutasya cikitsārthaṃ sa vajramukuṭo'ciram .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
आहाज्ञां देहि भूपाल यास्येहं कारणाटके ॥
त्वत्सुतस्य चिकित्सार्थं स वज्रमुकुटोऽचिरम् ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: "Grant permission, O king; I shall go to Karṇāṭaka / for the cure of your son; soon that Vajramukuṭa— 23

3.2.s:
āyāmi nā'tra sandeho yadi jīvayase sutam ..
tatheti matvā sa nṛpaḥ prādātputraṃ ca mantriṇe .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
आयामि नाऽत्र सन्देहो यदि जीवयसे सुतम् ॥
तथेति मत्वा स नृपः प्रादात्पुत्रं च मन्त्रिणे ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: I will return with him, there is no doubt of this, if you will let your son live." / Thinking, "So be it," the king entrusted his son to the minister's son. 24

3.2.s:
hayārūḍhau gatau śīghraṃ daṃtavaktrasya pattane ..
kācidvṛddhā sthitā tatra tasyā gehaṃ ca tau gatau .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
हयारूढौ गतौ शीघ्रं दंतवक्त्रस्य पत्तने ॥
काचिद्वृद्धा स्थिता तत्र तस्या गेहं च तौ गतौ ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: Mounted on horses, the two quickly went to Dantavaktra's city. / A certain old woman lived there, and the two went to her house. 25

3.2.s:
bahudravyaṃ dadau tasyai buddhidakṣo viśāradaḥ ..
ūṣaturmaṃdire tasminrātriṃ ghoratamovṛtām .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
बहुद्रव्यं ददौ तस्यै बुद्धिदक्षो विशारदः ॥
ऊषतुर्मंदिरे तस्मिन्रात्रिं घोरतमोवृताम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: The clever Buddhidakṣa gave her much wealth; / they stayed in that house for the night, which was enveloped in deep darkness. 26

3.2.s:
prātaḥkāle tu sā vṛddhā gacchatī rājamandiram ..
tāmāha mantritanayaḥ śṛṇu mātarvaco mama .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
प्रातःकाले तु सा वृद्धा गच्छती राजमन्दिरम् ॥
तामाह मन्त्रितनयः शृणु मातर्वचो मम ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: In the morning, as the old woman was going to the royal palace, / the minister's son said to her: "Listen, mother, to my words. 27

3.2.s:
padmāvatīṃ ca saṃprāpyaikāṃte madvacanaṃ vada ..
jyeṣṭhaśuklasya pañcamyāmiṃduvāre sarovare .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
पद्मावतीं च संप्राप्यैकांते मद्वचनं वद ॥
ज्येष्ठशुक्लस्य पञ्चम्यामिंदुवारे सरोवरे ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: When you approach Padmāvatī, speak my words to her in private: / 'On the fifth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, on Monday, at the lake... 28

3.2.s:
yo dṛṣṭaḥ puruṣo ramyastvadarthe samupāgataḥ..
iti śrutvā yayau vṛddhā padmaṃ tasyai nyavedayat .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
यो दृष्टः पुरुषो रम्यस्त्वदर्थे समुपागतः॥
इति श्रुत्वा ययौ वृद्धा पद्मं तस्यै न्यवेदयत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: “The handsome man who was seen has come for your sake.” / Having heard this, the old woman went and presented the lotus to her.

3.2.s:
ruṣṭā padmāvatī prāha caṃdanārdrāṃgulīyikā ..
gaccha gaccha mahāduṣṭe talenorasyatāḍayat ..3.2.1.30 ..
3.2.d:
रुष्टा पद्मावती प्राह चंदनार्द्रांगुलीयिका ॥
गच्छ गच्छ महादुष्टे तलेनोरस्यताडयत् ॥3.2.1.30 ॥
3.2.m: Angered, Padmāvatī, her fingers moist with sandalwood, said: / “Go! Go, you wretched woman!” and struck her on the chest with her palm.

3.2.s:
aṃgulībhiḥ kapolau ca tasyāḥ spṛṣṭvā yayau gṛham ..
sā tu vṛddhā buddhidakṣaṃ sarvaṃ bhāvaṃ nyavedayat .. .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
अंगुलीभिः कपोलौ च तस्याः स्पृष्ट्वा ययौ गृहम् ॥
सा तु वृद्धा बुद्धिदक्षं सर्वं भावं न्यवेदयत् ॥ ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: And having touched her cheeks with her fingers, she went into the house. / But that old woman reported the whole occurrence to Buddhidakṣa.

3.2.s:
sa mitraṃ duḥkhitaṃ prāha śṛṇu mitra śucaṃ tyaja ..
tvāmāha bhūpateḥ kanyā prāṇapriya vacaḥ śṛṇu .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
स मित्रं दुःखितं प्राह शृणु मित्र शुचं त्यज ॥
त्वामाह भूपतेः कन्या प्राणप्रिय वचः शृणु ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: He said to his distressed friend: “Listen, friend, abandon grief! / The king's daughter has spoken to you, beloved as life; listen to her words:

3.2.s:
tvadarthe tāḍitaṃ vakṣaḥ kadā mitraṃ bhaviṣyasi..
śrutvā tanmadhuraṃ vākyaṃ rajo dehe samāgatam .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
त्वदर्थे ताडितं वक्षः कदा मित्रं भविष्यसि॥
श्रुत्वा तन्मधुरं वाक्यं रजो देहे समागतम् ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: ‘For your sake my chest was struck; when will you become my companion?’ / Hearing those sweet words, the menstrual flow arrived in her body.

3.2.s:
rajasvalāṃte bho mitra tavāsyaṃ cuṃbitāsmyaham ..
iti śrutvā bhūpasutaḥ paramānandamāyayau .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
रजस्वलांते भो मित्र तवास्यं चुंबितास्म्यहम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा भूपसुतः परमानन्दमाययौ ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: ‘O friend, at the end of my period I shall kiss your face.’ / Having heard this, the king's son attained supreme joy.

3.2.s:
tridināṃte tu sā vṛddhā padmāvatyai nyavedayet ..
tvāmutsukaḥ sa bhūpālastava darśanalālasaḥ .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
त्रिदिनांते तु सा वृद्धा पद्मावत्यै न्यवेदयेत् ॥
त्वामुत्सुकः स भूपालस्तव दर्शनलालसः ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: At the end of three days, the old woman announced to Padmāvatī: / “That prince is eager for you, longing for a sight of you.

3.2.s:
taṃ bhajasvādya suśroṇi saphalaṃ jīvanaṃ kuru ..
iti śrutvā mahāhṛṣṭā sā masyārdrāṃgulīyakam .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
तं भजस्वाद्य सुश्रोणि सफलं जीवनं कुरु ॥
इति श्रुत्वा महाहृष्टा सा मस्यार्द्रांगुलीयकम् ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m: Adore him today, fair-hipped woman, and make your life fruitful.” / Having heard this, highly delighted, she dipped her fingers in ink,

3.2.s:
gavākṣadvāri niṣkāsya tale pṛṣṭhe ca tāḍitā ..
tathaiva vṛddhā taṃ prāpya mantriṇaṃ cābravīdvacaḥ .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
गवाक्षद्वारि निष्कास्य तले पृष्ठे च ताडिता ॥
तथैव वृद्धा तं प्राप्य मन्त्रिणं चाब्रवीद्वचः ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m: expelled [her] through the lattice door, and struck her on the back with her palm. / In that very way the old woman approached the minister and spoke these words.

3.2.s:
prasanno buddhidakṣaśca mitraṃ prāha śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ ..
paścime diśi bhoḥ svāmingavākṣaṃ tava nirmitam .. 38 ..
3.2.d:
प्रसन्नो बुद्धिदक्षश्च मित्रं प्राह शृणुष्व भोः ॥
पश्चिमे दिशि भोः स्वामिन्गवाक्षं तव निर्मितम् ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: Pleased, Buddhidakṣa said to his friend: “Listen, sir! / O master, a window in the western direction has been prepared for you.

3.2.s:
arddharātre tu saṃprāpya bhaja māṃ kāmavihvalām ..
śrutvā tadvajramukuṭaḥ priyādarśanalālasaḥ .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
अर्द्धरात्रे तु संप्राप्य भज मां कामविह्वलाम् ॥
श्रुत्वा तद्वज्रमुकुटः प्रियादर्शनलालसः ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m: Arrive at midnight and make love to me, agitated with desire.’ / Hearing that, Vajramukuṭa, longing to see his beloved,

3.2.s:
yayau śīghraṃ mahākāmī ramaṇīṃ tāmarāmayat ..
māsāṃte kāmaśithilo mitradarśanalālasaḥ .. 3.2.1.40 ..
3.2.d:
ययौ शीघ्रं महाकामी रमणीं तामरामयत् ॥
मासांते कामशिथिलो मित्रदर्शनलालसः ॥ 3.2.1.40 ॥
3.2.m: went swiftly, overcome with passion, and took pleasure with that charming woman. / At the end of a month, his passion slackening, longing to see his friend,

3.2.s:
padmāvatīṃ priyāṃ prāha śṛṇu vākyaṃ varānane ..
yena prāptavatī mahyaṃ tvaṃ subhrūḥ suradurlabhā .. 41 ..
3.2.d:
पद्मावतीं प्रियां प्राह शृणु वाक्यं वरानने ॥
येन प्राप्तवती मह्यं त्वं सुभ्रूः सुरदुर्लभा ॥ 41 ॥
3.2.m: he said to his beloved Padmāvatī: “Listen to my words, fair-faced woman! / That one through whom you, fair-browed one difficult for even gods to obtain, were gained by me—

3.2.s:
tanmitraṃ buddhidakṣaśca kiṃ nu tiṣṭhati sāṃpratam ..
ājñāṃ dehi priye mahyaṃ dṛṣṭvāyāsyāmi teṃ'tikam .. 42 ..
3.2.d:
तन्मित्रं बुद्धिदक्षश्च किं नु तिष्ठति सांप्रतम् ॥
आज्ञां देहि प्रिये मह्यं दृष्ट्वायास्यामि तेंऽतिकम् ॥ 42 ॥
3.2.m: how indeed is that friend, Buddhidakṣa, faring now? / Give me permission, beloved; having seen him, I shall return to your presence.”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya niṣṭhuraṃ kuliśopamam ..
miṣṭānnaṃ saviṣaṃ kṛtvā maṃtriṇe sā nyavedayat .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य निष्ठुरं कुलिशोपमम् ॥
मिष्टान्नं सविषं कृत्वा मंत्रिणे सा न्यवेदयत् ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing these words of his, harsh as a thunderbolt, / she prepared sweet food laced with poison and presented it to the minister.

3.2.s:
tadā tu buddhidakṣaśca citraguptaprapūjakaḥ ..
jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ na tu bhakṣitavānsvayam .. 44 ..
3.2.d:
तदा तु बुद्धिदक्षश्च चित्रगुप्तप्रपूजकः ॥
ज्ञात्वा तत्कारणं सर्वं न तु भक्षितवान्स्वयम् ॥ 44 ॥
3.2.m: Then Buddhidakṣa, a worshipper of Citragupta, / knowing the whole reason for it, did not eat it himself.

3.2.s:
etasminnantare prāpto bhūpatistvarayānvitaḥ ..
vivekavantaṃ mitraṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha ruṣānvitaḥ .. 45 ..
3.2.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राप्तो भूपतिस्त्वरयान्वितः ॥
विवेकवन्तं मित्रं तं दृष्ट्वा प्राह रुषान्वितः ॥ 45 ॥
3.2.m: In the meantime, the prince arrived in haste. / Seeing that wise friend, he said, filled with anger:

3.2.s:
kasmānna khāditaṃ mitra bhojanaṃ matpriyākṛtam ..
vihasya buddhidakṣastu sārameye dadau hi tat .. 46 ..
3.2.d:
कस्मान्न खादितं मित्र भोजनं मत्प्रियाकृतम् ॥
विहस्य बुद्धिदक्षस्तु सारमेये ददौ हि तत् ॥ 46 ॥
3.2.m: “Friend, why have you not eaten the food prepared by my beloved?” / Smiling, Buddhidakṣa gave it to a dog.

3.2.s:
bhuktvā sa maraṇaṃ prāptaḥ sa dṛṣṭvā vismito nṛpaḥ ..
strīcaritraṃ ca vijñāya snehaṃ tyaktvā'bravīttu tam ..47..
3.2.d:
भुक्त्वा स मरणं प्राप्तः स दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो नृपः ॥
स्त्रीचरित्रं च विज्ञाय स्नेहं त्यक्त्वाऽब्रवीत्तु तम् ॥47॥
3.2.m: Having eaten it, it died. Seeing that, the prince was astonished, / and knowing the nature of women, he cast off affection and said to him:

3.2.s:
mitra gaccha gṛhaṃ śīghraṃ mayā tyaktā ca pāpinī ..
sa āha śṛṇu bhūpāla gaccha śīghraṃ priyāṃtikam ..48..
3.2.d:
मित्र गच्छ गृहं शीघ्रं मया त्यक्ता च पापिनी ॥
स आह शृणु भूपाल गच्छ शीघ्रं प्रियांतिकम् ॥48॥
3.2.m: “Friend, let us go home quickly; I have abandoned that wicked woman.” / He said: “Listen, O prince! Go quickly to your beloved's side.

3.2.s:
tadalaṃkāramāhṛtya triśūlaṃ kuru jānuni ..
prasuptāṃ tyaja bho mitra yāhi tvaṃ mā vicāraya .. 49 ..
3.2.d:
तदलंकारमाहृत्य त्रिशूलं कुरु जानुनि ॥
प्रसुप्तां त्यज भो मित्र याहि त्वं मा विचारय ॥ 49 ॥
3.2.m: Taking her ornaments, make [the mark of] a trident on her knee. / Leave her while she is fast asleep, friend; go, do not hesitate!”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā yayau bhūpastathā kṛtvā samāgataḥ ..
svamitreṇa yayau sārdhaṃ smaśāne rudramaṇḍape .. 3.2.1.50 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा ययौ भूपस्तथा कृत्वा समागतः ॥
स्वमित्रेण ययौ सार्धं स्मशाने रुद्रमण्डपे ॥ 3.2.1.50 ॥
3.2.m: Having heard this, the prince went, did so, and returned. / Along with his friend, he went to the pavilion of Rudra in the cremation ground.

3.2.s:
śiṣyaṃ kṛtvā nṛpaṃ taṃ sa yogirūpo hi bhūṣaṇam ..
vikrayārthaṃ dadau tasmai svamitrāya sa buddhimān .. 51 ..
3.2.d:
शिष्यं कृत्वा नृपं तं स योगिरूपो हि भूषणम् ॥
विक्रयार्थं ददौ तस्मै स्वमित्राय स बुद्धिमान् ॥ 51 ॥
3.2.m: Having made that prince his disciple, he assumed the form of a yogin, / and the wise man gave the ornament to his friend to sell.

3.2.s:
sa vajramukuṭo matvā tadājñāṃ nagaraṃ gataḥ ..
coroyamiti taṃ matvā baddhvā rājño hi rakṣiṇaḥ .. 52 ..
3.2.d:
स वज्रमुकुटो मत्वा तदाज्ञां नगरं गतः ॥
चोरोयमिति तं मत्वा बद्ध्वा राज्ञो हि रक्षिणः ॥ 52 ॥
3.2.m: Vajramukuṭa, obeying his command, went to the city. / Thinking, “This is a thief,” the king's guards bound him,

3.2.s:
śīghraṃ nivedayāmāsurdantavaktrastamabravīt ..
kva prāptaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ ramyaṃ sarvaṃ kathaya pūruṣa .. 53 ..
3.2.d:
शीघ्रं निवेदयामासुर्दन्तवक्त्रस्तमब्रवीत् ॥
क्व प्राप्तं भूषणं रम्यं सर्वं कथय पूरुष ॥ 53 ॥
3.2.m: and swiftly reported him. Dantavaktra said to him: / “Where was this lovely ornament obtained? Tell everything, man!”

3.2.s:
jaṭilaḥ prāha bho rājanśmaśāne madguruḥ sthitaḥ ..
tena dattaṃ vikrayārthaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ svarṇaguṃṭhitam .. 54 ..
3.2.d:
जटिलः प्राह भो राजन्श्मशाने मद्गुरुः स्थितः ॥
तेन दत्तं विक्रयार्थं भूषणं स्वर्णगुंठितम् ॥ 54 ॥
3.2.m: The matted-haired ascetic said: “O king, my guru dwells in the cremation ground. / By him this gold-wrapped ornament was given to me to sell.”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā sa nṛpatistūrṇamāhūya tadgurum ..
bhūṣaṇaṃ pṛṣṭavānrājā yogī prāha śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ .. 55 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा स नृपतिस्तूर्णमाहूय तद्गुरुम् ॥
भूषणं पृष्टवान्राजा योगी प्राह शृणुष्व भोः ॥ 55 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the king quickly summoned his guru / and questioned him about the ornament. The yogin said: “Listen, sir!

3.2.s:
smaśāne saṃdhitaṃ maṃtraṃ mayā yogisvarūpiṇā ..
piśācī prāpitā kācittasyāścihnaṃ mayā kṛtam .. 56 ..
3.2.d:
स्मशाने संधितं मंत्रं मया योगिस्वरूपिणा ॥
पिशाची प्रापिता काचित्तस्याश्चिह्नं मया कृतम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.2.m: In the cremation ground, a mantra was practiced by me in the guise of a yogin. / A certain piśācī was summoned, and a mark was made by me upon her

3.2.s:
vāmajānuni śūlena tayā dattaṃ hi bhūṣaṇam ..
jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ rājā sutā niṣkāsitā gṛhāt .. 57 ..
3.2.d:
वामजानुनि शूलेन तया दत्तं हि भूषणम् ॥
ज्ञात्वा तत्कारणं राजा सुता निष्कासिता गृहात् ॥ 57 ॥
3.2.m: on her left knee with a trident, and indeed this ornament was given by her.” / Learning the cause of that, the king expelled his daughter from the house.

3.2.s:
sa vajramukuṭastāṃ tu gṛhītvā gṛhamāyayau ..
vihasya prāha vaitālaḥ śṛṇu vikramabhūpate .. 58 ..
3.2.d:
स वज्रमुकुटस्तां तु गृहीत्वा गृहमाययौ ॥
विहस्य प्राह वैतालः शृणु विक्रमभूपते ॥ 58 ॥
3.2.m: Vajramukuṭa took her and came home. / Laughing, the vetāla said: “Listen, King Vikrama!

3.2.s:
kasmai pāpaṃ mahatprāptaṃ caturṇā me vadādhunā ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā vacastasya vikramo nāma bhūpatiḥ .. 59 ..
3.2.d:
कस्मै पापं महत्प्राप्तं चतुर्णा मे वदाधुना ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य विक्रमो नाम भूपतिः ॥ 59 ॥
3.2.m: Tell me now, upon which of the four did great sin fall?” / Sūta said: / Hearing his words, the king named Vikrama,

3.2.s:
vihasya bhārgavaṃ prāha prāptaṃ pāpaṃ hi bhūpateḥ ..
mitrakāryamamātyena svāmikāryaṃ ca rakṣibhiḥ .. 3.2.1.60 ..
3.2.d:
विहस्य भार्गवं प्राह प्राप्तं पापं हि भूपतेः ॥
मित्रकार्यममात्येन स्वामिकार्यं च रक्षिभिः ॥ 3.2.1.60 ॥
3.2.m: smiling, said to Bhārgava: “The sin indeed fell upon the king. / By the minister, a friend's purpose was accomplished, and by the guards, their master's purpose;

3.2.s:
bhūpa putreṇārthasiddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tasmācca bhūpateḥ ..
mahatpāpaṃ ca saṃprāptaṃ tenāsau narakaṃ gataḥ .. 61 ..
3.2.d:
भूप पुत्रेणार्थसिद्धं कृतं तस्माच्च भूपतेः ॥
महत्पापं च संप्राप्तं तेनासौ नरकं गतः ॥ 61 ॥
3.2.m: by the king's son, his own desired goal was achieved. Therefore, upon the king / great sin fell, and because of it he went to hell.

3.2.s:
rajovatīṃ sutāṃ dṛṣṭvā na vivāheta yo naraḥ ..
sa pāpī narakaṃ yāti ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrakam .. 62 ..
3.2.d:
रजोवतीं सुतां दृष्ट्वा न विवाहेत यो नरः ॥
स पापी नरकं याति षष्टिवर्षसहस्रकम् ॥ 62 ॥
3.2.m: That man who, seeing his daughter menstruating, does not marry her off— / that sinner goes to hell for sixty thousand years.

3.2.s:
gāṃdharvaṃ ca vivāhaṃ vai kāminyā ca kṛtaṃ yayā ..
tasyā vighnakaro yo vai sa pāpī yamapīḍitaḥ .. 63 ..
3.2.d:
गांधर्वं च विवाहं वै कामिन्या च कृतं यया ॥
तस्या विघ्नकरो यो वै स पापी यमपीडितः ॥ 63 ॥
3.2.m: And if a gāndharva marriage has been made by a passionate woman, / whoever causes an obstacle to it is a sinner tormented by Yama.

3.2.s:
adṛṣṭadoṣāṃ yaḥ kanyāṃ vivekena vinā tyajet ..
sa pāpī narakaṃ yāti lakṣavarṣapramāṇakam .. 64 ..
3.2.d:
अदृष्टदोषां यः कन्यां विवेकेन विना त्यजेत् ॥
स पापी नरकं याति लक्षवर्षप्रमाणकम् ॥ 64 ॥
3.2.m: Whoever abandons a girl whose fault has not been seen, without discernment, / that sinner goes to hell for the measure of a hundred thousand years.”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā? sa vaitālo dharmagāthāṃ nṛperitām ..
prasannahṛdayaḥ prāha bhūpatiṃ dharmatatparam ..65 ..
mukuṭopari ṭippaṇī
tulanīya - vetālapaṃcaviṃśatiḥ
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा? स वैतालो धर्मगाथां नृपेरिताम् ॥
प्रसन्नहृदयः प्राह भूपतिं धर्मतत्परम् ॥65 ॥
मुकुटोपरि टिप्पणी
तुलनीय - वेतालपंचविंशतिः
3.2.m:
Hearing this discourse on dharma spoken by the king, that vetāla, / with a joyful heart, addressed the king devoted to dharma.
Note on the Mukuṭa
Compare: Vetālapañcaviṃśati.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
prasannamanasaṃ bhūpaṃ mahāsiṃhāsane sthitam ..
dvijavaryaḥ sa vaitālo vacaḥ prāha prasannadhīḥ ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
प्रसन्नमनसं भूपं महासिंहासने स्थितम् ॥
द्विजवर्यः स वैतालो वचः प्राह प्रसन्नधीः ॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / To the king of pleased mind seated on the great throne, / that best of twice-born, the vetāla, of delighted intellect, spoke these words:

3.2.s:
ekadā yamunātīre dharmasthalapurī śubhā ..
dhanadhānyasamāyuktā caturvarṇasamanvitā .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
एकदा यमुनातीरे धर्मस्थलपुरी शुभा ॥
धनधान्यसमायुक्ता चतुर्वर्णसमन्विता ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: “Once on the bank of the Yamunā was the auspicious city of Dharmasthala, / endowed with wealth and grain, and filled with the four castes.

3.2.s:
guṇādhipo mahīpālastatra rājyaṃ cakāra vai ..
hariśarmā purodhāstu snānapūjanatatparaḥ ..3 ..
3.2.d:
गुणाधिपो महीपालस्तत्र राज्यं चकार वै ॥
हरिशर्मा पुरोधास्तु स्नानपूजनतत्परः ॥3 ॥
3.2.m: There King Guṇādhipa indeed held rule. / His family priest was Hariśarman, devoted to bathing and worship.

3.2.s:
tasya patnī suśīlā ca pativrataparāyaṇā ..
satyaśīlaḥ suto jāto vidyādhyayanatatparaḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य पत्नी सुशीला च पतिव्रतपरायणा ॥
सत्यशीलः सुतो जातो विद्याध्ययनतत्परः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: His wife was Suśīlā, dedicated to her husband. / A son, Satyaśīla, was born [to them], devoted to the study of sacred lore.

3.2.s:
tasyānujā madhumatī śīlarūpaguṇānvitā ..
dvādaśābdavayaḥprāpte vivāhārthaṃ pitā yadā .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
तस्यानुजा मधुमती शीलरूपगुणान्विता ॥
द्वादशाब्दवयःप्राप्ते विवाहार्थं पिता यदा ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: His younger sister was Madhumatī, endowed with good conduct, beauty, and virtues. / When she attained the age of twelve years, when her father, for the sake of marriage,

3.2.s:
bhrātā? babhrāma tau sarvaṃ cinutaśca sutāvaram ..
kadācidrājaputrasya vivāhe samato dvijaḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
भ्राता? बभ्राम तौ सर्वं चिनुतश्च सुतावरम् ॥
कदाचिद्राजपुत्रस्य विवाहे समतो द्विजः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: The brother wandered, and they both sought an excellent husband for the daughter. / Once, at a prince's wedding, the twice-born [father] agreed [upon one].

3.2.s:
paṭhanārthe tu kāśyāṃ vai sattvaśīlaḥ svayaṃ gataḥ ..
etasminnaṃtare rājandvijaḥ kaścitsamāgataḥ .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
पठनार्थे तु काश्यां वै सत्त्वशीलः स्वयं गतः ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे राजन्द्विजः कश्चित्समागतः ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Meanwhile, Sattvaśīla himself went to Kāśī for study. / In the meantime, O king, a certain twice-born came there,

3.2.s:
vāmano nāma vikhyāto rūpaśīlavayovṛtaḥ ..
sutā madhumatī taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā kāmāturā'bhavat .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
वामनो नाम विख्यातो रूपशीलवयोवृतः ॥
सुता मधुमती तं च दृष्ट्वा कामातुराऽभवत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: famed by the name of Vāmana, endowed with beauty, virtue, and youth. / Seeing him, the daughter Madhumatī was stricken with desire.

3.2.s:
bhojanaṃ chādanaṃ pānaṃ svapnaṃ tyaktvā ca vihvalā ..
cakorīva vinā caṃdraṃ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
भोजनं छादनं पानं स्वप्नं त्यक्त्वा च विह्वला ॥
चकोरीव विना चंद्रं कामबाणप्रपीडिता ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Abandoning food, clothing, drink, and sleep, distraught, / afflicted by the arrows of love, she was like a cakorī bird without the moon.

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā suśīlā taṃ bālā vāmanaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tathā ..
vārayāmāsa tāṃbūlaiḥ svarṇadravyasamanvitaiḥ .. 3.2.2.10 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा सुशीला तं बाला वामनं ब्राह्मणं तथा ॥
वारयामास तांबूलैः स्वर्णद्रव्यसमन्वितैः ॥ 3.2.2.10 ॥
3.2.m: Seeing him, the young girl Suśīlā / betrothed that brāhmaṇa Vāmana with betel leaves accompanied by gold and wealth.

3.2.s:
hariśarmā prayoge ca dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā trivikramam ..
vedavedāṃtattvajñaṃ sutārthe'varayattadā .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
हरिशर्मा प्रयोगे च द्विजं दृष्ट्वा त्रिविक्रमम् ॥
वेदवेदांतत्त्वज्ञं सुतार्थेऽवरयत्तदा ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: At Prayāga, Hariśarmā, seeing the twice-born Trivikrama, / who knew the truth of the Vedas and Vedānta, chose him as groom for his daughter.

3.2.s:
satyaśīlastu kāśyāṃ vai guruputraṃ ca keśavam ..
varitvā taṃ bhaginyarthe yayau gehaṃ mudānvitaḥ .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यशीलस्तु काश्यां वै गुरुपुत्रं च केशवम् ॥
वरित्वा तं भगिन्यर्थे ययौ गेहं मुदान्वितः ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: Satyaśīla, in Kāśī, having chosen Keśava, / the guru's son, for his sister, went home filled with joy.

3.2.s:
māghakṛṣṇatrayodaśyāṃ bhṛgau lagnaṃ śubhaṃ smṛtam ..
trayo viprāstadā prāptāḥ kanyārthe rūpamohitāḥ .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
माघकृष्णत्रयोदश्यां भृगौ लग्नं शुभं स्मृतम् ॥
त्रयो विप्रास्तदा प्राप्ताः कन्यार्थे रूपमोहिताः ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: On the thirteenth lunar day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, on a Friday, an auspicious planetary alignment was declared. / Then the three brāhmaṇas arrived, enchanted by beauty, for the maiden's hand.

3.2.s:
tasminkāle tu sā kanyā bhujagenaiva daṃśitā ..
mṛtā pretatvamāpannā pūrvakarmaprabhāvataḥ .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मिन्काले तु सा कन्या भुजगेनैव दंशिता ॥
मृता प्रेतत्वमापन्ना पूर्वकर्मप्रभावतः ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: At that very time, the maiden was bitten by a serpent. / She died and became a preta, by the power of past deeds.

3.2.s:
tadā te brāhmaṇā yatnaṃ kārayāmāsuruttamam ..
na jīvanavatī bālā garalena vimohitā ..15..
3.2.d:
तदा ते ब्राह्मणा यत्नं कारयामासुरुत्तमम् ॥
न जीवनवती बाला गरलेन विमोहिता ॥15॥
3.2.m: Then those brāhmaṇas made the utmost effort, / but the girl, stupefied by poison, did not return to life.

3.2.s:
hariśarmā tu tatsarvaṃ kṛtvā vedavidhānataḥ ..
āyayau maṃdiraṃ rājantsutāguṇavimohitaḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
हरिशर्मा तु तत्सर्वं कृत्वा वेदविधानतः ॥
आययौ मंदिरं राजन्त्सुतागुणविमोहितः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Having performed everything according to Vedic injunctions, Hariśarmā / returned to his house, O king, bewitched by his daughter's virtues.

3.2.s:
trivikramastu bahudhā duḥkhaṃ kṛtvā smarānugaḥ ..
kaṃthādhārī yatirbhūtvā deśāddeśātaraṃ yayau .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
त्रिविक्रमस्तु बहुधा दुःखं कृत्वा स्मरानुगः ॥
कंथाधारी यतिर्भूत्वा देशाद्देशातरं ययौ ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: Trivikrama, lamenting greatly, devoted to love, / became an ascetic wearing patched rags and went from country to country.

3.2.s:
keśavastu mahāduḥkhī priyāsthīni gṛhītavān ..
tīrthāttīrthāṃtaraṃ prāptaḥ kāmabāṇena pīḍitaḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
केशवस्तु महादुःखी प्रियास्थीनि गृहीतवान् ॥
तीर्थात्तीर्थांतरं प्राप्तः कामबाणेन पीडितः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Keśava, deeply sorrowful, took his beloved's bones; / afflicted by the arrow of love, he wandered from holy bath to holy bath.

3.2.s:
bhasmagrāhī vāmanastu virahāgniprapīḍitaḥ ..
tasthau citāyāṃ kāmārtaḥ patnīdhyānaparāyaṇaḥ ..19..
3.2.d:
भस्मग्राही वामनस्तु विरहाग्निप्रपीडितः ॥
तस्थौ चितायां कामार्तः पत्नीध्यानपरायणः ॥19॥
3.2.m: Taking the ashes, Vāmana, afflicted by the fire of separation / and tormented by love, remained by the funeral pyre, absorbed in contemplation of his wife.

3.2.s:
ekadā sarayūtīre lakṣmaṇākhyapure śubhe ..
trivikramastu bhikṣārthe saṃprāpto dvijamaṃdire .. 3.2.2.20 ..
3.2.d:
एकदा सरयूतीरे लक्ष्मणाख्यपुरे शुभे ॥
त्रिविक्रमस्तु भिक्षार्थे संप्राप्तो द्विजमंदिरे ॥ 3.2.2.20 ॥
3.2.m: Once, on the bank of the Sarayū, in the auspicious city named Lakṣmaṇāpura, / Trivikrama arrived at a twice-born's house for alms.

3.2.s:
tasmindine rāmaśarmā śivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ ..
yatinaṃ varayāmāsa bhojanārthaṃ svamaṃdire .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मिन्दिने रामशर्मा शिवध्यानपरायणः ॥
यतिनं वरयामास भोजनार्थं स्वमंदिरे ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: On that day, Rāmaśarmā, devoted to the contemplation of Śiva, / invited the ascetic to eat in his house.

3.2.s:
tasya patnī viśālākṣī racitvā bahubhojanam ..
āhūya yatinaṃ rājanpātramālabhamākarot .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य पत्नी विशालाक्षी रचित्वा बहुभोजनम् ॥
आहूय यतिनं राजन्पात्रमालभमाकरोत् ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: His large-eyed wife, having prepared abundant food, / called the ascetic, O king, and touched the dish.

3.2.s:
tasminkāle ca tadbālo mṛtaḥ pāpavaśaṃgataḥ ..
arodīttasya sairaṃdhrī viśālākṣyapi bhartsitā .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मिन्काले च तद्बालो मृतः पापवशंगतः ॥
अरोदीत्तस्य सैरंध्री विशालाक्ष्यपि भर्त्सिता ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: At that moment, under the sway of past sin, their boy died. / His maidservant wept, and the large-eyed [mother] was also reprimanded.

3.2.s:
na rodanaṃ tyaktavatī putraśokāgnitāpitā ..
rāmaśarmā tadā prāpto maṃtraṃ saṃjīvanaṃ śubham .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
न रोदनं त्यक्तवती पुत्रशोकाग्नितापिता ॥
रामशर्मा तदा प्राप्तो मंत्रं संजीवनं शुभम् ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: Burned by the fire of grief for her son, she did not cease weeping. / Then Rāmaśarmā arrived, and with the auspicious saṃjīvana mantra,

3.2.s:
japitvā mārjanaṃ kṛtvā jīvayāmāsa bālakam ..
vinayāvanato viprastaṃ ca saṃnyāsinaṃ tadā.. .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
जपित्वा मार्जनं कृत्वा जीवयामास बालकम् ॥
विनयावनतो विप्रस्तं च संन्यासिनं तदा॥ ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: chanting it and performing aspersion, he revived the boy. / Then that twice-born, bowed with modesty, [fed] that ascetic

3.2.s:
bhojanaṃ kārayitvā tu maṃtraṃ saṃjīvanaṃ dadau ..
trivikramastu taṃ maṃtraṃ paṭhitvā yamunātaṭe ..26..
3.2.d:
भोजनं कारयित्वा तु मंत्रं संजीवनं ददौ ॥
त्रिविक्रमस्तु तं मंत्रं पठित्वा यमुनातटे ॥26॥
3.2.m: and, after feeding him, gave him the saṃjīvana mantra. / Having recited that mantra, Trivikrama, on the bank of the Yamunā,

3.2.s:
prāptavānyatra sā nārī dāhitā hariśarmaṇā..
etasminnantare tatra rājaputro mṛtiṃ gataḥ .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
प्राप्तवान्यत्र सा नारी दाहिता हरिशर्मणा॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र राजपुत्रो मृतिं गतः ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: arrived where that woman had been cremated by Hariśarmā. / In the meantime, a prince died there.

3.2.s:
dāhitastanayaḥ pitrā śokakartrā tadāmunā ..
jīvanaṃ prāptavānbālastasya maṃtraprabhāvataḥ .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
दाहितस्तनयः पित्रा शोककर्त्रा तदामुना ॥
जीवनं प्राप्तवान्बालस्तस्य मंत्रप्रभावतः ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: When the son had been cremated by his sorrowing father, / the boy then received life through the power of his mantra.

3.2.s:
guṇādhipasya tanayo rājño dharmasthalīpateḥ ..
trivikramaṃ vacaḥ prāha vīrabāhurmahābalaḥ ..29..
3.2.d:
गुणाधिपस्य तनयो राज्ञो धर्मस्थलीपतेः ॥
त्रिविक्रमं वचः प्राह वीरबाहुर्महाबलः ॥29॥
3.2.m: Vīrabāhu, the son of Guṇādhipa, the mighty king / who ruled Dharmasthalī, addressed these words to Trivikrama:

3.2.s:
jīvanaṃ dattavānmahyaṃ varayādya varaṃ mama ..
sa vipraḥ prāha bho rājankeśavo nāma yo dvijaḥ .. 3.2.2.30 ..
3.2.d:
जीवनं दत्तवान्मह्यं वरयाद्य वरं मम ॥
स विप्रः प्राह भो राजन्केशवो नाम यो द्विजः ॥ 3.2.2.30 ॥
3.2.m: "You have given me life; choose a boon from me today." / That twice-born said, "O king, the twice-born named Keśava,

3.2.s:
gṛhītvāsthi gatastīrthe tamanveṣaya mā ciram ..
vīrabāhustathā matvā dūtamārgeṇa taṃ prati .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
गृहीत्वास्थि गतस्तीर्थे तमन्वेषय मा चिरम् ॥
वीरबाहुस्तथा मत्वा दूतमार्गेण तं प्रति ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: who took the bones and went to the holy baths—search for him without delay." / Vīrabāhu, considering this, sent a messenger to him.

3.2.s:
prāptastaṃ kathayāmāsa yathā prāptaṃ hi jīvanam ..
iti śrutvā vacastasya keśavo'sthisamanvitaḥ .32..
3.2.d:
प्राप्तस्तं कथयामास यथा प्राप्तं हि जीवनम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य केशवोऽस्थिसमन्वितः .32॥
3.2.m: The messenger, having reached him, told him how life had been regained. / Hearing his words, Keśava, bearing the bones,

3.2.s:
pragatyāsthīni sarvāṇi dadau tasmai dvijātaye ..
punaḥ saṃjīvitā bālā keśavādīnvaco'bravīt..33..
3.2.d:
प्रगत्यास्थीनि सर्वाणि ददौ तस्मै द्विजातये ॥
पुनः संजीविता बाला केशवादीन्वचोऽब्रवीत्॥33॥
3.2.m: approached and gave all the bones to that twice-born. / The girl was brought back to life again, and spoke to Keśava and the others:

3.2.s:
yogyā dharmeṇa yasyāhaṃ tasmai prāyāmi dharmiṇe..
iti śrutvā vacastasyā maunavaṃtastrayaḥ sthitāḥ..34..
3.2.d:
योग्या धर्मेण यस्याहं तस्मै प्रायामि धर्मिणे॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्या मौनवंतस्त्रयः स्थिताः॥34॥
3.2.m: "I shall belong in accordance with dharma to that righteous man to whom I am suited." / Hearing these words of hers, the three remained silent.

3.2.s:
atastvaṃ vikramāditya dharmajña kathayasva me ..
kasmai yogyā ca sā bālā nāmnā madhumatī śubhā .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
अतस्त्वं विक्रमादित्य धर्मज्ञ कथयस्व मे ॥
कस्मै योग्या च सा बाला नाम्ना मधुमती शुभा ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: "Therefore, O Vikramāditya, knower of dharma, tell me: / to whom does that auspicious maiden named Madhumatī rightfully belong?"

3.2.s:
..sūta uvāca .. ..
vihasya vikramādityo vaitālaṃ prāha namradhīḥ..
yogyā madhumatī nārī vāmanāya dvijanmane..36..
3.2.d:
॥सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
विहस्य विक्रमादित्यो वैतालं प्राह नम्रधीः॥
योग्या मधुमती नारी वामनाय द्विजन्मने॥36॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Smiling, Vikramāditya, humble in mind, spoke to the vetāla: / "The woman Madhumatī is suited to the twice-born Vāmana.

3.2.s:
prāṇadātā tu yo vipraḥ piteva guṇatatparaḥ ..
asthidātā tu yo vipro bhrātṛtulyassa vedavit .. 37 ..
vāmanopari ṭippaṇī
keśavopari ṭippaṇī
asthnopari ṭippaṇī
tulanīya - vetālapañcaviṃśatiḥ
3.2.d:
प्राणदाता तु यो विप्रः पितेव गुणतत्परः ॥
अस्थिदाता तु यो विप्रो भ्रातृतुल्यस्स वेदवित् ॥ 37 ॥
वामनोपरि टिप्पणी
केशवोपरि टिप्पणी
अस्थ्नोपरि टिप्पणी
तुलनीय - वेतालपञ्चविंशतिः
3.2.m:
The twice-born who gave life is like a father intent on virtue; / and the twice-born who gave the bones, knower of the Vedas, is equal to a brother."
Note on Vāmana.
Note on Keśava.
Note on the bone.
Compare: Vetālapañcaviṃśati.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
vipravarya mahābhāga śṛṇu gāthāṃ manoramām..
vaitālo bhūpatiśreṣṭhaṃ punarvikramamabravīt ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
विप्रवर्य महाभाग शृणु गाथां मनोरमाम्॥
वैतालो भूपतिश्रेष्ठं पुनर्विक्रममब्रवीत् ॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / O best of twice-born, fortunate one, hear this delightful tale. / The vetāla spoke again to the foremost of kings, Vikrama:

3.2.s:
varddhavannagare ramye nānājananiṣevite..
tatrābhavanmahīpālo rūpaseno mahābalaḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
वर्द्धवन्नगरे रम्ये नानाजननिषेविते॥
तत्राभवन्महीपालो रूपसेनो महाबलः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: In the charming city of Vardhavana, inhabited by diverse peoples, / there lived a mighty king named Rūpasena.

3.2.s:
vidvanmālā priyā tasya patisevāparāyaṇā ..
ekadā kṣatriyaḥ kaścinnāmnā vīravaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
विद्वन्माला प्रिया तस्य पतिसेवापरायणा ॥
एकदा क्षत्रियः कश्चिन्नाम्ना वीरवरः स्मृतः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: His beloved, Vidvanmālā, was devoted to serving her husband. / Once a certain kṣatriya known by the name of Vīravara

3.2.s:
putrakanyāsapatnīko vṛttyarthaṃ samupāgataḥ ..
vinayāvanato bhūtvā rūpasenaṃ mahīpatim .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
पुत्रकन्यासपत्नीको वृत्त्यर्थं समुपागतः ॥
विनयावनतो भूत्वा रूपसेनं महीपतिम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: came seeking a livelihood, accompanied by his son, daughter, and wife. / Bowing low with modesty before King Rūpasena,

3.2.s:
kiṃcicchrutvā dadau svarṇaṃ sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ nṛpa ..
vīrasenastu tallabdhvā vahnau tīrthe dvijātiṣu ..5..
3.2.d:
किंचिच्छ्रुत्वा ददौ स्वर्णं सहस्रं प्रत्यहं नृप ॥
वीरसेनस्तु तल्लब्ध्वा वह्नौ तीर्थे द्विजातिषु ॥5॥
3.2.m: having heard a little, [the king] gave him a thousand gold coins every day, O king. / Having obtained it, Vīrasena, on fire, holy baths, and the twice-born

3.2.s:
vyayaṃ kṛtvā tu taccheṣaṃ sa kulye bhuktavānsvayam ..
evaṃ varṣe gate rājanrājalakṣmīḥ śivājñayā ..6..
3.2.d:
व्ययं कृत्वा तु तच्छेषं स कुल्ये भुक्तवान्स्वयम् ॥
एवं वर्षे गते राजन्राजलक्ष्मीः शिवाज्ञया ॥6॥
3.2.m: having spent it, enjoyed the remainder himself with his family. / When a year had thus passed, O king, the Goddess of Royal Fortune, by Śiva's command,

3.2.s:
parīkṣārthaṃ smaśāne ca rodanaṃ bahu kurvatī ..
ardharātre tadā rājā buddhvā prāha svasevakam .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
परीक्षार्थं स्मशाने च रोदनं बहु कुर्वती ॥
अर्धरात्रे तदा राजा बुद्ध्वा प्राह स्वसेवकम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: to test him, wept bitterly in the cremation ground. / Awaking then at midnight, the king said to his servant:

3.2.s:
gaccha vīravara tvaṃ vai yato'sau śrūyate ravaḥ ..
jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ mahyaṃ śīghraṃ nivedaya .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
गच्छ वीरवर त्वं वै यतोऽसौ श्रूयते रवः ॥
ज्ञात्वा तत्कारणं सर्वं मह्यं शीघ्रं निवेदय ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: "Go, Vīravara, to where this sound is heard; / ascertain the entire cause of it, and report it to me quickly."

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vīravaraḥ śastrāstrakuśalo balī ..
sa tatra gatvā yatrāste rājalakṣmīḥ śubhānanā .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वीरवरः शस्त्रास्त्रकुशलो बली ॥
स तत्र गत्वा यत्रास्ते राजलक्ष्मीः शुभानना ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the strong Vīravara, skilled in weapons and missiles, / went to where the fair-faced Goddess of Royal Fortune was staying.

3.2.s:
ślakṣṇaṃ vacaśca tāmāha kimarthaṃ rodane sthitā ..
mahatkaṣṭaṃ ca kiṃ prāptaṃ kāraṇaṃ devi me vada .. 3.2.3.10 ..
3.2.d:
श्लक्ष्णं वचश्च तामाह किमर्थं रोदने स्थिता ॥
महत्कष्टं च किं प्राप्तं कारणं देवि मे वद ॥ 3.2.3.10 ॥
3.2.m: He spoke gentle words to her: "Why are you weeping? / What great suffering has occurred? Tell me the reason, O goddess."

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā rājalakṣmīrvīrasenaṃ tamabravīt ..
rājalakṣmīṃ ca māṃ viddhi rūpasenasya bhūpateḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा राजलक्ष्मीर्वीरसेनं तमब्रवीत् ॥
राजलक्ष्मीं च मां विद्धि रूपसेनस्य भूपतेः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, the royal Fortune said to Vīrasena:
"Know me to be the royal Fortune of King Rūpasena.

3.2.s:
māsānte pralayaṃ yāsye tasmācchocāmi bho balin ..
sa āha śṛṇu bho devi tvadalpāyussa mīritam ..
kena puṇyena dīrghāyustvaṃ bhaveḥ kāraṇaṃ vada .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
मासान्ते प्रलयं यास्ये तस्माच्छोचामि भो बलिन् ॥
स आह शृणु भो देवि त्वदल्पायुस्स मीरितम् ॥
केन पुण्येन दीर्घायुस्त्वं भवेः कारणं वद ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
At the end of the month I shall go to destruction; therefore, O strong one, I grieve."
He said: "Hear, O goddess! It has been declared that your life is short.
By what merit might you obtain a long life? Tell me the means."

3.2.s:
devyuvāca ..
mahābāho mahāprājña yadi te tanayasya vai .. 13 .. ..
3.2.d:
देव्युवाच ॥
महाबाहो महाप्राज्ञ यदि ते तनयस्य वै ॥ 13 ॥ ॥
3.2.m:
The goddess said:
"O mighty-armed one, O exceedingly wise one! If of your son indeed...

3.2.s:
kapālamarpaya tvaṃ ca caṃḍikāyai tadānagha ..
dīrghāyurbhavitā cāhaṃ svāmikāryaṃ prasādhaya..14..
3.2.d:
कपालमर्पय त्वं च चंडिकायै तदानघ ॥
दीर्घायुर्भविता चाहं स्वामिकार्यं प्रसाधय॥14॥
3.2.m:
...you offer the skull to Caṇḍikā, then, O sinless one,
I shall become long-lived. Accomplish your master’s business!"

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vīravaro maṃdiraṃ svayamāgataḥ ..
patnīṃ prāha prasannātmā sutaṃ devyai nivedaya .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वीरवरो मंदिरं स्वयमागतः ॥
पत्नीं प्राह प्रसन्नात्मा सुतं देव्यै निवेदय ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, Vīravara went to his own home,
and with a cheerful heart said to his wife: "Offer our son to the goddess."

3.2.s:
tathetyuktvā tu sā sādhvī tanayaṃ prāha nirbhayā ..
rājño'rthe tava dehaṃ vai putra pāsi kuruṣva tat .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा तु सा साध्वी तनयं प्राह निर्भया ॥
राज्ञोऽर्थे तव देहं वै पुत्र पासि कुरुष्व तत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m:
Saying 'So be it,' that virtuous woman, fearless, spoke to her son:
"For the sake of the king, my son, give your body; do this!"

3.2.s:
tathā matvā tu tatputro bhaginyā mātṛsaṃyutaḥ..
caṃḍikābhavanaṃ prāpyābravītsvapitaraṃ tadā .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
तथा मत्वा तु तत्पुत्रो भगिन्या मातृसंयुतः॥
चंडिकाभवनं प्राप्याब्रवीत्स्वपितरं तदा ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m:
Consenting to that, the son, accompanied by his sister and mother,
went to the temple of Caṇḍikā and then spoke to his father:

3.2.s:
bhostāta me kapālaṃ ca caṃḍikāyai samarpaya ..
dīrghāyuryena yatnena rājalakṣmīśca tatkuru .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
भोस्तात मे कपालं च चंडिकायै समर्पय ॥
दीर्घायुर्येन यत्नेन राजलक्ष्मीश्च तत्कुरु ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m:
"O father! Offer my skull to Caṇḍikā,
and do that by which effort the royal Fortune may become long-lived."

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vīrasenaḥ śiraśchittvā samārpayat ..
tasyānujā mṛtā tatra tathā mātā tathā pitā .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वीरसेनः शिरश्छित्त्वा समार्पयत् ॥
तस्यानुजा मृता तत्र तथा माता तथा पिता ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, Vīrasena severed his head and offered it.
His younger sister died there, as did his mother, and so his father.

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā tadrūpa senastu kāraṇaṃ sarvamāditaḥ ..
sevakaṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ ca matvā tu svaśiro'rpayat .. 3.2.3.20 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा तद्रूप सेनस्तु कारणं सर्वमादितः ॥
सेवकं सत्यसंधं च मत्वा तु स्वशिरोऽर्पयत् ॥ 3.2.3.20 ॥
3.2.m:
Having seen all that reason from the beginning, Rūpasena,
recognizing his servant to be true to his word, offered his own head.

3.2.s:
tadā prasannā sā devī nṛpamujīvya sābravīt ..
varaṃ varaya bhūpāla yatheṣṭaṃ śīghramāpnuyāḥ .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
तदा प्रसन्ना सा देवी नृपमुजीव्य साब्रवीत् ॥
वरं वरय भूपाल यथेष्टं शीघ्रमाप्नुयाः ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m:
Then that pleased goddess, reviving the king, said:
"Choose a boon, O protector of the earth; obtain quickly whatever you desire."

3.2.s:
sa āha vīrasenastu sakulo jīvamāpnuyāt ..
tathetyuktvā tu sā devī tatraivāṃtarhitābhavat .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
स आह वीरसेनस्तु सकुलो जीवमाप्नुयात् ॥
तथेत्युक्त्वा तु सा देवी तत्रैवांतर्हिताभवत् ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
He said: "May Vīrasena, along with his family, obtain life."
Saying 'So be it,' that goddess disappeared right there.

3.2.s:
rūpasenaḥ prasannātmā svasutāṃ kāmarūpiṇīm ..
dadau sutāya vaitālo nṛpatiṃ prāha vismitaḥ..
mukhyasnehaṃ kṛtaṃ kena teṣāṃ madhye vadasva me ..23..
3.2.d:
रूपसेनः प्रसन्नात्मा स्वसुतां कामरूपिणीम् ॥
ददौ सुताय वैतालो नृपतिं प्राह विस्मितः॥
मुख्यस्नेहं कृतं केन तेषां मध्ये वदस्व मे ॥23॥
3.2.m:
Rūpasena, delighted at heart, gave his daughter of wondrous beauty
to his son. The vetāla, astonished, said to the king:
"Tell me, among them, by whom was the foremost love displayed?"

3.2.s:
.. rājovāca ..
mukhyasnehaṃ kṛtaṃ rājñā dāsārthe svatanuṃ dadau ..
svarṇasnehī vīravaro dhamarprītiḥ pativratā ..
baṃdhuprītiśca bhaginī pitṛsnehī tu putrakaḥ .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
॥ राजोवाच ॥
मुख्यस्नेहं कृतं राज्ञा दासार्थे स्वतनुं ददौ ॥
स्वर्णस्नेही वीरवरो धमर्प्रीतिः पतिव्रता ॥
बंधुप्रीतिश्च भगिनी पितृस्नेही तु पुत्रकः ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m:
The king said:
"The foremost love was displayed by the king, who gave his own body for the sake of his servant.
Vīravara loved gold; the devoted wife loved righteousness;
the sister loved her kin; and the little son loved his father.

3.2.s:
mahānsnehaḥ kṛto rājñā rūpasenena dhīmatā .. 25 ..
tulanīya - vetālapañcaviṃśati
vīravara - śūdrakopari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
महान्स्नेहः कृतो राज्ञा रूपसेनेन धीमता ॥ 25 ॥
तुलनीय - वेतालपञ्चविंशति
वीरवर - शूद्रकोपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
The great love was displayed by the wise king Rūpasena."
[Comparable to: Vetālapañcaviṃśati]
[Note on Vīravara and Śūdraka]

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā sa vaitālo rājānamidamabravīt ..
kācidbhogāvatī nāmnā nagarī paramādbhutā ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा स वैतालो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
काचिद्भोगावती नाम्ना नगरी परमाद्भुता ॥1॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
Hearing this, the vetāla spoke these words to the king:
"There was a certain exceedingly wonderful city named Bhogāvatī.

3.2.s:
rūpavarmā ca nṛpatistatra rājyaṃ karoti vai ..
cūḍāmaṇiriti khyātaḥ śuko buddhiviśāradaḥ ..2..
3.2.d:
रूपवर्मा च नृपतिस्तत्र राज्यं करोति वै ॥
चूडामणिरिति ख्यातः शुको बुद्धिविशारदः ॥2॥
3.2.m:
And King Rūpavarmā ruled there.
A parrot renowned as Cūḍāmaṇi, skilled in wisdom,

3.2.s:
tasya bhūpasya gehe ca nivasanañcchubhapaṃjare ..
kadācidrūpavarmā ca triṃśadabda urūrjitaḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य भूपस्य गेहे च निवसनञ्च्छुभपंजरे ॥
कदाचिद्रूपवर्मा च त्रिंशदब्द उरूर्जितः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m:
dwelt in the house of that king in an auspicious cage.
Once, Rūpavarmā, thirty years of age and very mighty,

3.2.s:
papraccha mama yogyā vai śuka kācidvarāṃganā ..
cedasti tarhi me brūhi śrutvā taṃ cābravīcchukaḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
पप्रच्छ मम योग्या वै शुक काचिद्वरांगना ॥
चेदस्ति तर्हि मे ब्रूहि श्रुत्वा तं चाब्रवीच्छुकः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m:
asked: 'O parrot, is there any excellent woman worthy of me?
If there is, tell me.' Hearing that, the parrot said to him:

3.2.s:
magadheśvarabhūpasya kanyā candravatī śubhā ..
tava yogyā hi bho rājansāṃprataṃ tāṃ gṛhāṇa vai .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
मगधेश्वरभूपस्य कन्या चन्द्रवती शुभा ॥
तव योग्या हि भो राजन्सांप्रतं तां गृहाण वै ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
'The auspicious maiden Candravatī, daughter of the king of Magadha,
is indeed worthy of you, O king; take her now.'

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā sa nṛpatirgaṇeśaṃ dvijasattamam ..
preṣayitvā dadau dravyaṃ yathodvāhyā tathā kuru .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा स नृपतिर्गणेशं द्विजसत्तमम् ॥
प्रेषयित्वा ददौ द्रव्यं यथोद्वाह्या तथा कुरु ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, the king, sending Gaṇeśa, the best of twice-borns,
gave wealth [saying]: 'Act in such a way that she is married [to me].'

3.2.s:
gaṇeśopi gatastūrṇaṃ deśe māgadhake śubhe ..
mahādevaṃ ca saṃpūjya cakāra stavanaṃ mudā .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
गणेशोपि गतस्तूर्णं देशे मागधके शुभे ॥
महादेवं च संपूज्य चकार स्तवनं मुदा ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m:
Gaṇeśa too quickly went to the auspicious land of Magadha,
and having worshipped Mahādeva, joyfully performed a hymn of praise:

3.2.s:
namaḥ śivāya śāṃtāya sarvābhīṣṭapradāyine ..
bhavāya śaṃkarāyaiva rudrāya satataṃ namaḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
नमः शिवाय शांताय सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायिने ॥
भवाय शंकरायैव रुद्राय सततं नमः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m:
'Obeisance to Śiva, the peaceful, the granter of all desires,
to Bhava, to Śaṅkara, and perpetual obeisance to Rudra!

3.2.s: mṛḍāyānaṃdarūpāya sarvaduḥkhaharāya ca .. 9 ..
3.2.d: मृडायानंदरूपाय सर्वदुःखहराय च ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: To Mṛḍa, whose nature is bliss, and the remover of all suffering!'

3.2.s:
ityuktavati vipre ca tadā candravatī śubhā ..
kāmāturābravīccaināṃ nāmnā madanamañjarīm .. 3.2.4.10 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्तवति विप्रे च तदा चन्द्रवती शुभा ॥
कामातुराब्रवीच्चैनां नाम्ना मदनमञ्जरीम् ॥ 3.2.4.10 ॥
3.2.m:
While the brāhmaṇa was speaking thus, the auspicious Candravatī,
afflicted with desire, then spoke to that [maina] named Madanamañjarī:

3.2.s:
mama yogyaśca puruṣaḥ kaścidasti mahītale ..
sāha bho rūpavarmā ca yogyo bhogāpurīpatiḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
मम योग्यश्च पुरुषः कश्चिदस्ति महीतले ॥
साह भो रूपवर्मा च योग्यो भोगापुरीपतिः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m:
'Is there any man on the face of the earth who is worthy of me?'
She said: 'O [lady], Rūpavarmā, the lord of Bhogāpurī, is worthy.'

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā tu sā devī durgāṃ vāñchitadāyinīm ..
tuṣṭāva manasā subhrūryayā jātamidaṃ jagat .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु सा देवी दुर्गां वाञ्छितदायिनीम् ॥
तुष्टाव मनसा सुभ्रूर्यया जातमिदं जगत् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, that fair-browed maiden mentally praised Durgā,
the giver of desires, by whom this universe was brought forth:

3.2.s:
namonamo jaganmātarmama kāryapradāyini ..
triliṃgajananī tvaṃ vai varṇamūrtiḥ sanātanī ..13..
3.2.d:
नमोनमो जगन्मातर्मम कार्यप्रदायिनि ॥
त्रिलिंगजननी त्वं वै वर्णमूर्तिः सनातनी ॥13॥
3.2.m:
'Obeisance, obeisance, O mother of the universe, granter of my purpose!
You are the mother of the three liṅgas, the eternal embodiment of the sacred syllables.

3.2.s:
tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā saṃdhyā namastasyai namonamaḥ ..
nṛpatiṃ rūpavarmāṇaṃ matpatiṃ kuru bhoḥ śive..14..
3.2.d:
त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा संध्या नमस्तस्यै नमोनमः ॥
नृपतिं रूपवर्माणं मत्पतिं कुरु भोः शिवे॥14॥
3.2.m:
You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, the twilight prayer; obeisance to her, obeisance, obeisance!
O Śivā, make King Rūpavarmā my husband!'

3.2.s:
iti stutyā prasannābhūjjagadaṃbā jaganmayī..
pitaraṃ magadheśaṃ ca mohayitvā ca mātaram ..15..
3.2.d:
इति स्तुत्या प्रसन्नाभूज्जगदंबा जगन्मयी॥
पितरं मगधेशं च मोहयित्वा च मातरम् ॥15॥
3.2.m:
Pleased by this hymn of praise, the Mother of the Universe, who comprises all existence,
infatuated her father, the lord of Magadha, and her mother,

3.2.s:
vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa māsānte siddharūpiṇī ..
rūpavarmā caṃdravatī bubhujāte paraṃ sukham ..16..
3.2.d:
विवाहं कारयामास मासान्ते सिद्धरूपिणी ॥
रूपवर्मा चंद्रवती बुभुजाते परं सुखम् ॥16॥
3.2.m:
and, being one whose form brings perfection, brought about the marriage at the end of the month.
Rūpavarmā and Candravatī enjoyed supreme happiness.

3.2.s:
ekasmindivase rājanmenāṃ madanamaṃjarīm..
nṛpaḥ prāha vivāhaṃ tvaṃ suśukena kuruṣva bhoḥ .. ..17..
3.2.d:
एकस्मिन्दिवसे राजन्मेनां मदनमंजरीम्॥
नृपः प्राह विवाहं त्वं सुशुकेन कुरुष्व भोः ॥ ॥17॥
3.2.m:
One day, O king, the monarch said to the maina Madanamañjarī:
'Marry with the noble parrot!'

3.2.s:
menakā prāha bho rājanvivāhāścedṛśo matāḥ ..
uttamādhamamadhyāśca puruṣāstrividhāḥ smṛtāḥ..18..
3.2.d:
मेनका प्राह भो राजन्विवाहाश्चेदृशो मताः ॥
उत्तमाधममध्याश्च पुरुषास्त्रिविधाः स्मृताः॥18॥
3.2.m:
The maina said: 'O king, marriages are regarded thus:
men are declared to be of three kinds—superior, inferior, and middling.

3.2.s:
tathaiva trividhā nārī yathā yogyo varo bhavet..
uttamā yo bhavennārī yogyāyā cādhamāya vai ..19..
3.2.d:
तथैव त्रिविधा नारी यथा योग्यो वरो भवेत्॥
उत्तमा यो भवेन्नारी योग्याया चाधमाय वै ॥19॥
3.2.m:
Likewise, a woman is of three kinds, according as a groom may be suitable.
Should a superior woman be suitable indeed for an inferior one?

3.2.s:
śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ rājanmayā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā'bhavat ..
ilāpure vasatyeko vaiśyo lakṣapatirdhanī.. 3.2.4.20 ..
3.2.d:
शृणु तत्कारणं राजन्मया दृष्टं यथाऽभवत् ॥
इलापुरे वसत्येको वैश्यो लक्षपतिर्धनी॥ 3.2.4.20 ॥
3.2.m:
Hear the reason for that, O king, as it was seen by me:
In Ilāpura dwells a wealthy vaiśya, a possessor of hundreds of thousands,

3.2.s:
anapatyo devayājī tasya patnī pativratā ..
bahuyatnena tanayastasya jāto mahādhamaḥ .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
अनपत्यो देवयाजी तस्य पत्नी पतिव्रता ॥
बहुयत्नेन तनयस्तस्य जातो महाधमः ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m:
childless, a performer of sacrifices to the gods; his wife was devoted to her husband.
With great effort a son was born to him, exceedingly vile,

3.2.s:
dyūtakrīḍāparo nityaṃ surāpāne ratassadā ..
veśyāgāmī mahādhūrto nityaṃ māṃsāśanaḥ khalaḥ .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
द्यूतक्रीडापरो नित्यं सुरापाने रतस्सदा ॥
वेश्यागामी महाधूर्तो नित्यं मांसाशनः खलः ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
continually intent on gambling, always devoted to drinking wine,
frequenting courtesans, very wicked, constantly eating meat, base.

3.2.s:
tasya dharmaṃ ca pitarau samālokya vanaṃ gatau ..
naraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ dhyātvā paramaṃ padamāpatuḥ .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य धर्मं च पितरौ समालोक्य वनं गतौ ॥
नरं नारायणं ध्यात्वा परमं पदमापतुः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m:
Seeing his conduct, the parents went to the forest;
meditating on Nara and Nārāyaṇa, they attained the supreme abode.

3.2.s:
madapālastu tanayaḥ kṛtvā sarvadhanavyayam ..
anyadeśe ca vṛttyarthaṃ jagāma dhanavarjitaḥ ..24..
3.2.d:
मदपालस्तु तनयः कृत्वा सर्वधनव्ययम् ॥
अन्यदेशे च वृत्त्यर्थं जगाम धनवर्जितः ॥24॥
3.2.m:
The son, named Madapāla, having squandered all his wealth,
went destitute of money to another country for the sake of a livelihood.

3.2.s:
prāptaścaṃdrapure ramye yatra hemapatiḥ sthitaḥ..
vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa vaiśyaṃ hemapatiṃ hi saḥ .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
प्राप्तश्चंद्रपुरे रम्ये यत्र हेमपतिः स्थितः॥
वृत्तांतं कथयामास वैश्यं हेमपतिं हि सः ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m:
He arrived at charming Candrapura where Hemapati resided.
He related his story to the vaiśya Hemapati:

3.2.s:
devayājī suto'haṃ vai svalpaṃ vai dhanamāhṛtam ..
deśāntare vikrayārthe sindhumārgeṇa prāptavān .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
देवयाजी सुतोऽहं वै स्वल्पं वै धनमाहृतम् ॥
देशान्तरे विक्रयार्थे सिन्धुमार्गेण प्राप्तवान् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m:
'I am the son of Devayājī; a small amount of wealth was gathered [by me];
I arrived by way of the ocean to sell it in another country.

3.2.s:
mahāvāyu prabhāvena dravyaṃ tanmagnamaṃbhasi ..
tallajjayā na yāsye'haṃ pitaraṃ prati māriṣa .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
महावायु प्रभावेन द्रव्यं तन्मग्नमंभसि ॥
तल्लज्जया न यास्येऽहं पितरं प्रति मारिष ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m:
By the power of a great storm, that property sank into the water;
out of shame on that account, I will not return to my father, O worthy sir.'

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā hemapatiḥ svapatnīṃ kāmamaṃjarīm ..
vacaḥ prāha prasannātmā saṃyogo vidhinā kṛtaḥ .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा हेमपतिः स्वपत्नीं काममंजरीम् ॥
वचः प्राह प्रसन्नात्मा संयोगो विधिना कृतः ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, Hemapati, with a delighted heart, spoke these words
to his wife Kāmamañjarī: 'A union has been arranged by destiny.'

3.2.s:
caṃdrakāṃtiṃ sutāṃ dāsye tadvarāya tvadājñayā ..
saṃmaṃtrya daṃpatī rājandadau kanyāṃ vidhānataḥ .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
चंद्रकांतिं सुतां दास्ये तद्वराय त्वदाज्ञया ॥
संमंत्र्य दंपती राजन्ददौ कन्यां विधानतः ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: "I shall give my daughter Candrakānti as his bride with your permission." / Having consulted together, O king, the couple gave away the maiden according to the rules.

3.2.s:
svagṛhe vāsayāmāsa madapālaṃ sutāpatim ..
māsamekamuṣitvā taṃ śvaśuraṃ prāha namradhīḥ .. 3.2.4.30 ..
3.2.d:
स्वगृहे वासयामास मदपालं सुतापतिम् ॥
मासमेकमुषित्वा तं श्वशुरं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥ 3.2.4.30 ॥
3.2.m: He had his son-in-law Madapāla dwell in his own house. / Having resided there for one month, he spoke to his father-in-law with humble mind:

3.2.s:
ājñāṃ dehi dhanādhyakṣa svagehaṃ yāmi mā ciram ..
iti śrutvā hemapatiḥ svasutāṃ svarṇabhūṣitām ..31..
3.2.d:
आज्ञां देहि धनाध्यक्ष स्वगेहं यामि मा चिरम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा हेमपतिः स्वसुतां स्वर्णभूषिताम् ॥31॥
3.2.m: "Give me permission, O master of wealth; I shall go to my own house without delay." / Hearing this, Hemapati [went], having adorned his daughter with gold,

3.2.s:
caṃdrakāṃtiṃ sadāsīṃ ca tasmai dattvā gṛhaṃ yayau ..
narānvisṛjya duṣṭātmā śibikāvāhakānnṛpa ... .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
चंद्रकांतिं सदासीं च तस्मै दत्त्वा गृहं ययौ ॥
नरान्विसृज्य दुष्टात्मा शिबिकावाहकान्नृप ॥॥। 32 ॥
3.2.m: and having given Candrakānti along with a maidservant to him, he went to his house. / Dismissing the men, O king—the palanquin-bearers—the evil-minded one,

3.2.s:
dāsīṃ hatvā tadā patnīṃ visṛjya dhanavarjitām ..
ekākī prāptavāngehaṃ madapālo mahādhamaḥ .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
दासीं हत्वा तदा पत्नीं विसृज्य धनवर्जिताम् ॥
एकाकी प्राप्तवान्गेहं मदपालो महाधमः ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: having then killed the maidservant and abandoned his wife stripped of her wealth, / Madapāla, the most vile man, reached home all alone.

3.2.s:
varṣāṃtare ca tatsvarṇaṃ vyayaṃ kṛtvā kumārgake ..
bubhukṣitaḥ punaḥ śokaṃ cakāra bahudhā nṛpa .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
वर्षांतरे च तत्स्वर्णं व्ययं कृत्वा कुमार्गके ॥
बुभुक्षितः पुनः शोकं चकार बहुधा नृप ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: And within a year, having squandered that gold on evil ways, / hungry once more, O king, he lamented in manifold ways.

3.2.s:
punaśca śvaśurasyaiva gṛhe saṃprāptavānkhalaḥ ..
caṃdrakāṃtistu taṃ dṛṣṭvā svapatiṃ prāha namradhīḥ .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
पुनश्च श्वशुरस्यैव गृहे संप्राप्तवान्खलः ॥
चंद्रकांतिस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा स्वपतिं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: And again the rogue arrived at the very house of his father-in-law. / But seeing him, her own husband, Candrakānti spoke with humble mind:

3.2.s:
mayā niveditaṃ pitre dhanaṃ cauraiśca luṃṭhitam ..
atastvaṃ tyaja saṃtāpaṃ ciraṃ vasa gṛhe mama .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
मया निवेदितं पित्रे धनं चौरैश्च लुंठितम् ॥
अतस्त्वं त्यज संतापं चिरं वस गृहे मम ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m: "I have reported to my father that the wealth was plundered by thieves. / Therefore abandon your distress, and reside in my house for a long time."

3.2.s:
tathetyuktvā mahādhūrta uvāsa katiciddinam ..
jñātvā vimohitā patnīmarddharātre tamovṛte .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा महाधूर्त उवास कतिचिद्दिनम् ॥
ज्ञात्वा विमोहिता पत्नीमर्द्धरात्रे तमोवृते ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m: Saying "So be it," the arch-rogue dwelt there for some days. / Knowing that his wife was asleep in the middle of the night veiled in darkness,

3.2.s:
hatvā tāṃ sa yayau gehaṃ gṛhītvā bahubhūṣaṇam ..
ayogyoyamato rājanvivāhaḥ śukamenayoḥ .. 38 ..
3.2.d:
हत्वा तां स ययौ गेहं गृहीत्वा बहुभूषणम् ॥
अयोग्योयमतो राजन्विवाहः शुकमेनयोः ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: he killed her, took many ornaments, and went home. / Therefore, O king, this marriage between the parrot and the myna is unsuitable.

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā śukaḥ prāha bhūpatiṃ karuṇānidhim ..
vivāhaṃ na kariṣyāmi nāryyā cādhamayā saha .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा शुकः प्राह भूपतिं करुणानिधिम् ॥
विवाहं न करिष्यामि नार्य्या चाधमया सह ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the parrot said to the king, the treasury of compassion: / "I will not marry a base woman.

3.2.s:
adhamā menakā nārī śyāmāṃgā ca kurūpiṇī ..
uttamo'haṃ śuko rājanpuruṣaśca harettanum .. 3.2.4.40 ..
3.2.d:
अधमा मेनका नारी श्यामांगा च कुरूपिणी ॥
उत्तमोऽहं शुको राजन्पुरुषश्च हरेत्तनुम् ॥ 3.2.4.40 ॥
3.2.m: Menakā is a base woman, dark-limbed and deformed. / I am a noble parrot, O king, and a man can take [any] form.

3.2.s:
śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ bhūpa mayā dṛṣṭaṃ mahottamam ..
nagare kāṃcanapure vaṇikchaṃkhapatiḥ śrutaḥ .. 41 ..
3.2.d:
शृणु तत्कारणं भूप मया दृष्टं महोत्तमम् ॥
नगरे कांचनपुरे वणिक्छंखपतिः श्रुतः ॥ 41 ॥
3.2.m: Hear the reason for that, O king, which was seen by me, most noble. / In the city of Kāñcanapura, a merchant named Śaṅkhapati was renowned.

3.2.s:
tasya putrastu medhāvī sindhugupto guṇī dhanī ..
prabhāvatī priyā tasya śrīdattastatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 42 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य पुत्रस्तु मेधावी सिन्धुगुप्तो गुणी धनी ॥
प्रभावती प्रिया तस्य श्रीदत्तस्तत्सुतः स्मृतः ॥ 42 ॥
3.2.m: His son was Sindhugupta, intelligent, virtuous, and wealthy. / Prabhāvatī was his beloved, and Śrīdatta was known as their son.

3.2.s:
vivāhamakarottasya jayaśrīpattane śubhe ..
somadattasya sutayā jayalakṣmyā samanvitam .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
विवाहमकरोत्तस्य जयश्रीपत्तने शुभे ॥
सोमदत्तस्य सुतया जयलक्ष्म्या समन्वितम् ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m: He performed his marriage in the auspicious town of Jayaśrīpattana / with Jayalakṣmī, the daughter of Somadatta.

3.2.s:
śrīdattastu gato deśaṃ vāṇijyārthaṃ kurusthalam ..
āyāti dvādaśābde tu sadhano gehamāgataḥ .. 44 ..
3.2.d:
श्रीदत्तस्तु गतो देशं वाणिज्यार्थं कुरुस्थलम् ॥
आयाति द्वादशाब्दे तु सधनो गेहमागतः ॥ 44 ॥
3.2.m: Śrīdatta, however, went to the Kurusthala country for trade. / In the twelfth year he returned, and came home wealthy.

3.2.s:
jayalakṣmīstu kāmena pīḍitā pitṛmaṃdire ..
amātyatanayenaiva homadattena mohitā .. 45 ..
3.2.d:
जयलक्ष्मीस्तु कामेन पीडिता पितृमंदिरे ॥
अमात्यतनयेनैव होमदत्तेन मोहिता ॥ 45 ॥
3.2.m: Meanwhile, Jayalakṣmī, tormented by passion in her father's mansion, / was infatuated with Homadatta, the minister's son.

3.2.s:
dūtī mārgeṇa taṃ prāpya vyayaṃ kṛtvā dhanaṃ bahu ..
ramayāmāsa sā nārī tena sārddhaṃ mahādhamā .. 46 ..
3.2.d:
दूती मार्गेण तं प्राप्य व्ययं कृत्वा धनं बहु ॥
रमयामास सा नारी तेन सार्द्धं महाधमा ॥ 46 ॥
3.2.m: Reaching him by means of a female messenger and having spent much wealth, / that most vile woman took her pleasure with him.

3.2.s:
trimāsānte ca tatsvāmī śrīdattaḥ śvaśurālaye ..
saṃprāptaḥ sā tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadduḥkhamupāyayau .. 47 ..
3.2.d:
त्रिमासान्ते च तत्स्वामी श्रीदत्तः श्वशुरालये ॥
संप्राप्तः सा तु तं दृष्ट्वा महद्दुःखमुपाययौ ॥ 47 ॥
3.2.m: At the end of three months her husband Śrīdatta arrived / at his father-in-law's house; but seeing him, she fell into great sorrow.

3.2.s:
ardharātre tu tanmātrā preṣitā svapatiṃ prati ..
jayalakṣmīśca saṃprāptā krodhena sphuritādharā..48..
3.2.d:
अर्धरात्रे तु तन्मात्रा प्रेषिता स्वपतिं प्रति ॥
जयलक्ष्मीश्च संप्राप्ता क्रोधेन स्फुरिताधरा॥48॥
3.2.m: At midnight, sent by her mother to her husband, / Jayalakṣmī arrived, her lower lip trembling with anger.

3.2.s:
bahumānena svapatisnehaṃ kṛtvālayaṃ yayau ..
tadā tu kulaṭā sā ca gatā dūtīgṛhaṃ prati .. 49 ..
3.2.d:
बहुमानेन स्वपतिस्नेहं कृत्वालयं ययौ ॥
तदा तु कुलटा सा च गता दूतीगृहं प्रति ॥ 49 ॥
3.2.m: Having shown affection for her husband with great respect, she went to her room; / then that unchaste woman went to the house of the female messenger.

3.2.s:
śūnyālaye homadatto daṃśito bhujagena vai ..
suṣvāpa maraṇaṃ prāpya tadā bālā samāgatā .. 3.2.4.50 ..
3.2.d:
शून्यालये होमदत्तो दंशितो भुजगेन वै ॥
सुष्वाप मरणं प्राप्य तदा बाला समागता ॥ 3.2.4.50 ॥
3.2.m: In an empty house, Homadatta had indeed been bitten by a serpent; / having met his death, he lay asleep; then the young woman arrived.

3.2.s:
vegena ramayāmāsa taṃ jāraṃ viṣamohitam ..
pippalasthaḥ piśācaśca dṛṣṭvā tāṃ jāriṇīṃ śubhām .. 51 ..
3.2.d:
वेगेन रमयामास तं जारं विषमोहितम् ॥
पिप्पलस्थः पिशाचश्च दृष्ट्वा तां जारिणीं शुभाम् ॥ 51 ॥
3.2.m: Impetuously she made love to that paramour stupified by poison. / And a piśāca sitting on a sacred fig tree, seeing that fair adulteress,

3.2.s:
śavadehaṃ ca saṃprāpya ramaṇīṃ tāmarīramat ..
khanitvā daśanairnāsāṃ pippalopari so'gamat .. 52 ..
3.2.d:
शवदेहं च संप्राप्य रमणीं तामरीरमत् ॥
खनित्वा दशनैर्नासां पिप्पलोपरि सोऽगमत् ॥ 52 ॥
3.2.m: entered the corpse and took pleasure with that lovely woman; / biting off her nose with his teeth, he climbed back up the sacred fig tree.

3.2.s:
kaphallo nāma caurastu dṛṣṭvā tatkāraṇaṃ tadā ..
kāminyā anugo bhūtvā maṃdiraṃ tatpraviṣṭavān .. 53 ..
3.2.d:
कफल्लो नाम चौरस्तु दृष्ट्वा तत्कारणं तदा ॥
कामिन्या अनुगो भूत्वा मंदिरं तत्प्रविष्टवान् ॥ 53 ॥
3.2.m: A thief named Kaphalla, seeing that event at that time, / followed the passionate woman and entered that mansion.

3.2.s:
tadā tu jayalakṣmīśca svapatiṃ prāpya durbhagā ..
cakre sā rodanaṃ gāḍhaṃ sarve lokāḥ prata sthire .. 54 ..
3.2.d:
तदा तु जयलक्ष्मीश्च स्वपतिं प्राप्य दुर्भगा ॥
चक्रे सा रोदनं गाढं सर्वे लोकाः प्रत स्थिरे ॥ 54 ॥
3.2.m: Then, however, that wretched Jayalakṣmī, going to her husband, / began weeping bitterly, and all the people stood frozen.

3.2.s:
nāsāhīnāṃ sutāṃ dṛṣṭvā somadatto mahādhanaḥ ..
baddhvā jāmātaraṃ śīghraṃ rājāṃtikamupāyayau .. 55 ..
3.2.d:
नासाहीनां सुतां दृष्ट्वा सोमदत्तो महाधनः ॥
बद्ध्वा जामातरं शीघ्रं राजांतिकमुपाययौ ॥ 55 ॥
3.2.m: Seeing his daughter without her nose, the wealthy Somadatta / quickly bound his son-in-law and approached the king.

3.2.s:
nṛpājñayā rājadūtāstamudbaṃdhanamādadhuḥ ..
tadā kaphallaḥ saṃprāpya sarvaṃ rājñe nyavedayat .. 56 ..
3.2.d:
नृपाज्ञया राजदूतास्तमुद्बंधनमादधुः ॥
तदा कफल्लः संप्राप्य सर्वं राज्ञे न्यवेदयत् ॥ 56 ॥
3.2.m: By the king's command, royal officers prepared him for hanging; / then Kaphalla arrived and reported everything to the king.

3.2.s:
matvā tasya vacaḥ satyaṃ jayalakṣmīṃ mahādhamām ..
rāsabhopari saṃsthāpya kṛtvā durgatirūpiṇīm .. 57 ..
3.2.d:
मत्वा तस्य वचः सत्यं जयलक्ष्मीं महाधमाम् ॥
रासभोपरि संस्थाप्य कृत्वा दुर्गतिरूपिणीम् ॥ 57 ॥
3.2.m: Believing his word to be true, having placed that most vile Jayalakṣmī / upon a donkey and made her into the very image of degradation,

3.2.s:
nagarātpreṣayāmāsa vanaṃ śārdūlasevitam ..
atastvaṃ śṛṇu bhūpāla menā madyogyikā na hi .. 58 ..
3.2.d:
नगरात्प्रेषयामास वनं शार्दूलसेवितम् ॥
अतस्त्वं शृणु भूपाल मेना मद्योग्यिका न हि ॥ 58 ॥
3.2.m: he banished her from the city to a forest frequented by tigers. / Therefore listen, O king: Menā is certainly not suited for me."

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo vikramaṃ prāha namradhīḥ ..
nārī pāpādhikā vātha puruṣastadvadvasva me .. 59 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो विक्रमं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥
नारी पापाधिका वाथ पुरुषस्तद्वद्वस्व मे ॥ 59 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, that vetāla said to Vikrama with humble mind: / "Tell me, is woman more prone to sin, or is man?"

3.2.s:
.. vikrama uvāca .. ..
brahmaṇo'guṇarūpasya māyāvarṇasva rūpiṇī ..
tamo na puṃsakaṃ jñeyaṃ triliṃgaikaṃ tadavyayam .. 3.2.4.60 ..
3.2.d:
॥ विक्रम उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रह्मणोऽगुणरूपस्य मायावर्णस्व रूपिणी ॥
तमो न पुंसकं ज्ञेयं त्रिलिंगैकं तदव्ययम् ॥ 3.2.4.60 ॥
3.2.m: Vikrama said: / "Of Brahman, which is without attributes, Māyā is the visual form; / darkness is to be known as neuter, and the imperishable is united in the three genders.

3.2.s:
avyayaṃ brahmaṇo dhāma māyā liṃgasvarūpiṇī ..
tayā jātamidaṃ viśvaṃ tadaṃbāyai namonamaḥ .. 61 ..
3.2.d:
अव्ययं ब्रह्मणो धाम माया लिंगस्वरूपिणी ॥
तया जातमिदं विश्वं तदंबायै नमोनमः ॥ 61 ॥
3.2.m: The imperishable abode of Brahman has Māyā as the form of gender; / by her this universe was born; salutations again and again to that mother.

3.2.s:
klībā strī sarvadā śreṣṭhā striyāstu puruṣastathā ..
avyādhikaśca puruṣo nārī karmādhikā matā .. 62 ..
3.2.d:
क्लीबा स्त्री सर्वदा श्रेष्ठा स्त्रियास्तु पुरुषस्तथा ॥
अव्याधिकश्च पुरुषो नारी कर्माधिका मता ॥ 62 ॥
3.2.m: A woman is always better than a neuter, and so a man is [better] than a woman. / A man is superior in knowledge, while a woman is considered superior in ritual action.

3.2.s:
klībamajñānamadhikaṃ kathitaṃ pūrvakovidaiḥ ..
karmaiva bandhanaṃ puṃsāṃ jñānaṃ nirbaṃdhana smṛtam .. 63 ..
3.2.d:
क्लीबमज्ञानमधिकं कथितं पूर्वकोविदैः ॥
कर्मैव बन्धनं पुंसां ज्ञानं निर्बंधन स्मृतम् ॥ 63 ॥
3.2.m: The neuter is described by ancient sages as predominantly ignorant; / action alone is the bondage of men, while knowledge is remembered as liberation from bondage.

3.2.s:
ataḥ pāpādhikā nārī puruṣo hīnakilbiṣaḥ .. .. 64 .. ..
tulanīya - vetālapaṃcaviṃśati
śukopari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
अतः पापाधिका नारी पुरुषो हीनकिल्बिषः ॥ ॥ 64 ॥ ॥
तुलनीय - वेतालपंचविंशति
शुकोपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
Therefore, woman has more sin, while man has lesser fault."
Compare: Vetālapañcaviṃśati.
Note on the parrot.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
bhṛguvarya mahābhāga śrutvā vaitāla eva saḥ ..
prasannātmā vacaḥ prāha bhūpatiṃ jñānasaṃpadam .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
भृगुवर्य महाभाग श्रुत्वा वैताल एव सः ॥
प्रसन्नात्मा वचः प्राह भूपतिं ज्ञानसंपदम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / O best of Bhṛgus, O fortunate one, having heard [this], that very vetāla, / being pleased in mind, spoke to the king, who was rich in knowledge:

3.2.s:
ujjayinyāṃ mahārāja mahābala iti śrutaḥ ..
caṃdravaṃśī nṛpaḥ prājño vedaśāstraviśāradaḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
उज्जयिन्यां महाराज महाबल इति श्रुतः ॥
चंद्रवंशी नृपः प्राज्ञो वेदशास्त्रविशारदः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: "In Ujjayinī, O great king, there was renowned a wise king named Mahābala, / of the Lunar dynasty, skilled in the Vedas and Śāstras.

3.2.s:
tasya dūto harerdāsaḥ svāmikāryakaraḥ sadā ..
bhaktimālā priyā tasya sādhusevāparāyaṇā .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य दूतो हरेर्दासः स्वामिकार्यकरः सदा ॥
भक्तिमाला प्रिया तस्य साधुसेवापरायणा ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: His messenger was Haridāsa, always devoted to his master's business; / Bhaktimālā was his beloved, devoted to the service of holy men.

3.2.s:
tasyāṃ jātā rūpavatī kanyā kamalalocanā ..
mahādevīti vikhyātā sarvavidyāviśāradā .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
तस्यां जाता रूपवती कन्या कमललोचना ॥
महादेवीति विख्याता सर्वविद्याविशारदा ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: From her was born a beautiful maiden with lotus-like eyes, / known as Mahādevī, skilled in all sciences.

3.2.s:
haridāsaṃ ca sā prāha śṛṇu tāta vaco mama ..
matto'dhiko naro yo vai tasmai māṃ tu dadasva bhoḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
हरिदासं च सा प्राह शृणु तात वचो मम ॥
मत्तोऽधिको नरो यो वै तस्मै मां तु ददस्व भोः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: And she said to Haridāsa: 'Listen, father, to my word: / Give me to that man who is superior to me.'

3.2.s:
tathetyuktvā pitā rājanrājñāhūto gataḥ sabhām ..
natvā taṃ nṛpatiḥ prāha haridāsa śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा पिता राजन्राज्ञाहूतो गतः सभाम् ॥
नत्वा तं नृपतिः प्राह हरिदास शृणुष्व भोः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Saying 'So be it,' the father, summoned by the king, went to the assembly, O king. / Having bowed to him, the king said: 'Hear, Haridāsa:

3.2.s:
tailaṃgādhipatiṃ gaccha hariścaṃdraṃ mahīpatim ..
tasya kṣemaṃ tathā jñātvā māṃ nivedaya mā ciram .. .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
तैलंगाधिपतिं गच्छ हरिश्चंद्रं महीपतिम् ॥
तस्य क्षेमं तथा ज्ञात्वा मां निवेदय मा चिरम् ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Go to King Hariścandra, the ruler of Tailaṅga; / learn of his welfare, and report to me without delay.'"

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā dvijaḥ prāgāddhariścaṃdraṃ mahāmatim ..
kuśalaṃ varṇayāmāsa mahābalanṛpasya vai .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा द्विजः प्रागाद्धरिश्चंद्रं महामतिम् ॥
कुशलं वर्णयामास महाबलनृपस्य वै ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the twice-born went to the wise Hariścandra / and reported the welfare of King Mahābala.

3.2.s:
śrutvā prasannahṛdayo hariścaṃdro mahīpatiḥ ..
śvaśurastasya nṛpateḥ sa bhūyo harṣamāgataḥ .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नहृदयो हरिश्चंद्रो महीपतिः ॥
श्वशुरस्तस्य नृपतेः स भूयो हर्षमागतः ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing it, King Hariścandra felt joyful in his heart; / being the father-in-law of that king, he rejoiced greatly.

3.2.s:
haridāsaṃ sa papraccha kalerāgamanaṃ kadā ..
ityuktaḥ sa tu taṃ prāha nyūhaśca bhavitādhikam .. 3.2.5.10 ..
3.2.d:
हरिदासं स पप्रच्छ कलेरागमनं कदा ॥
इत्युक्तः स तु तं प्राह न्यूहश्च भविताधिकम् ॥ 3.2.5.10 ॥
3.2.m: He asked Haridāsa: “When is the arrival of the Kali [age]?” / Thus addressed, he said to him: “A flood [of vices] will exceedingly arise.

3.2.s:
yadā rājyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena kalerāgamamanaṃ tadā ..
brahmaṇosya mukhājjāta oṃkāraḥ satyapūjitaḥ ..11..
3.2.d:
यदा राज्यं कृतं तेन कलेरागममनं तदा ॥
ब्रह्मणोस्य मुखाज्जात ओंकारः सत्यपूजितः ॥11॥
3.2.m: When rule is established by him, then comes the arrival of Kali. / From the face of Brahmā was born the Omkāra, worshipped by truth;

3.2.s:
dvitīyāsyācca vividhā bhāṣā loka vimohinī ..
jātā kalerhitārthāya yamalokahitaiṣiṇī .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
द्वितीयास्याच्च विविधा भाषा लोक विमोहिनी ॥
जाता कलेर्हितार्थाय यमलोकहितैषिणी ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: and from his second mouth arose diverse speech that bewilders the world, / meant for the benefit of Kali and desiring the welfare of Yama’s world.

3.2.s:
yadā dharmaṃ ca vedoktaṃ viparītaṃ hi dṛśyate ..
kalirājyaṃ tadā jñeyaṃ mlecchā yasya priyāḥ smṛtāḥ.. .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
यदा धर्मं च वेदोक्तं विपरीतं हि दृश्यते ॥
कलिराज्यं तदा ज्ञेयं म्लेच्छा यस्य प्रियाः स्मृताः॥ ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: When the righteousness declared by the Vedas is seen to be reversed, / then the reign of Kali should be known, to whom the barbarians are said to be dear.

3.2.s:
kalinā'dharmamitreṇa sarve devā nirākṛtāḥ ..
pāpasyaiva mṛṣā bhāryā duḥkhaṃ tattanayaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
कलिनाऽधर्ममित्रेण सर्वे देवा निराकृताः ॥
पापस्यैव मृषा भार्या दुःखं तत्तनयः स्मृतः ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: By Kali, the friend of unrighteousness, all gods are set aside; / Falsehood is the wife of Sin, and Sorrow is said to be their son.

3.2.s:
durgatistasya cārdhāṃgī gehegehe tadā bhavet ..
krodhavaśyāḥ nṛpāḥ sarve brāhmaṇāḥ kāmakiṃkarāḥ .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
दुर्गतिस्तस्य चार्धांगी गेहेगेहे तदा भवेत् ॥
क्रोधवश्याः नृपाः सर्वे ब्राह्मणाः कामकिंकराः ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Misfortune becomes his half-body in every house. / All kings are swayed by anger, and brāhmaṇas are slaves of lust.

3.2.s:
lobhavaśyāstu dhanino mahattvaṃ śūdrakā gatāḥ ..
nāryo lajjāvihīnāśca kiṃkarāḥ svāmighātakāḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
लोभवश्यास्तु धनिनो महत्त्वं शूद्रका गताः ॥
नार्यो लज्जाविहीनाश्च किंकराः स्वामिघातकाः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: The wealthy are under the sway of greed, and low-caste people attain greatness. / Women are shameless, and servants kill their masters.

3.2.s:
niṣphalā tu mahī jātā kalau prāpte hi dṛśyate ..
ye hareḥ śaraṇaṃ prāptāste sarve muditāḥ kalau .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
निष्फला तु मही जाता कलौ प्राप्ते हि दृश्यते ॥
ये हरेः शरणं प्राप्तास्ते सर्वे मुदिताः कलौ ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: When Kali arrives, the earth is seen to have become barren. / Those who take refuge in Hari are all delighted in the Kali [age].”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā hariścaṃdro dattvā tasmai sudakṣiṇām ..
svagehaṃ prāptavānrājā viprastu śibiraṃ yayau .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा हरिश्चंद्रो दत्त्वा तस्मै सुदक्षिणाम् ॥
स्वगेहं प्राप्तवान्राजा विप्रस्तु शिबिरं ययौ ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, Hariścandra gave him a generous priestly fee; / the king returned to his own home, and the vipra went to his lodging.

3.2.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra brāhmaṇo buddhikovidaḥ ..
svavidyāṃ darśayāmāsa haridāsāya dhīmate .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र ब्राह्मणो बुद्धिकोविदः ॥
स्वविद्यां दर्शयामास हरिदासाय धीमते ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: In the meantime, a brāhmaṇa skilled in intellect / demonstrated his lore to the wise Haridāsa.

3.2.s:
vimānaṃ śīghragaṃ nāma devyā dattaṃ mahottamam ..
maṃtrajāpātsamudbhūtaṃ kāmajaṃ vismayapradam .. 3.2.5.20 ..
3.2.d:
विमानं शीघ्रगं नाम देव्या दत्तं महोत्तमम् ॥
मंत्रजापात्समुद्भूतं कामजं विस्मयप्रदम् ॥ 3.2.5.20 ॥
3.2.m: A celestial chariot named Śīghraga, excellent and bestowed by the goddess, / born from the chanting of mantras, moving at will, inspiring wonder—

3.2.s:
tasmindadarśa kanyārthe tadā vipro vimohitaḥ ..
varitvā taṃ svakanyārthaṃ tataḥ svapuramāgataḥ .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मिन्ददर्श कन्यार्थे तदा विप्रो विमोहितः ॥
वरित्वा तं स्वकन्यार्थं ततः स्वपुरमागतः ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: seeing him in it, the vipra was enchanted for the sake of his daughter. / Having chosen him for his daughter, he then returned to his own city.

3.2.s:
haridāsasya tanayo mukuṃdo nāma kovidaḥ ..
paṭhitvā svaguruṃ prāha vṛṇīṣva gurudakṣiṇām .. 22..
3.2.d:
हरिदासस्य तनयो मुकुंदो नाम कोविदः ॥
पठित्वा स्वगुरुं प्राह वृणीष्व गुरुदक्षिणाम् ॥ 22॥
3.2.m: Haridāsa had a learned son named Mukunda. / Having finished his studies, he said to his teacher: “Choose your teacher’s fee.”

3.2.s:
gururāha ca śiṣyaṃ taṃ śṛṇu vācaṃ mukuṃda me ..
dāpaya svasya bhaginīṃ matputrāya ca dhīmate ..23..
3.2.d:
गुरुराह च शिष्यं तं शृणु वाचं मुकुंद मे ॥
दापय स्वस्य भगिनीं मत्पुत्राय च धीमते ॥23॥
3.2.m: The teacher said to the disciple: “Listen to my word, Mukunda: / give your sister to my wise son.”

3.2.s:
tathetyuktvā mukuṃdastu svagehaṃ śīghramāyayau ..
tasminkāle mahādevī drauṇiśiṣyaṃ dvijaṃ śubham .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा मुकुंदस्तु स्वगेहं शीघ्रमाययौ ॥
तस्मिन्काले महादेवी द्रौणिशिष्यं द्विजं शुभम् ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: Saying “So be it,” Mukunda went quickly to his own home. / At that time, Mahādevī [chose] an auspicious twice-born disciple of Drauṇi;

3.2.s:
vāmanaṃ varayāmāsa taṃ vipraṃ śabdavedhinam ..
dakṣiṇādibhirabhyarcya tāṃbūlena vidhānataḥ .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
वामनं वरयामास तं विप्रं शब्दवेधिनम् ॥
दक्षिणादिभिरभ्यर्च्य तांबूलेन विधानतः ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: she chose Vāmana, that vipra who could shoot arrows by sound alone, / having duly honoured him with fees, betel, and other offerings.

3.2.s:
trayaste brāhmaṇāḥ prāptāḥ sutārthe guṇakovidāḥ ..
etasminnantare kāmī rākṣaso daivamohitaḥ .. .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
त्रयस्ते ब्राह्मणाः प्राप्ताः सुतार्थे गुणकोविदाः ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे कामी राक्षसो दैवमोहितः ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: Thus three brāhmaṇas skilled in virtues arrived for the sake of the daughter. / In the meantime, a lustful rākṣasa, deluded by destiny,

3.2.s:
mahādevīṃ jahārāśu prāpto viṃdhyācale girau ..
tadā te duḥkhino bhūtvā vilepuḥ kāmapīḍitā .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
महादेवीं जहाराशु प्राप्तो विंध्याचले गिरौ ॥
तदा ते दुःखिनो भूत्वा विलेपुः कामपीडिता ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: swiftly abducted Mahādevī and reached the Vindhya mountain. / Then, stricken with grief and tormented by longing, they lamented.

3.2.s:
dhīmānnāma dvijo vidvāṃstānprāha gaṇakottamaḥ..

3.2.m: Engaged in dispute with each other, having seen the girl and being pursued by love, / [the vetāla asked:] “To whom is the maiden suited? O King, kindly tell me.”

3.2.m: Sūta said: / Hearing his words, King Vikrama, / bent with humility, addressed the vetāla, the servant of Rudra:

arddharātre mahāgaurī nṛpaṃ prāha vṛṇīṣva bhoḥ ..

3.2.m: At midnight Mahāgaurī said to the king: ‘Choose a boon!’ / Hearing that nectar-like utterance, Dharmaśīla, best of kings, / bowed in humility and offered praise so that Durgā would be pleased.”

3.2.m: Dharmaśīla said: / “You alone are primordial Nature, eternal, the embodiment of all letters.

3.2.m: are born through your sport. O Mother of the universe, salutations to you!” / To the king who had spoken thus, an incorporeal voice spoke:

3.2.m: Walking along the royal road accompanied by her father, afflicted by fatigue, / the washerman Kalibhojana was infatuated by the force of passion.

3.2.s:
kāmāṃdhaścaṃḍikāṃ prāha jaganmātaḥ sanātani ..

3.2.m: Blinded by passion, he said to Caṇḍikā: “O Mother of the world, eternal one! / If this fair-browed girl becomes mine, then I will offer you my head.

3.2.s:

3.2.m: She is the washerman’s auspicious daughter, suited to my caste.” / Hearing this speech of the washerman, indeed, the goddess

3.2.m: Having enjoyed diverse pleasures with her that granted happiness, / after a year he went quickly and offered his head to the goddess.

3.2.s:

3.2.s:
caṃpāpurī ca vikhyātā campakeśo mahīpatiḥ ..
tatrāste balavāndhanvī mahiṣī tatsulocanā .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
चंपापुरी च विख्याता चम्पकेशो महीपतिः ॥
तत्रास्ते बलवान्धन्वी महिषी तत्सुलोचना ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: There was a celebrated city named Campāpurī, and its king was Campakeśa. / There lived that strong archer; his queen was Sulocanā.

3.2.s:
trilokasuṃdarī nāma kanyā tasyāmajāyata ..
vadanaṃ candravadyasyā bhruvau cāpasame smṛte .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
त्रिलोकसुंदरी नाम कन्या तस्यामजायत ॥
वदनं चन्द्रवद्यस्या भ्रुवौ चापसमे स्मृते ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: A maiden named Trilokasundarī was born to her, / whose face was like the moon, and whose eyebrows were like bows.

3.2.s:
mṛgākṣī kokilaravā komalāṃgī mahottamā ..
devairmanovṛtā bālā kimanyairmānuṣairnṛpa .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
मृगाक्षी कोकिलरवा कोमलांगी महोत्तमा ॥
देवैर्मनोवृता बाला किमन्यैर्मानुषैर्नृप ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: Deer-eyed, with the voice of a cuckoo, tender-limbed, and most excellent, / that maiden was desired in heart by the gods, to say nothing of mortals, O king!

3.2.s:
tasyāḥ svayaṃvaro jāto nṛpā bahuvidhāstadā ..
tasyā yogena saṃprāptā ye bhūpā bhuvi viśrutāḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
तस्याः स्वयंवरो जातो नृपा बहुविधास्तदा ॥
तस्या योगेन संप्राप्ता ये भूपा भुवि विश्रुताः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: A svayaṃvara was held for her, and then kings of many kinds, / rulers famous on earth, arrived in connection with her.

3.2.s:
indro yamaḥ kuberaśca varuṇo vibudhottamaḥ ..
kṛtvā naramayaṃ rūpaṃ tadarthe samupāgatāḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
इन्द्रो यमः कुबेरश्च वरुणो विबुधोत्तमः ॥
कृत्वा नरमयं रूपं तदर्थे समुपागताः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Indra, Yama, Kubera, and Varuṇa, the best of gods, / having assumed human forms, arrived for her sake.

3.2.s:
caṃpakeśamidaṃ prāha śṛṇu rājanvaco mama ..
sarvaśāstreṣu nipuṇaṃ rūpavantaṃ manoramam ..
indradattaṃ ca māṃ viddhi svasutāṃ me samarpaya .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
चंपकेशमिदं प्राह शृणु राजन्वचो मम ॥
सर्वशास्त्रेषु निपुणं रूपवन्तं मनोरमम् ॥
इन्द्रदत्तं च मां विद्धि स्वसुतां मे समर्पय ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: [One] said this to Campakeśa: “Listen, O king, to my words! / Know me as Indradatta, skilled in all scriptures, handsome, and delightful; / give your daughter to me!”

3.2.s:
dvitīyastu tadā prāha dharmadattaṃ manoramam ..
dhanurvedeṣu nipuṇaṃ svakanyāṃ dātumarhasi .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
द्वितीयस्तु तदा प्राह धर्मदत्तं मनोरमम् ॥
धनुर्वेदेषु निपुणं स्वकन्यां दातुमर्हसि ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: Then the second said: “You ought to give your maiden / to Dharmadatta, who is charming and skilled in archery.”

3.2.s:
tṛtīyaścāha bho rājandhanapālāya śobhine ..
sarvajīvasya bhāṣāṇāṃ jñāyine guṇarūpiṇe ..
