तथैव मत्वा स नृपः सुतां चन्द्रावलीं शुभाम् ॥ 3.2.14.30 ॥
3.2.m:
"O king, give your daughter to me for the sexual pleasure of his son."
Thinking in that very way, that king, having given his auspicious daughter Candrāvalī,

3.2.s:
dattvā ca vedavidhinā bahudhā dravyasaṃyutām ..
svayaṃ cakāra rājyaṃ vai brahmadoṣavivarjitaḥ .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
दत्त्वा च वेदविधिना बहुधा द्रव्यसंयुताम् ॥
स्वयं चकार राज्यं वै ब्रह्मदोषविवर्जितः ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m:
according to Vedic rites, together with abundant wealth,
himself ruled the kingdom, freed from the sin against a Brahmin.

3.2.s:
śaśī tu bhūpateḥ kanyāṃ gṛhītvā svagṛhaṃ yayau ..
sudevastu tadā duḥkhī mūladevamuvāca ha .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
शशी तु भूपतेः कन्यां गृहीत्वा स्वगृहं ययौ ॥
सुदेवस्तु तदा दुःखी मूलदेवमुवाच ह ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m:
Śaśin, having taken the king's daughter, went to his own house.
Then Sudeva, sorrowful, said to Mūladeva:

3.2.s:
madīyeyaṃ nṛpasutā bhogapatnī mahottamā ..
tacchrutvā mūladevastu vismitaḥ sa tathākarot .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
मदीयेयं नृपसुता भोगपत्नी महोत्तमा ॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा मूलदेवस्तु विस्मितः स तथाकरोत् ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m:
"This daughter of the king is my most excellent wife for pleasure."
Having heard that, Mūladeva, astonished, acted accordingly.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā nṛpatiṃ prāha vaitālo rudrakiṃkaraḥ ..
kasmai prāptā nṛpasutā dharmatastadvadasva me .. 34 .. ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा नृपतिं प्राह वैतालो रुद्रकिंकरः ॥
कस्मै प्राप्ता नृपसुता धर्मतस्तद्वदस्व मे ॥ 34 ॥ ॥
3.2.m:
Having said this, the vetāla, the attendant of Rudra, said to the king:
"Tell me, by law, to whom did the king's daughter belong?"

3.2.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
pitāmātrājñayā putrī devānāṃ sanmukhe sthitā ..
yasmai niveditā tasmai sā yogyā dharmataḥ sadā .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
॥ राजोवाच ॥ ॥
पितामात्राज्ञया पुत्री देवानां सन्मुखे स्थिता ॥
यस्मै निवेदिता तस्मै सा योग्या धर्मतः सदा ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m:
The king said:
"By the command of father and mother, the daughter standing before the gods,
to whomever she was given, she is lawfully and always suited for him.

3.2.s:
śāstreṣu kathitaṃ deva strīratnaṃ sarvadaiva hi ..
yathākṣetraṃ bhuvi khyātaṃ bījamantrena ropitam .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
शास्त्रेषु कथितं देव स्त्रीरत्नं सर्वदैव हि ॥
यथाक्षेत्रं भुवि ख्यातं बीजमन्त्रेन रोपितम् ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m:
In the scriptures, O lord, an excellent woman is always spoken of [thus]:
just as a field known on earth, where a seed is planted with a mantra,

3.2.s:
tatkṣetraṃ kṛṣikārasya bījadāturna caiva ha ..
tasmādvai rājatanayā śaśinaṃ varayiṣyati .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
तत्क्षेत्रं कृषिकारस्य बीजदातुर्न चैव ह ॥
तस्माद्वै राजतनया शशिनं वरयिष्यति ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m:
that field belongs to the farmer, and not to the giver of the seed.
Therefore the king's daughter shall indeed choose Śaśin.

3.2.s: sudevasya vai tanayo yogyatvaṃ hi gamiṣyati .. 38 ..
3.2.d: सुदेवस्य वै तनयो योग्यत्वं हि गमिष्यति ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: The son of Sudeva will indeed attain suitability."

3.2.s:
iti te kathitaṃ deva yathāśāstreṣu bhāṣitam ..
kiṃ kṛtaṃ mantriputreṇa tathaiva kathayasva me .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
इति ते कथितं देव यथाशास्त्रेषु भाषितम् ॥
किं कृतं मन्त्रिपुत्रेण तथैव कथयस्व मे ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m:
"This has been told to you, O divine one, as it is declared in the scriptures.
Tell me likewise what was done by the minister's son."

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā sa hovāca sa putro madanālasaḥ ..
vṛndāvanaṃ śubhaṃ prāpya rādhākuṇḍe samāgataḥ .. 3.2.14.40 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा स होवाच स पुत्रो मदनालसः ॥
वृन्दावनं शुभं प्राप्य राधाकुण्डे समागतः ॥ 3.2.14.40 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, he spoke: "That son, Madanālasa,
having reached auspicious Vṛndāvana, came to Rādhākuṇḍa.

3.2.s:
sa snātvā bahulā ṣṭamyāṃ tatpuṇyena nṛpottama ..
bhasmasādabhavatpāpaṃ yena mohatvamāgataḥ .. 41 ..
3.2.d:
स स्नात्वा बहुला ष्टम्यां तत्पुण्येन नृपोत्तम ॥
भस्मसादभवत्पापं येन मोहत्वमागतः ॥ 41 ॥
3.2.m:
Having bathed there on the dark aṣṭamī, by the merit of that, O best of kings,
the sin by which he had fallen into delusion was reduced to ashes.

3.2.s: smṛtvā sa hṛdi goviṃdaṃ tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā .. 42 ..
3.2.d: स्मृत्वा स हृदि गोविंदं तुष्टाव श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ॥ 42 ॥
3.2.m: Remembering Govinda in his heart, he praised [Him] with gentle voice:"

3.2.s:
.. madanālasa uvāca .. ..
namaste dayāsiṃdhave kṛṣṇadeva tvayedaṃ tataṃ viśvamambhodhirūpam ..
tvayaikena līlārthato devadeva priyārādhayā sārddhametaddhi guptam.. .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
॥ मदनालस उवाच ॥ ॥
नमस्ते दयासिंधवे कृष्णदेव त्वयेदं ततं विश्वमम्भोधिरूपम् ॥
त्वयैकेन लीलार्थतो देवदेव प्रियाराधया सार्द्धमेतद्धि गुप्तम्॥ ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m:
Madanālasa said:
"Homage to You, ocean of compassion, Lord Kṛṣṇa! By You this universe has been spread out in the form of an ocean.
By You alone, for the sake of sport, O God of gods, this has been kept secret together with beloved Rādhā.

3.2.s:
jagatyantakāle tvayā kālamūrtyā jagatsaṃhṛtaṃ vai namastenamaste ..
madīyā ca buddhirhṛṣīkeśa śuddhā yathā syāttathaiveśa śīghraṃ kuru tvam .. .. 44 ..
3.2.d:
जगत्यन्तकाले त्वया कालमूर्त्या जगत्संहृतं वै नमस्तेनमस्ते ॥
मदीया च बुद्धिर्हृषीकेश शुद्धा यथा स्यात्तथैवेश शीघ्रं कुरु त्वम् ॥ ॥ 44 ॥
3.2.m:
At the time of the world's end, the universe is destroyed by You in the form of Time; homage to You, homage!
And make my intellect pure, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Lord, quickly make it so!"

3.2.s:
iti stotraprabhāvena devadevena mocitā ..
kāmapāśāttasya buddhiḥ sa kṣatrī gṛhamāyayau .. 45 ..
3.2.d:
इति स्तोत्रप्रभावेन देवदेवेन मोचिता ॥
कामपाशात्तस्य बुद्धिः स क्षत्री गृहमाययौ ॥ 45 ॥
3.2.m:
By the power of this hymn, his intellect was released
from the snare of lust by the God of gods; that kṣatriya returned home.

3.2.s:
ramaṇīṃ svāṃ samāliṃgya nananda mudito nṛpa ..
vipradoṣavināśāya hṛdi saṃcintya buddhimān..
sudevaṃ sa samāhūya svāṃ svasāraṃ dadau mudā .. 46..
3.2.d:
रमणीं स्वां समालिंग्य ननन्द मुदितो नृप ॥
विप्रदोषविनाशाय हृदि संचिन्त्य बुद्धिमान्॥
सुदेवं स समाहूय स्वां स्वसारं ददौ मुदा ॥ 46॥
3.2.m:
Embracing his lovely woman, he rejoiced, delighted, O king.
Reflecting in his heart to destroy the sin against the Brahmin, the wise one,
having summoned Sudeva, joyfully gave his own sister [to him].

3.2.s:
sudevastasya bhaginīṃ kṣatriyasya madāturām ..
dharmeṇodvāhya svagehaṃ prāptavānkāmakiṃkaraḥ .. 47 ..
3.2.d:
सुदेवस्तस्य भगिनीं क्षत्रियस्य मदातुराम् ॥
धर्मेणोद्वाह्य स्वगेहं प्राप्तवान्कामकिंकरः ॥ 47 ॥
3.2.m:
Sudeva, a servant of desire, having lawfully married
the sister of that kṣatriya, who was stricken with passion, went to his own home.

3.2.s:
iti te kathitaṃ bhūpa caritraṃ tasya dhīmataḥ ..
mūladevasya viprasya tathānyatkathayāmyaham.. .. 48 ..
tulanīya - kathāsaritsāgare vetālapañcaviṃśati
3.2.d:
इति ते कथितं भूप चरित्रं तस्य धीमतः ॥
मूलदेवस्य विप्रस्य तथान्यत्कथयाम्यहम्॥ ॥ 48 ॥
तुलनीय - कथासरित्सागरे वेतालपञ्चविंशति
3.2.m:
"Thus has the conduct of that wise Brahmin Mūladeva been told to you, O king.
Now I shall tell another."
To be compared with the Vetālapañcaviṃśati in the Kathāsaritsāgara.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
praśasya bhūpatiṃ śuddhaṃ vetālo rudrakiṃkaraḥ ..
punarākhyānakaṃ vipra varṇayāmāsa sundaram .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
प्रशस्य भूपतिं शुद्धं वेतालो रुद्रकिंकरः ॥
पुनराख्यानकं विप्र वर्णयामास सुन्दरम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
Having praised the pure king, the vetāla, the attendant of Rudra,
again described a beautiful story, O Brahmin.

3.2.s:
kānyakujje mahārāja brāhmaṇo dānaśīlakaḥ ..
babhūva satyasaṃdhaśca devīpūjanatatparaḥ ..
pratigraheṇa yaddravyaṃ tena dānamacīkarat .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
कान्यकुज्जे महाराज ब्राह्मणो दानशीलकः ॥
बभूव सत्यसंधश्च देवीपूजनतत्परः ॥
प्रतिग्रहेण यद्द्रव्यं तेन दानमचीकरत् ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m:
"In Kānyakubja, O great king, there was a Brahmin devoted to giving,
true to his word, and intent on worshipping the Goddess.
Whatever wealth [he obtained] by acceptance of gifts, with that he gave charity.

3.2.s:
kadācittu śaratkāle navadurgāvrataṃ hyabhūt ..
na prāptaṃ dānato dravyaṃ tadā ciṃtāturo'bhavat ..3..
3.2.d:
कदाचित्तु शरत्काले नवदुर्गाव्रतं ह्यभूत् ॥
न प्राप्तं दानतो द्रव्यं तदा चिंतातुरोऽभवत् ॥3॥
3.2.m:
Once in autumn there occurred the Navadurgā vrata.
Wealth was not obtained through donations; then he became distressed with worry:

3.2.s:
kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā cādya yena dravyayuto hyaham ..
kanyā nimaṃtritāścādya kathaṃ tāṃ bhojayāmyaham ..4..
3.2.d:
किं कर्तव्यं मया चाद्य येन द्रव्ययुतो ह्यहम् ॥
कन्या निमंत्रिताश्चाद्य कथं तां भोजयाम्यहम् ॥4॥
3.2.m:
'What should be done by me today so that I may possess wealth?
Maidens have been invited today; how shall I feed them?'

3.2.s:
iti śokasamāyuktastadā devīprasādataḥ ..
mudrāḥ pañca tadā prāptāstābhirvratamacīkarat .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
इति शोकसमायुक्तस्तदा देवीप्रसादतः ॥
मुद्राः पञ्च तदा प्राप्तास्ताभिर्व्रतमचीकरत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
While he was filled with grief in this manner, then by the grace of the Goddess,
five coins were obtained; with them he performed the vrata.

3.2.s:
nirāhāravrataṃ tena kṛtaṃ tu navamāhnikam ..
tena vrataprabhāvena mṛto devatvamāgataḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
निराहारव्रतं तेन कृतं तु नवमाह्निकम् ॥
तेन व्रतप्रभावेन मृतो देवत्वमागतः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
He performed a fasting vrata lasting nine days.
By the power of that vrata, having died, he attained divinity.

3.2.s:
jīmūtaketuriti ca sobhūdvidyādharādhipaḥ ..
himācalagirau ramye pure vidyādhare śubhe ..7..
3.2.d:
जीमूतकेतुरिति च सोभूद्विद्याधराधिपः ॥
हिमाचलगिरौ रम्ये पुरे विद्याधरे शुभे ॥7॥
3.2.m:
He became the lord of the vidyādharas named Jīmūtaketu,
on the delightful Himācala mountain, in the auspicious city of the vidyādharas.

3.2.s:
uvāsa katicidvarṣāndivya bhogaprabhogavān..
tatra kalpadrumaṃ nityaṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
उवास कतिचिद्वर्षान्दिव्य भोगप्रभोगवान्॥
तत्र कल्पद्रुमं नित्यं पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m:
He lived for some years enjoying celestial pleasures.
There he daily worshipped the wish-granting tree with devotion.

3.2.s:
tena vṛkṣaprabhāvena jātaḥ putro mahottamaḥ ..
sarvākalāsu nipuṇo nāmnā jīmūtavāhanaḥ .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
तेन वृक्षप्रभावेन जातः पुत्रो महोत्तमः ॥
सर्वाकलासु निपुणो नाम्ना जीमूतवाहनः ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m:
By the power of that tree, a most excellent son was born,
skilled in all the arts, named Jīmūtavāhana.

3.2.s:
sa vai pūrvabhave rājanmadhyadeśe mahottame ..
kṣatriyaḥ śūrasenākhyo babhūva vasudhādhipaḥ .. 3.2.15.10 ..
3.2.d:
स वै पूर्वभवे राजन्मध्यदेशे महोत्तमे ॥
क्षत्रियः शूरसेनाख्यो बभूव वसुधाधिपः ॥ 3.2.15.10 ॥
3.2.m:
In a previous birth, O king, in the most excellent Madhyadeśa,
he had been a ruler of the earth, a kṣatriya named Śūrasena.

3.2.s:
ekadā mṛgayākelilolupaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ ..
prāptavānutpalāraṇyaṃ yatra vālmīkisaṃsthitiḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
एकदा मृगयाकेलिलोलुपः स महीपतिः ॥
प्राप्तवानुत्पलारण्यं यत्र वाल्मीकिसंस्थितिः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m:
Once, eager for the sport of hunting, that king
reached the Utpala forest where Vālmīki resided.

3.2.s:
caitraśuklanavamyāṃ tu na kṛtaṃ jīvaghātanam ..
utsavaṃ rāmadivase cakāra vidhivannṛpaḥ .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
चैत्रशुक्लनवम्यां तु न कृतं जीवघातनम् ॥
उत्सवं रामदिवसे चकार विधिवन्नृपः ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
On the ninth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, he did not kill any living creature.
The king duly held a festival on the day of Rāma.

3.2.s: vālmīkeśca kuṭīmadhye rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtam .. 13 ..
3.2.d: वाल्मीकेश्च कुटीमध्ये रात्रौ जागरणं कृतम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: A vigil was kept at night inside the hut of Vālmīki.

3.2.s:
śrutā rāmamayī gāthā tasya puṇyaprabhāvataḥ ..
vidyādharatvamāpanno mumude tatra śakravat ..14..
3.2.d:
श्रुता राममयी गाथा तस्य पुण्यप्रभावतः ॥
विद्याधरत्वमापन्नो मुमुदे तत्र शक्रवत् ॥14॥
3.2.m:
The story relating to Rāma was heard; by the power of that merit,
he attained the state of a vidyādhara and rejoiced there like Śakra.

3.2.s:
kalpavṛkṣasya vai pūjā kṛtā tena mahātmanā ..
varṣāṃtare drumaḥ prāha varaṃ varaya sattama .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
कल्पवृक्षस्य वै पूजा कृता तेन महात्मना ॥
वर्षांतरे द्रुमः प्राह वरं वरय सत्तम ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m:
Worship of the wish-granting tree was performed by that great-souled one.
After a year, the tree said: 'Choose a boon, O best of men!'

3.2.s:
sa tamāha mahāvṛkṣa madīyaṃ nagaraṃ śubham ..
dhanadhānyasa māyuktaṃ yathaiva syāttathā kuru .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
स तमाह महावृक्ष मदीयं नगरं शुभम् ॥
धनधान्यस मायुक्तं यथैव स्यात्तथा कुरु ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m:
He said to it: 'O great tree, act in such a way
that my auspicious city may be endowed with wealth and grain.'

3.2.s:
ityukte sati vṛkṣeṇa nagaraṃ bhūpateḥ samam ..
kṛtaṃ tadā na ko'pyāsīdyo manyetpārthivāśrayam .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्ते सति वृक्षेण नगरं भूपतेः समम् ॥
कृतं तदा न कोऽप्यासीद्यो मन्येत्पार्थिवाश्रयम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m:
When this was spoken by the tree, the city was made equal to [the wealth of] a king;
then there was no one who regarded the patronage of a monarch [as necessary].

3.2.s:
sarve te rājatulyāśca kalpavṛkṣaprasādataḥ ..
tadā tau tu pitāputrau tapaso'rthe vanaṃ gatau ..18..
3.2.d:
सर्वे ते राजतुल्याश्च कल्पवृक्षप्रसादतः ॥
तदा तौ तु पितापुत्रौ तपसोऽर्थे वनं गतौ ॥18॥
3.2.m:
All of them were equal to kings by the grace of the wish-granting tree.
Then both father and son went to the forest for the sake of austerities.

3.2.s:
malayādrau mahāramye tepaturbahulaṃ tapaḥ..
ekasmindivase rājanmalayadhvajabhūpateḥ .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
मलयाद्रौ महारम्ये तेपतुर्बहुलं तपः॥
एकस्मिन्दिवसे राजन्मलयध्वजभूपतेः ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m:
On the very delightful Malaya mountain, they performed intense austerities.
One day, O king, of King Malayadhvaja,

3.2.s:
kamalākṣīti vikhyātā kanyā ca śivamaṃdire ..
svasakhyā sahitā prāptā śivapūjanatatparā .. 3.2.15.20 ..
3.2.d:
कमलाक्षीति विख्याता कन्या च शिवमंदिरे ॥
स्वसख्या सहिता प्राप्ता शिवपूजनतत्परा ॥ 3.2.15.20 ॥
3.2.m:
the daughter known as Kamalākṣī, accompanied by her female friend,
intent on worshipping Śiva, arrived at the temple of Śiva.

3.2.s:
jīmūtavāhanaścaiva pūjārthe maṃdiraṃ yayau ..
bālāṃ dadarśa divyāṃgīṃ sarvabhūṣāsamanvitām .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
जीमूतवाहनश्चैव पूजार्थे मंदिरं ययौ ॥
बालां ददर्श दिव्यांगीं सर्वभूषासमन्विताम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m:
And Jīmūtavāhana too went to the temple for the purpose of worship.
He saw the young girl of divine limbs, adorned with all ornaments.

3.2.s:
tasyā darśanamātreṇa kāmabāṇena pīḍitaḥ ..
manasā kāmadevaṃ taṃ tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
तस्या दर्शनमात्रेण कामबाणेन पीडितः ॥
मनसा कामदेवं तं तुष्टाव श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
Merely upon seeing her, he was tormented by the arrow of Kāma.
In his mind, he praised Kāmadeva with a gentle voice:

3.2.s:
jīmūtavāhana uvāca .. ..
madanāya namastubhyaṃ kṛṣṇaputrāya te namaḥ ..
śaṃbaraprāṇahaṃtre ca caturvyūhāya te namaḥ .. .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
जीमूतवाहन उवाच ॥ ॥
मदनाय नमस्तुभ्यं कृष्णपुत्राय ते नमः ॥
शंबरप्राणहंत्रे च चतुर्व्यूहाय ते नमः ॥ ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m:
Jīmūtavāhana said:
"Homage to you, O Madana, homage to you, the son of Kṛṣṇa,
slayer of the life of Śambara, and consisting of the fourfold manifestation, homage to you!"

3.2.s:
paṃcabāṇāya kāmāya pradyumnāya namonamaḥ ..
madyogyāṃ kuru suśroṇīṃ kāminīṃ kamalānanām .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
पंचबाणाय कामाय प्रद्युम्नाय नमोनमः ॥
मद्योग्यां कुरु सुश्रोणीं कामिनीं कमलाननाम् ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: Homage, homage to Pradyumna, to Kāma who holds the five arrows! / Make this lovely lady with splendid hips and a lotus face suitable for me.

3.2.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavānmakaradhvajadevatā ..
mohayitvā ca pitaraṃ tadvivāhamakārayat .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्मकरध्वजदेवता ॥
मोहयित्वा च पितरं तद्विवाहमकारयत् ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: Then the blessed deity whose emblem is the makara was pleased, / and bewitching her father, he caused their marriage to take place.

3.2.s:
viśvāvasuriti khyātastasya bhūpasya vai sutaḥ ..
bhaginīpatinā sārddhaṃ sa yayau gaṃdhamādanam .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
विश्वावसुरिति ख्यातस्तस्य भूपस्य वै सुतः ॥
भगिनीपतिना सार्द्धं स ययौ गंधमादनम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: The son of that king, renowned as Viśvāvasu, / went to Gandhamādana together with his sister's husband.

3.2.s:
naraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ natvā garuḍottuṃgamāyayau ..
tadā nāgasya vai mātā śaṃkhacūḍasya bho nṛpa ..27..
3.2.d:
नरं नारायणं नत्वा गरुडोत्तुंगमाययौ ॥
तदा नागस्य वै माता शंखचूडस्य भो नृप ॥27॥
3.2.m: Having bowed to Nara and Nārāyaṇa, he came to Garuḍa's Peak. / Then the mother of the serpent Śaṅkhacūḍa, O king,

3.2.s:
ruroda bahudhā tatra yatra jīmūtavāhanaḥ..
duḥkhitaḥ sa jagāmāśu dayālurdīnavatsalaḥ .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
रुरोद बहुधा तत्र यत्र जीमूतवाहनः॥
दुःखितः स जगामाशु दयालुर्दीनवत्सलः ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: wept profusely there, where Jīmūtavāhana was. / Afflicted with grief, he, compassionate and kind to the distressed, went quickly.

3.2.s:
vṛddhāmāśvāsya papraccha kenedaṃ duḥkhamāgatam ..
sāha me tanayo deva garuḍāsye gamiṣyati .. .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
वृद्धामाश्वास्य पप्रच्छ केनेदं दुःखमागतम् ॥
साह मे तनयो देव गरुडास्ये गमिष्यति ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: Comforting the old woman, he asked: “Whence has this sorrow come?” / She said: “My lord, my son will enter Garuḍa's mouth.

3.2.s:
tadviyogena duḥkhārtā vilapāmi mahākulā ..
iti jñātvā sa nṛpatirgaruḍottuṃgamāyayau .. 3.2.15.30 ..
3.2.d:
तद्वियोगेन दुःखार्ता विलपामि महाकुला ॥
इति ज्ञात्वा स नृपतिर्गरुडोत्तुंगमाययौ ॥ 3.2.15.30 ॥
3.2.m: Pained by grief at separation from him, I lament in great agony.” / Knowing this, the king went to Garuḍa's Peak.

3.2.s:
garuḍo'pi gṛhītvā taṃ nabhomārgamupāgamat ..
tasyāṃgado'sṛjā lipto nyadhāttattatra bhāminī .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
गरुडोऽपि गृहीत्वा तं नभोमार्गमुपागमत् ॥
तस्यांगदोऽसृजा लिप्तो न्यधात्तत्तत्र भामिनी ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: Garuḍa seized him and went along the path of the sky. / His armlet, smeared with blood, fell there, and the lovely lady picked it up.

3.2.s:
kamalākṣī tu viyati sthitaṃ garuḍabhakṣitam ..
vilokya cārudadgāḍhaṃ patiduḥkhena duḥkhitā .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
कमलाक्षी तु वियति स्थितं गरुडभक्षितम् ॥
विलोक्य चारुदद्गाढं पतिदुःखेन दुःखिता ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: Beholding him standing in the sky being devoured by Garuḍa, / the lotus-eyed woman wept bitterly, pained by sorrow for her husband.

3.2.s:
tadā tu garuḍastrastastatrāgatya tvarānvitaḥ ..
jīmūtavāhanaṃ prāha kasmāttvaṃ mama bhakṣitaḥ .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
तदा तु गरुडस्त्रस्तस्तत्रागत्य त्वरान्वितः ॥
जीमूतवाहनं प्राह कस्मात्त्वं मम भक्षितः ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: Then Garuḍa, alarmed, swiftly approached that place / and said to Jīmūtavāhana: “Why are you being devoured by me?”

3.2.s:
sa hovāca prabho medya vacaḥ śṛṇu mahāmate ..
śaṃkhacūḍasya jananī mahāduḥkhena duḥkhitā .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
स होवाच प्रभो मेद्य वचः शृणु महामते ॥
शंखचूडस्य जननी महादुःखेन दुःखिता ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: He said: “O lord, listen today to my words, O wise one! / The mother of Śaṅkhacūḍa was pained by great sorrow.

3.2.s:
tasyāḥ putrasya rakṣārthaṃ saṃprāpto'haṃ tavāṃtikam ..
ityukte sati bhūpāla śaṃkhacūḍaśca pannagaḥ .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
तस्याः पुत्रस्य रक्षार्थं संप्राप्तोऽहं तवांतिकम् ॥
इत्युक्ते सति भूपाल शंखचूडश्च पन्नगः ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: I came to your presence to protect her son.” / When this was spoken, O ruler of the earth, the serpent Śaṅkhacūḍa,

3.2.s:
tadvyālasyaiva duḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ śatrumāptavān ..
māṃ prabhakṣa kṛpāsiṃdho tvadāhārārthamāgatam .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
तद्व्यालस्यैव दुःखेन दुःखितः शत्रुमाप्तवान् ॥
मां प्रभक्ष कृपासिंधो त्वदाहारार्थमागतम् ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m: pained by the grief of that very snake, approached his enemy [and said]: / “Devour me, O ocean of mercy, who have arrived for your food!

3.2.s:
saṃtyajya mānuṣaṃ divyaṃ kurvāhāraṃ mahāmate ..
tadā prasanno garuḍo dadau tasmai varatrayam ..37 ..
3.2.d:
संत्यज्य मानुषं दिव्यं कुर्वाहारं महामते ॥
तदा प्रसन्नो गरुडो ददौ तस्मै वरत्रयम् ॥37 ॥
3.2.m: Leave this celestial man and take your meal, O wise one!” / Then Garuḍa, pleased, granted three boons to him,

3.2.s:
jīmūtavāhanāyaiva vidyādharasutāya ca ..
śaṃkhacūḍakulaṃ nāhaṃ bhakṣayiṣye kadā cana .. 38 ..
3.2.d:
जीमूतवाहनायैव विद्याधरसुताय च ॥
शंखचूडकुलं नाहं भक्षयिष्ये कदा चन ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: to Jīmūtavāhana, the son of the Vidyādhara: / “Never shall I devour the family of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

3.2.s:
tvaṃ tu vidyādharapure prāpya rājyaṃ mahottamam ..
subhojayitvā lakṣābdaṃ tato vaikuṇṭhameṣyasi .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
त्वं तु विद्याधरपुरे प्राप्य राज्यं महोत्तमम् ॥
सुभोजयित्वा लक्षाब्दं ततो वैकुण्ठमेष्यसि ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m: You, having attained a supreme kingdom in the city of the Vidyādharas, / having enjoyed it well for a hundred thousand years, will then go to Vaikuṇṭha.”

3.2.s:
ityuktvāntardadhau devaḥ sa pitrā rājyamāptavān ..
svapatnyā saha rājyāṃgaṃ bhuktvā vaikuṃṭhamāyayau .. 3.2.15.40 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधौ देवः स पित्रा राज्यमाप्तवान् ॥
स्वपत्न्या सह राज्यांगं भुक्त्वा वैकुंठमाययौ ॥ 3.2.15.40 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, the deity vanished. He received the kingdom from his father, / and having enjoyed the kingdom together with his wife, he went to Vaikuṇṭha.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo nṛpatiṃ prāha namradhīḥ ..
teṣāṃ madhye mahārāja kasya prāptaṃ mahāphalam .. 41 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो नृपतिं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥
तेषां मध्ये महाराज कस्य प्राप्तं महाफलम् ॥ 41 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, the vetāla with humble mind said to the king: / “Among them, O great king, who obtained the great fruit?”

3.2.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
śaṃkhacūḍasya saṃprāptaṃ jīvadānamahāphalam ..
nṛpasyaivopakāraṃ ca svabhāvo vidhinā kṛtaḥ .. 42 ..
3.2.d:
॥ राजोवाच ॥ ॥
शंखचूडस्य संप्राप्तं जीवदानमहाफलम् ॥
नृपस्यैवोपकारं च स्वभावो विधिना कृतः ॥ 42 ॥
3.2.m: The king said: / “The great fruit of the gift of life was obtained by Śaṅkhacūḍa. / Assisting others was the king's very nature, made by destiny.

3.2.s:
pativratāprabhāvena jīvadānena bhūpateḥ ..
santuṣṭo garuḍo jātastasya kiṃ tarhi tatphalam .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
पतिव्रताप्रभावेन जीवदानेन भूपतेः ॥
सन्तुष्टो गरुडो जातस्तस्य किं तर्हि तत्फलम् ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m: Through the power of the devoted wife and through the king’s gift of life, / Garuḍa was satisfied; so what fruit was that to him?

3.2.s:
nirbhayaḥ śaṃkhacūḍastu svaśatruṃ prati cāgamat ..
śarīramarpayitvā taṃ tataḥ prāptaṃ mahāphalam .. 44 ..
tulanīya - kathāsaritsāgare vetālapaṃcaviṃśati
jīmūtavāhanopari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
निर्भयः शंखचूडस्तु स्वशत्रुं प्रति चागमत् ॥
शरीरमर्पयित्वा तं ततः प्राप्तं महाफलम् ॥ 44 ॥
तुलनीय - कथासरित्सागरे वेतालपंचविंशति
जीमूतवाहनोपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
Śaṅkhacūḍa, however, went without fear before his own enemy / and offered his body to him; therefore he obtained the great fruit.”
Compare: The Vetālapañcaviṃśati in the Kathāsaritsāgara.
Note on Jīmūtavāhana.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
punaḥ prāha sa vaitālo bhūpatiṃ jñānakovidam ..
caṃdraśekharabhūpasya nagarī dakṣiṇe sthitā .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
पुनः प्राह स वैतालो भूपतिं ज्ञानकोविदम् ॥
चंद्रशेखरभूपस्य नगरी दक्षिणे स्थिता ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Again that vetāla spoke to the king who was skilled in knowledge: / “The city of King Candraśekhara stood in the south.

3.2.s:
ratnadattovasadvaiśyo dharmajño dhanadhānyavān..
kāmāvarūthinī tasya sutā jātā mahottamā .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
रत्नदत्तोवसद्वैश्यो धर्मज्ञो धनधान्यवान्॥
कामावरूथिनी तस्य सुता जाता महोत्तमा ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: A vaiśya named Ratnadatta lived there, righteous and endowed with wealth and grain. / A daughter named Kāmāvarūthinī was born to him, exceedingly excellent.

3.2.s:
tadrūpamuttamaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vaiśyo bhūpatiṃ prati ..
uvāca bho mahārāja sutā mama surepsitā .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
तद्रूपमुत्तमं दृष्ट्वा स वैश्यो भूपतिं प्रति ॥
उवाच भो महाराज सुता मम सुरेप्सिता ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: Seeing her excellent beauty, that vaiśya said to the king: / ‘O great king, my daughter is desired by the gods.

3.2.s:
tāṃ gṛhāṇa kṛpāsiṃdho tvadyogyā vidhinirmitā ..
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ bhūpatiścaṃdraśekharaḥ... .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
तां गृहाण कृपासिंधो त्वद्योग्या विधिनिर्मिता ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं भूपतिश्चंद्रशेखरः॥॥। 4 ॥
3.2.m: Take her, O ocean of mercy; she was fashioned by destiny as worthy of you.’ / Having heard these words, King Candraśekhara

3.2.s:
maṃtriṇaṃ viduraṃ prāha tvaṃ ca gaccha mahāmate ..
yathāyogyaṃ hi tadrūpaṃ māṃ nivedaya satvaram .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
मंत्रिणं विदुरं प्राह त्वं च गच्छ महामते ॥
यथायोग्यं हि तद्रूपं मां निवेदय सत्वरम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: said to his minister Vidura: ‘Go, O wise one, / and report to me quickly whether her form is truly suitable.’

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa yayau gehaṃ bhūpatiścaṃdraśekharaḥ.
śyāmalā nāma tatpatnī jñātvā rājānamāgatam..6..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स ययौ गेहं भूपतिश्चंद्रशेखरः।
श्यामला नाम तत्पत्नी ज्ञात्वा राजानमागतम्॥6॥
3.2.m: Having said this, King Candraśekhara went home. / His wife named Śyāmalā, knowing that the king had arrived,

3.2.s:
dhūpadīpādibhiḥ puṣpairyathāyogyaiḥ samārcayat ..
etasminneva kāle tu gauśca śārdūlapīḍitā..7..
3.2.d:
धूपदीपादिभिः पुष्पैर्यथायोग्यैः समार्चयत् ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु गौश्च शार्दूलपीडिता॥7॥
3.2.m: worshipped him appropriately with incense, lamps, and flowers. / Just at that time, a cow, tormented by a tiger,

3.2.s:
haṃbhāśabdena mahatā vilalāpa bhayāturā ..
tacchrutvā sa tu bhūpālaḥ khaḍgahastaḥ samabhyagāt .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
हंभाशब्देन महता विललाप भयातुरा ॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा स तु भूपालः खड्गहस्तः समभ्यगात् ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: bellowed loudly, crying out in terror. / Hearing that, the king went forward, sword in hand.

3.2.s:
śīghraṃ hatvā tu śārdūlaṃ mumoda nṛpatistadā ..
mukulo dānavo nāma taddehādrūpamāptavān ..9..
3.2.d:
शीघ्रं हत्वा तु शार्दूलं मुमोद नृपतिस्तदा ॥
मुकुलो दानवो नाम तद्देहाद्रूपमाप्तवान् ॥9॥
3.2.m: Quickly killing the tiger, the king then rejoiced. / A dānava named Mukula regained his form from that body.

3.2.s:
bhūpatiṃ prāha namrātmā dharmajñaṃ caṃdraśekharam ..
tvayā vimocito nātha yāsyāmi varuṇālayam ..1 0..
3.2.d:
भूपतिं प्राह नम्रात्मा धर्मज्ञं चंद्रशेखरम् ॥
त्वया विमोचितो नाथ यास्यामि वरुणालयम् ॥1 0॥
3.2.m: He, bowing his self, said to the righteous King Candraśekhara: / ‘Freed by you, O lord, I shall go to the realm of Varuṇa.

3.2.s:
prahrādasyaiva śāpena vyāghradehatvamāgataḥ ..
parikramya yayau daityaḥ prahlādaṃ prati satvaraḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
प्रह्रादस्यैव शापेन व्याघ्रदेहत्वमागतः ॥
परिक्रम्य ययौ दैत्यः प्रह्लादं प्रति सत्वरः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: Through the curse of Prahrāda I had attained the body of a tiger.’ / Having circumambulated [him], the daitya went quickly towards Prahlāda.

3.2.s:
nṛpatirgṛhamāgatya suṣvāpa parayā mudā ..
prabhāte bodhito rājā sabhāyāṃ svayamāgamat .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
नृपतिर्गृहमागत्य सुष्वाप परया मुदा ॥
प्रभाते बोधितो राजा सभायां स्वयमागमत् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: The king, having returned home, slept with great joy. / Awakened at dawn, the king himself came to the assembly hall.

3.2.s:
nṛpoktaḥ sa yayau tatra yatra kāmāvarūthinī ..
divyamūrtimayīṃ dṛṣṭvāciṃtayatsa svamānase .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
नृपोक्तः स ययौ तत्र यत्र कामावरूथिनी ॥
दिव्यमूर्तिमयीं दृष्ट्वाचिंतयत्स स्वमानसे ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Ordered by the king, he went where Kāmāvarūthinī was. / Seeing her celestial form, he thought in his mind:

3.2.s:
asyā mūrtiprabhāvena rājāsau mohamāpsyati..
iti jñātvā nṛpaṃ prāha saiva tvadyogyakā na hi..14..
3.2.d:
अस्या मूर्तिप्रभावेन राजासौ मोहमाप्स्यति॥
इति ज्ञात्वा नृपं प्राह सैव त्वद्योग्यका न हि॥14॥
3.2.m: ‘By the power of her form, this king will fall into delusion.’ / Deciding thus, he told the king: ‘She is not suitable for you.’

3.2.s:
tathā matvā sa nṛpatirna vivāhamathākarot..
ratnadattasya bhūpasya senāyāḥ pataye dadau .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
तथा मत्वा स नृपतिर्न विवाहमथाकरोत्॥
रत्नदत्तस्य भूपस्य सेनायाः पतये ददौ ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Thinking it to be so, the king did not marry her. / Ratnadatta gave her to the commander of the king's army.

3.2.s:
balabhadrasya sā patnī babhūva varavarṇinī ..
ekadā nṛpatistāṃ vai dṛṣṭvā kāmāvatharūthinīm .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
बलभद्रस्य सा पत्नी बभूव वरवर्णिनी ॥
एकदा नृपतिस्तां वै दृष्ट्वा कामावथरूथिनीम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: The fair-complexioned lady became the wife of Balabhadra. / Once the king saw that Kāmāvarūthinī,

3.2.s:
mohitaḥ kāmabāṇena mūrcchitaḥ patito bhuvi ..
tadā senāpatistūrṇaṃ nṛpamutthāpya satvaram .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
मोहितः कामबाणेन मूर्च्छितः पतितो भुवि ॥
तदा सेनापतिस्तूर्णं नृपमुत्थाप्य सत्वरम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: and struck by the arrows of Kāma, he fainted and fell to the ground. / Then the army commander swiftly raised the king,

3.2.s:
śibikāṃ caiva saṃsthāpya sabhāyāṃ ca samairayat ..
tadā prabuddho nṛpatiḥ prāha senāpatiṃ mudā .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
शिबिकां चैव संस्थाप्य सभायां च समैरयत् ॥
तदा प्रबुद्धो नृपतिः प्राह सेनापतिं मुदा ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: placed him in a palanquin, and brought him to the assembly hall. / Then the awakened king joyfully said to the army commander:

3.2.s:
kasyeyaṃ sundarī bhāryā kuto jātā mahottamā ..
balabhadrastu tacchrutvā nṛpatiṃ prāha namradhīḥ .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
कस्येयं सुन्दरी भार्या कुतो जाता महोत्तमा ॥
बलभद्रस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: ‘Whose beautiful wife is this? Whence was this most excellent lady born?’ / Hearing that, Balabhadra, with humble mind, said to the king:

3.2.s:
mameyaṃ sundarī nārī ratnadattasya sā sutā ..
rājyabhaṃgabhayānmantrī na rūpaṃ tvayi varṇivān .. 20 ..
3.2.d:
ममेयं सुन्दरी नारी रत्नदत्तस्य सा सुता ॥
राज्यभंगभयान्मन्त्री न रूपं त्वयि वर्णिवान् ॥ 20 ॥
3.2.m: ‘This beautiful woman is mine, the daughter of Ratnadatta. / Fearing the ruin of the kingdom, the minister did not describe her beauty to you.

3.2.s:
mama dāsasya yā patnī tvadyogyā bhūpate sadā ..
tavecchāṃ pūrayiṣyāmi tāṃ gṛhāṇa kṛpānidhe .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
मम दासस्य या पत्नी त्वद्योग्या भूपते सदा ॥
तवेच्छां पूरयिष्यामि तां गृहाण कृपानिधे ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: She who is the wife of me, your servant, is ever worthy of you, O ruler of the earth. / I will fulfill your desire; take her, O treasure of mercy!’

3.2.s:
ityuktaḥ krodhatāmrākṣo bhūpatistamuvāca ha ..
taveyaṃ dharmato bhāryā prāptā sundararūpiṇī .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्तः क्रोधताम्राक्षो भूपतिस्तमुवाच ह ॥
तवेयं धर्मतो भार्या प्राप्ता सुन्दररूपिणी ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
Having been addressed thus, the king, his eyes copper-red with anger, said to him:
“According to dharma, she was obtained by you as your wife, she of lovely form.

3.2.s:
gṛhṇāmi yadi tāṃ devīṃ narake yamakiṃkarāḥ ..
pātayitvā mahāduḥkhaṃ bhajayiṣyanti tarhi bhoḥ .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
गृह्णामि यदि तां देवीं नरके यमकिंकराः ॥
पातयित्वा महादुःखं भजयिष्यन्ति तर्हि भोः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m:
If I accept that lady, then, O man, the servants of Yama,
having cast [me] into hell, will make me suffer great torment.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā bhūpatistūrṇaṃ virahāgniprapīḍitaḥ ..
maraṇaṃ prāptavānrājā gato dharmapurāṃtike .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भूपतिस्तूर्णं विरहाग्निप्रपीडितः ॥
मरणं प्राप्तवान्राजा गतो धर्मपुरांतिके ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m:
Having spoken thus, the king, tormented by the fire of separation, quickly
met his death and went near the city of Dharma.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo nṛpaṃ prāha śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ ..
mṛte rājani tatpatnī satī bhūtvā pradṛśyate ..25..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो नृपं प्राह शृणुष्व भोः ॥
मृते राजनि तत्पत्नी सती भूत्वा प्रदृश्यते ॥25॥
3.2.m:
Having said this, that vetāla said to the king: “Listen, O man!
When the king died, his wife was seen becoming a satī.

3.2.s:
senāpatistu tatraiva bhasmasādabhavatkṣaṇāt ..
kāmāvarūthinī devī bhasma kṛtvā kalevaram ..26..
3.2.d:
सेनापतिस्तु तत्रैव भस्मसादभवत्क्षणात् ॥
कामावरूथिनी देवी भस्म कृत्वा कलेवरम् ॥26॥
3.2.m:
And the commander-in-chief was reduced to ashes in an instant on that very spot.
The lady Kāmāvarūthinī, having turned her body to ashes,

3.2.s:
svargaṃ gatāstu te sarve kasya puṇyādhikaṃ matam ..
sa hovāca ca vaitālaṃ rājā dharmādhiko mataḥ ..27 ..
3.2.d:
स्वर्गं गतास्तु ते सर्वे कस्य पुण्याधिकं मतम् ॥
स होवाच च वैतालं राजा धर्माधिको मतः ॥27 ॥
3.2.m:
they all went to heaven. Whose merit is considered greater?”
And he said to the vetāla: “The king is considered greater in dharma.

3.2.s:
maraṇaṃ kiṃkarasyaiva yogyaṃ bhūpatihetave ..
pativratāyā maraṇaṃ patisaṃgena yogyakam .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
मरणं किंकरस्यैव योग्यं भूपतिहेतवे ॥
पतिव्रताया मरणं पतिसंगेन योग्यकम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m:
Death is indeed fitting for a servant for the sake of his king;
death is fitting for a devoted wife by accompanying her husband.

3.2.s:
dattā yatkiṃkareṇaiva suṃdarī nṛpahetave ..
dharmabhītyā na nṛpatistāmagṛhṇātsa kāmukaḥ .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
दत्ता यत्किंकरेणैव सुंदरी नृपहेतवे ॥
धर्मभीत्या न नृपतिस्तामगृह्णात्स कामुकः ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m:
Though the beautiful woman was given by the servant for the sake of the king,
the king, though lovesick, did not accept her out of fear of violating dharma.

3.2.s:
jitvā kāmaṃ tathā pālyaṃ dharmaṃ tasmānnṛpe'dhikam .. 30 .. ..
tulanīya - kathāsaritsāgare vetālapaṃcaviṃśati
mukulopari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
जित्वा कामं तथा पाल्यं धर्मं तस्मान्नृपेऽधिकम् ॥ 30 ॥ ॥
तुलनीय - कथासरित्सागरे वेतालपंचविंशति
मुकुलोपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
Having conquered passion, dharma was thus protected; therefore [the merit] is greater in the king.”
Comparable to the Vetālapañcaviṃśati in the Kathāsaritsāgara.
Note on Mukula.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
punaḥ provāca vetālastadā brāhmaṇarūpavān ..
śṛṇu bhūpa mahābhāga kathāṃ tava manoramām .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
पुनः प्रोवाच वेतालस्तदा ब्राह्मणरूपवान् ॥
शृणु भूप महाभाग कथां तव मनोरमाम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
Then the vetāla, having assumed the form of a brāhmaṇa, spoke again:
“Hear, O highly fortunate king, a delightful tale for you.

3.2.s:
ujjayinyāṃ mahābhāga mahāseno nṛpo'bhavet ..
tasya rājye'vasadvipro devaśarmeti viśrutaḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
उज्जयिन्यां महाभाग महासेनो नृपोऽभवेत् ॥
तस्य राज्येऽवसद्विप्रो देवशर्मेति विश्रुतः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m:
In Ujjayinī, O highly fortunate one, there was a king named Mahāsena.
In his kingdom lived a brāhmaṇa known as Devaśarman.

3.2.s:
guṇākarastasya suto madyamāṃsaparāyaṇaḥ ..
dyūtena saṃkṣayaṃ vittaṃ tasya pāpasya cābhavat .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
गुणाकरस्तस्य सुतो मद्यमांसपरायणः ॥
द्यूतेन संक्षयं वित्तं तस्य पापस्य चाभवत् ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m:
His son was Guṇākara, addicted to liquor and meat;
and through gambling, the wealth of that wicked man was destroyed.

3.2.s:
bāṃdhavaiḥ sa parityakto babhrāma vasudhātale ..
kadāciddaivayogena siddhāśramamupāgamat .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
बांधवैः स परित्यक्तो बभ्राम वसुधातले ॥
कदाचिद्दैवयोगेन सिद्धाश्रममुपागमत् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m:
Abandoned by his kinsmen, he wandered over the surface of the earth.
Once, by the turn of fate, he arrived at Siddhāśrama.

3.2.s:
kapardī nāma taṃ yogī kapālānnairapūjayat ..
jñātvā paiśācamannaṃ sa bubhukṣurna gṛhītavān .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
कपर्दी नाम तं योगी कपालान्नैरपूजयत् ॥
ज्ञात्वा पैशाचमन्नं स बुभुक्षुर्न गृहीतवान् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
A yogin named Kapardī honored him with food from a skull.
Recognizing it as piśāca-like food, he, though hungry, did not accept it.

3.2.s:
tadātithyaṃ tadarthaṃ sa yakṣiṇīṃ samupāhvayat ..
tayā rātrau mahānandaṃ prāptavānsa dvijaḥ śayī .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
तदातिथ्यं तदर्थं स यक्षिणीं समुपाह्वयत् ॥
तया रात्रौ महानन्दं प्राप्तवान्स द्विजः शयी ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
Then, for that hospitality, for his sake, he summoned a yakṣiṇī.
Lying down at night, that twice-born attained great bliss with her.

3.2.s:
prātaḥ kāle tu saṃprāpte kailāsaṃ yakṣiṇī gatā ..
sa dvijastadviyogena yogyaṃtikamupāyayau .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
प्रातः काले तु संप्राप्ते कैलासं यक्षिणी गता ॥
स द्विजस्तद्वियोगेन योग्यंतिकमुपाययौ ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m:
When morning arrived, the yakṣiṇī went to Kailāsa.
Due to separation from her, that twice-born went near the yogin.

3.2.s:
kapardī pradadau tasmai vidyāṃ yakṣiṇikarṣiṇīm ..
catvāriṃśaddinānyeva niśīthe jalamadhyagaḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
कपर्दी प्रददौ तस्मै विद्यां यक्षिणिकर्षिणीम् ॥
चत्वारिंशद्दिनान्येव निशीथे जलमध्यगः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m:
Kapardī gave him the spell that attracts a yakṣiṇī.
For forty days, standing in the middle of water at midnight,

3.2.s:
sa jajāpa śubhaṃ mantraṃ na prāptā kāmacāriṇī ..
tadā yogyājñayā vipraḥ svayaṃ tu mamatāṃ tyajan .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
स जजाप शुभं मन्त्रं न प्राप्ता कामचारिणी ॥
तदा योग्याज्ञया विप्रः स्वयं तु ममतां त्यजन् ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m:
he chanted the auspicious mantra, but she who moves at will was not attained.
Then, by the command of the yogin, the brāhmaṇa, abandoning his attachment,

3.2.s: prāptavānpitarau natvā svagehe nivasanniśi .. 3.2.17.10..
3.2.d: प्राप्तवान्पितरौ नत्वा स्वगेहे निवसन्निशि ॥ 3.2.17.10॥
3.2.m: went home, bowed to his parents, and lived in his own house at night.

3.2.s:
pratibodhivanaṃ prāptastacchiṣyatvamupāyayau ..
pañcāgnimadhye sa sthitvā tanmaṃtramajapacchuciḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
प्रतिबोधिवनं प्राप्तस्तच्छिष्यत्वमुपाययौ ॥
पञ्चाग्निमध्ये स स्थित्वा तन्मंत्रमजपच्छुचिः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m:
Having reached the Pratibodhi forest, he became his disciple.
Standing amidst the five fires, purified, he chanted that mantra.

3.2.s:
na prāptā yoginī devī tadā cintāturo 'bhavat ..
ityuktvā sa vaitālo nṛpatiṃ jñānakovidam .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
न प्राप्ता योगिनी देवी तदा चिन्तातुरो ऽभवत् ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स वैतालो नृपतिं ज्ञानकोविदम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
The divine yoginī was not attained; then he became afflicted with anxiety.”
Having said this, that vetāla said to the king, who was skilled in knowledge:

3.2.s:
punarāha kathaṃ devī na prāptā yakṣiṇī priyā ..
śrutvāha nṛpatirvipra vaitālaṃ rudra kiṃkaram .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
पुनराह कथं देवी न प्राप्ता यक्षिणी प्रिया ॥
श्रुत्वाह नृपतिर्विप्र वैतालं रुद्र किंकरम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m:
He spoke again: “Why was the divine yakṣiṇī, his beloved, not attained?”
Having heard, the king, a brāhmaṇa, said to the vetāla, the servant of Rudra:

3.2.s:
trividhaṃ karma bho vipra siddhyarthe sādhakāya vai ..
manovāgvihitaṃ karma paraloke sukhapradam .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
त्रिविधं कर्म भो विप्र सिद्ध्यर्थे साधकाय वै ॥
मनोवाग्विहितं कर्म परलोके सुखप्रदम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m:
“Action is threefold, O brāhmaṇa, for an adept to attain success.
Action performed through mind and speech grants happiness in the other world.

3.2.s:
sundarāṃgakṛtaṃ jñeyaṃ punarvākkāyasaṃbhavam ..
kiñcitsiddhipradaṃ jñeyamiha janmani vīkṣitam .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
सुन्दरांगकृतं ज्ञेयं पुनर्वाक्कायसंभवम् ॥
किञ्चित्सिद्धिप्रदं ज्ञेयमिह जन्मनि वीक्षितम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m:
It should be known as accomplished by the handsome body; moreover, that produced by speech and body
is known to bestow slight success, seen in this very birth.

3.2.s:
paratra ca bhuvarloke piṇḍadehakṛtaṃ smṛtam ..
manaḥkāyena saṃbhūtaṃ para janmani rājyadam .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
परत्र च भुवर्लोके पिण्डदेहकृतं स्मृतम् ॥
मनःकायेन संभूतं पर जन्मनि राज्यदम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m:
In the other world, in Bhuvarloka, it is remembered as accomplished by the physical body.
That which arises from mind and body bestows a kingdom in another birth.

3.2.s:
manovākkāyasaṃbhūtamiha janmani siddhidam ..
paratra paramāṃ siddhiṃ tatkarma pradadāti hi .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
मनोवाक्कायसंभूतमिह जन्मनि सिद्धिदम् ॥
परत्र परमां सिद्धिं तत्कर्म प्रददाति हि ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m:
That which arises from mind, speech, and body grants success in this birth;
indeed, that action grants supreme perfection in the other world.

3.2.s:
tasmātkartavyameveha trividhaṃ karma sādhakaiḥ ..
anyavitttena sa dvijaḥ kṛtavānkarma mantrajam ..
ato'nyajanmani prāpto yakṣatvaṃ tatparo dvijaḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मात्कर्तव्यमेवेह त्रिविधं कर्म साधकैः ॥
अन्यवित्त्तेन स द्विजः कृतवान्कर्म मन्त्रजम् ॥
अतोऽन्यजन्मनि प्राप्तो यक्षत्वं तत्परो द्विजः ॥ 18 ॥

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālaḥ prasannavadano'bhavat .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालः प्रसन्नवदनोऽभवत् ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
When he had said this, that vetāla became pleased in countenance.

3.2.s:
sādhu sādhviti taṃ procya sadvākyaiḥ samapūjayat ..
itihāsaṃ punaḥ prāha parīkṣārthe nṛpāya saḥ .. 3.2.17.20 .. ..
tulanīya - kathāsaritsāgare vetālapaṃcaviṃśati
yakṣiṇyopari ṭippaṇī
yakṣiṇīsādhana mantrāḥ
kapardyupari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
साधु साध्विति तं प्रोच्य सद्वाक्यैः समपूजयत् ॥
इतिहासं पुनः प्राह परीक्षार्थे नृपाय सः ॥ 3.2.17.20 ॥ ॥
तुलनीय - कथासरित्सागरे वेतालपंचविंशति
यक्षिण्योपरि टिप्पणी
यक्षिणीसाधन मन्त्राः
कपर्द्युपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
Saying to him, “Well done! Well done!”, he honored him with pleasant words.
He told another story to the king in order to test him.
Comparable to the Vetālapañcaviṃśati in the Kathāsaritsāgara.
Note on the Yakṣiṇī.
Mantras for the propitiation of a yakṣiṇī.
Note on Kapardī.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
bhoḥ śaunaka mahāprājña vaitālastaṃ hi so'bravīt ..
sudakṣo nāma nṛpatirvasankaṃbalake pure .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
भोः शौनक महाप्राज्ञ वैतालस्तं हि सोऽब्रवीत् ॥
सुदक्षो नाम नृपतिर्वसन्कंबलके पुरे ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
“O Śaunaka of great wisdom, the vetāla indeed said to him:
There was a king named Sudakṣa residing in the city of Kambalaka,

3.2.s:
nyāyavāndharmavāñchūro dātā śivaparāyaṇaḥ ..
tasya rājye'vasadvaiśyo dhanādhyakṣa iti śrutaḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
न्यायवान्धर्मवाञ्छूरो दाता शिवपरायणः ॥
तस्य राज्येऽवसद्वैश्यो धनाध्यक्ष इति श्रुतः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m:
just, righteous, heroic, generous, and devoted to Śiva.
In his kingdom lived a vaiśya known as Dhanādhyakṣa.

3.2.s:
tanayā sundarī tasya nāmnā dhanavatī śubhā ..
gaurīdattāya vaiśyāya pitrā dattā varāṃganā .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
तनया सुन्दरी तस्य नाम्ना धनवती शुभा ॥
गौरीदत्ताय वैश्याय पित्रा दत्ता वरांगना ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m:
He had an auspicious and lovely daughter named Dhanavatī;
that excellent woman was given by her father to the vaiśya Gaurīdatta.

3.2.s:
kiyatā caiva kālena mohinī tatsutābhavat ..
dvādaśābdavayastasyāḥ pitā tu nidhanaṃ gataḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
कियता चैव कालेन मोहिनी तत्सुताभवत् ॥
द्वादशाब्दवयस्तस्याः पिता तु निधनं गतः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m:
After some time, Mohinī became their daughter.
When she was twelve years of age, her father passed away.

3.2.s:
tadā dhanavatī raṃḍā nidhanā pituraṃtike ..
kanyayā saha saṃprāptā niśi mārge tamomaye .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
तदा धनवती रंडा निधना पितुरंतिके ॥
कन्यया सह संप्राप्ता निशि मार्गे तमोमये ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
Then the widowed Dhanavatī, destitute, went to her father
along with her maiden daughter, at night on a dark path.

3.2.s:
nyāyaśarmā dvijaḥ kaścidbrahmasvasyāpahārakaḥ ..
nāmasatyatvabhāvena śūlyāṃ na nidhanaṃ gataḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
न्यायशर्मा द्विजः कश्चिद्ब्रह्मस्वस्यापहारकः ॥
नामसत्यत्वभावेन शूल्यां न निधनं गतः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
A certain twice-born named Nyāyaśarman, who had stolen brāhmaṇa property,
did not die on the stake because of the truthfulness of his name.

3.2.s:
akasmādvaiśyajā prāptā tatkaraṃ sā tadāspṛśat ..
tena duḥkhena mahatā rurodo ccairdvijaśca saḥ ..7..
3.2.d:
अकस्माद्वैश्यजा प्राप्ता तत्करं सा तदास्पृशत् ॥
तेन दुःखेन महता रुरोदो च्चैर्द्विजश्च सः ॥7॥
3.2.m:
Suddenly the vaiśya woman arrived and then touched his hand.
Because of that great pain, that twice-born wept aloud:

3.2.s:
hā rāmakṛṣṇa pradyumnāniruddheti punaḥpunaḥ ..
śrutvā dhanavatī dīnā ko bhavāniti sābravīt ..8..
3.2.d:
हा रामकृष्ण प्रद्युम्नानिरुद्धेति पुनःपुनः ॥
श्रुत्वा धनवती दीना को भवानिति साब्रवीत् ॥8॥
3.2.m:
‘Alas, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha!’ again and again.
Hearing this, the wretched Dhanavatī said: ‘Who are you?’

3.2.s:
dvija āha ca vipro'haṃ tryahaṃ śūlyāṃ nirūpitaḥ ..
yadi dāsyasi me kanyāṃ koṭisvarṇaṃ dadāmi te .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
द्विज आह च विप्रोऽहं त्र्यहं शूल्यां निरूपितः ॥
यदि दास्यसि मे कन्यां कोटिस्वर्णं ददामि ते ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m:
The twice-born said: ‘I am a brāhmaṇa, placed upon the stake for three days.
If you give me your maiden daughter, I will give you a crore of gold.’

3.2.s:
śrutvā dhanavatī tasmā udvāhya mohinīṃ sutām ..
vaṭamūle sthitaṃ dravyaṃ khanitvā gṛhamāyayau .. 3.2.18.10 ..
3.2.d:
श्रुत्वा धनवती तस्मा उद्वाह्य मोहिनीं सुताम् ॥
वटमूले स्थितं द्रव्यं खनित्वा गृहमाययौ ॥ 3.2.18.10 ॥
3.2.m:
Hearing this, Dhanavatī, having given her daughter Mohinī in marriage to him,
dug up the wealth lying at the root of a banyan tree and went home.

3.2.s:
mohinyapi patiṃ prāha bhavānmṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ ..
kuto jāyeta tanayastanme brūhi dayānidhe .. 1 1..
3.2.d:
मोहिन्यपि पतिं प्राह भवान्मृत्युवशं गतः ॥
कुतो जायेत तनयस्तन्मे ब्रूहि दयानिधे ॥ 1 1॥
3.2.m:
Mohinī too said to her husband: ‘You have fallen under the sway of death;
how could a son be born? Tell me that, O treasure of compassion!’”

3.2.s:
dvijaḥ prāha śṛṇu vyaṃge yadā te hṛcchayo bhavet ..
datā tvaṃ paṃḍitaṃ prāpya putramutpādayāśu vai ..12..
3.2.d:
द्विजः प्राह शृणु व्यंगे यदा ते हृच्छयो भवेत् ॥
दता त्वं पंडितं प्राप्य पुत्रमुत्पादयाशु वै ॥12॥
3.2.m: The twice-born said: “Listen, O limbless one! When desire arises in your heart, / you, being given [in marriage], having approached a learned scholar, beget a son at once.”

3.2.s:
ityuktvā maraṇaṃ prāpya yamalokaṃ gato dvijaḥ ..
nārakīṃ yātanāṃ nityaṃ bubhuje niṃdyakarmajām .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मरणं प्राप्य यमलोकं गतो द्विजः ॥
नारकीं यातनां नित्यं बुभुजे निंद्यकर्मजाम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus and met his death, the twice-born went to the realm of Yama. / He constantly endured hellish torment born of his reprehensible deeds.

3.2.s:
māturgṛhe tu sā nārī mohinī yauvanānvitā ..
samayaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā tiṣṭhaṃtī ca punaḥpunaḥ .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
मातुर्गृहे तु सा नारी मोहिनी यौवनान्विता ॥
समयं हृदये कृत्वा तिष्ठंती च पुनःपुनः ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: That woman Mohinī, endowed with youth, [dwelling] in her mother’s house, / kept this agreement in her heart, remaining there continually.

3.2.s:
ke bhogāśca kimāścaryaṃ ko jāgarti śayīta kaḥ ..
pāpo vyādhiśca duḥkhaṃ ca kuto jātaṃ hṛdi sthitam .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
के भोगाश्च किमाश्चर्यं को जागर्ति शयीत कः ॥
पापो व्याधिश्च दुःखं च कुतो जातं हृदि स्थितम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: [She asked:] “What are the pleasures, and what is a wonder? Who is awake, and who should sleep? / Whence are sin, disease, and sorrow, which reside in the heart, born?”

3.2.s:
iti ślokaṃ dvijānāha nottaraṃ ca dadurdvijāḥ ..
medhāvī nāma kāśmīre sthito vipraḥ samāgataḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्लोकं द्विजानाह नोत्तरं च ददुर्द्विजाः ॥
मेधावी नाम काश्मीरे स्थितो विप्रः समागतः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: She recited this verse to the twice-born, but the twice-born gave no answer. / [Then] a brāhmaṇa named Medhāvī, who lived in Kashmir, arrived.

3.2.s:
tāmuvāca prasannātmā śṛṇu mohini suṃdari ..
sugaṃdhi vanitā vastraṃ gītaṃ pānaṃ ca bhojanam ..
śayyā ca bhūṣaṇaṃ jñeyo bhogo hyaṣṭavidho budhaiḥ .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
तामुवाच प्रसन्नात्मा शृणु मोहिनि सुंदरि ॥
सुगंधि वनिता वस्त्रं गीतं पानं च भोजनम् ॥
शय्या च भूषणं ज्ञेयो भोगो ह्यष्टविधो बुधैः ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: Delighted in heart, he said to her: “Listen, O fair Mohinī! / Fragrance, women, clothing, singing, drink, food, / a bed, and ornaments—these eight kinds of pleasure are recognised by the wise.

3.2.s:
ahanyahani bhūtāni mriyante janayanti ca ..
mamatāṃ yaḥ karotyeṣāṃ tadāścaryaṃ smṛtaṃ budhaiḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
अहन्यहनि भूतानि म्रियन्ते जनयन्ति च ॥
ममतां यः करोत्येषां तदाश्चर्यं स्मृतं बुधैः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Day after day beings die and give birth. / Whoever conceives a sense of ownership toward them—that is considered a wonder by the wise.

3.2.s:
yo vivekaṃ samāsādya kurute karmasaṃgraham ..
saṃsāre ghoratamasi sa jāgarti vivekavān.. 19 ..
3.2.d:
यो विवेकं समासाद्य कुरुते कर्मसंग्रहम् ॥
संसारे घोरतमसि स जागर्ति विवेकवान्॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: He who, having attained discernment, performs the accumulation of actions / in this world of terrible darkness—that discerning man is awake.

3.2.s:
saṃsārājagaraṃ jñātvā vairāgyaṃ yo'karodbhuvi ..
audāsīnyaṃ samādhiṃ ca sukhaṃ śete hi mānavaḥ ..3.2.18.20..
3.2.d:
संसाराजगरं ज्ञात्वा वैराग्यं योऽकरोद्भुवि ॥
औदासीन्यं समाधिं च सुखं शेते हि मानवः ॥3.2.18.20॥
3.2.m: Having recognized this worldly existence as a python, whoever on earth practices detachment, / indifference, and meditative absorption—that person indeed sleeps happily.

3.2.s:
saṃkalpājjāyate kāmastato lobhaḥ prajāyate..
lobhājjātaśca tṛṣṇāyāṃ sa pāpo nirayapradaḥ .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
संकल्पाज्जायते कामस्ततो लोभः प्रजायते॥
लोभाज्जातश्च तृष्णायां स पापो निरयप्रदः ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: From desire-intent passion is born; from that, greed is produced. / Born from greed in thirst, that sin leads to hell.

3.2.s:
jalaprakṛtyāṃ yo jāto raso rasavikāravān ..
rasājātasya dehe'sminvyādhiḥ karmamayo'śubhaḥ .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
जलप्रकृत्यां यो जातो रसो रसविकारवान् ॥
रसाजातस्य देहेऽस्मिन्व्याधिः कर्ममयोऽशुभः ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: From the watery nature is born the taste that undergoes bodily transformations. / Born from taste in this body, disease is composed of action and brings misfortune.

3.2.s:
rudrātkālyāṃ samudbhūto moho hṛdi ca lokahā ..
sa tuṣṭāva mahādevīṃ patnyarthe surapūjitām .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
रुद्रात्काल्यां समुद्भूतो मोहो हृदि च लोकहा ॥
स तुष्टाव महादेवीं पत्न्यर्थे सुरपूजिताम् ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: From Rudra in Kālī, delusion, the destroyer of the world, was born in the heart. / He praised the Great Goddess, worshipped by the gods, for the sake of a wife.

3.2.s:
mithyādṛṣṭistato jātā mohasya dayitābhavat..
tasmātsnehaśca tatpatnyāṃ jātaśca mamatāpriyaḥ .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
मिथ्यादृष्टिस्ततो जाता मोहस्य दयिताभवत्॥
तस्मात्स्नेहश्च तत्पत्न्यां जातश्च ममताप्रियः ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: From that arose false view, who became the beloved of Delusion. / From him, affection was born in that wife, as was love of ownership.

3.2.s:
tayoḥ sakāśātsaṃjātaṃ duḥkhaṃ śokasamanvitam ..
iti śrutvā tu sā nārī muhoha varavarṇinī .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
तयोः सकाशात्संजातं दुःखं शोकसमन्वितम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तु सा नारी मुहोह वरवर्णिनी ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: From those two was born sorrow accompanied by grief.” / Having heard this, that fair-complexioned woman was bewildered.

3.2.s:
mānī śūraśca caturo'dhikārī guṇavānsakhā ..
strīrakṣakaśca puruṣo vaśaṃ nārīṃ sadā nayet .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
मानी शूरश्च चतुरोऽधिकारी गुणवान्सखा ॥
स्त्रीरक्षकश्च पुरुषो वशं नारीं सदा नयेत् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: A man who is proud, heroic, clever, in authority, virtuous, friendly, / and a protector of women can always bring a woman under his control.

3.2.s:
tasyai garbhaṃ ca vipro'sau dattvā svarṇaṃ gṛhītavān ..
sāpi nārī sukhaṃ lebhe tena garbheṇa pratyaham .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
तस्यै गर्भं च विप्रोऽसौ दत्त्वा स्वर्णं गृहीतवान् ॥
सापि नारी सुखं लेभे तेन गर्भेण प्रत्यहम् ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: That brāhmaṇa gave her a child in her womb and received gold. / And that woman experienced happiness day after day through that pregnancy.

3.2.s:
kadāciddaśamāsāṃte mohinīmabravīcchivaḥ ..
svapnāṃtare mahārāja sāpi jñātvā tathākarot .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
कदाचिद्दशमासांते मोहिनीमब्रवीच्छिवः ॥
स्वप्नांतरे महाराज सापि ज्ञात्वा तथाकरोत् ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: Once, at the end of ten months, Śiva spoke to Mohinī / within a dream, O great king, and understanding [his words], she acted accordingly.

3.2.s:
dolāmadhye sahasraṃ ca svarṇaṃ caiva svabālakam ..
rājadvāre sthāpayitvā suṣvāpa jananī sukham .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
दोलामध्ये सहस्रं च स्वर्णं चैव स्वबालकम् ॥
राजद्वारे स्थापयित्वा सुष्वाप जननी सुखम् ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: Having placed a thousand [pieces of] gold and her own boy inside a cradle / at the king’s gate, the mother slept happily.

3.2.s:
śivena bodhito rājā sutārthī rudrapūjakaḥ ..
dvijaputraṃ samālebhe mohinyāṃ jātamuttamam .. 3.2.18.30 ..
3.2.d:
शिवेन बोधितो राजा सुतार्थी रुद्रपूजकः ॥
द्विजपुत्रं समालेभे मोहिन्यां जातमुत्तमम् ॥ 3.2.18.30 ॥
3.2.m: Instructed by Śiva, the king, who desired a son and worshipped Rudra, / obtained the excellent twice-born son born to Mohinī.

3.2.s:
kārayitvā jātakarma vitatāra dhanaṃ bahu ..
haradattaśca nāmnāsītsarvavidyāviśāradaḥ .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
कारयित्वा जातकर्म विततार धनं बहु ॥
हरदत्तश्च नाम्नासीत्सर्वविद्याविशारदः ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: Having had the birth rites performed, he gave away much wealth. / Named Haradatta, he became proficient in all branches of learning.

3.2.s:
piturante ca tadrājyaṃ prāpya dharmaṃ prakāśayan ..
gayāśrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tena phalgutīre vidhānataḥ .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
पितुरन्ते च तद्राज्यं प्राप्य धर्मं प्रकाशयन् ॥
गयाश्राद्धं कृतं तेन फल्गुतीरे विधानतः ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: After his father’s passing, he obtained that kingdom, manifesting righteousness. / He performed the ancestral rite of Gayā on the bank of the Phalgu according to the rules.

3.2.s: trayo hastāstadā jātāḥ sa rājā vismito'bhavat .. 33 ..
3.2.d: त्रयो हस्तास्तदा जाताः स राजा विस्मितोऽभवत् ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: Then three hands appeared; the king was astonished.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo nṛpatiṃ prāha bho nṛpa ..
kasmai yogyo hi piṃḍo'sau śrutvā rājābravīdidam .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो नृपतिं प्राह भो नृप ॥
कस्मै योग्यो हि पिंडोऽसौ श्रुत्वा राजाब्रवीदिदम् ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, that vetāla said to the king: “O king, / to whom is that rice ball due?” Hearing this, the king said:

3.2.s:
dravyārthī paṃḍito jñeyo gurutulyaśca bhūpatiḥ ..
caurāya piṃḍa ucito yasya nārī ca mohinī .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
द्रव्यार्थी पंडितो ज्ञेयो गुरुतुल्यश्च भूपतिः ॥
चौराय पिंड उचितो यस्य नारी च मोहिनी ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: “The scholar should be understood as desiring wealth, and the king is equal to a guru; / the rice ball is proper for the thief whose wife was Mohinī.”

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tena piṃḍaprabhāvena sa cauro brahmadravyahā ..
nirayānniḥsṛto vipra svargalokaṃ samāgataḥ .. 36 ..
tulanīya - vetālapañcaviṃśatiḥ
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
तेन पिंडप्रभावेन स चौरो ब्रह्मद्रव्यहा ॥
निरयान्निःसृतो विप्र स्वर्गलोकं समागतः ॥ 36 ॥
तुलनीय - वेतालपञ्चविंशतिः
3.2.m:
Sūta said: / “By the power of that rice ball, that thief who stole the property of brāhmaṇas / was released from hell, O brāhmaṇa, and went to the world of heaven.”
To be compared with: Vetālapañcaviṃśati.

3.2.s:
citrakūṭe ca nṛpatī rūpadatta iti śrutaḥ ..
vane mṛgaprasaṃgena vanāntaramupāyayau..1..
3.2.d:
चित्रकूटे च नृपती रूपदत्त इति श्रुतः ॥
वने मृगप्रसंगेन वनान्तरमुपाययौ॥1॥
3.2.m: In Citrakūṭa there was a king known as Rūpadatta. / In the forest, in pursuit of deer, he entered another forest.

3.2.s:
madhyāhne sarasastīre muniputro dadarśa saḥ..
cinvatīṃ padmakusumaṃ rūpayauvanaśālinīm ..2..
3.2.d:
मध्याह्ने सरसस्तीरे मुनिपुत्रो ददर्श सः॥
चिन्वतीं पद्मकुसुमं रूपयौवनशालिनीम् ॥2॥
3.2.m: At midday, on the bank of a lake, he saw a sage’s daughter / gathering lotus blossoms, endowed with beauty and youth.

3.2.s:
tasyā netre svayaṃ netre caikībhūte samāgate..
etasminnaṃtare viprastatra prāpto dadarśa tau ..3..
3.2.d:
तस्या नेत्रे स्वयं नेत्रे चैकीभूते समागते॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विप्रस्तत्र प्राप्तो ददर्श तौ ॥3॥
3.2.m: Her eyes and his eyes met and became one. / Meanwhile, a brāhmaṇa arrived there and saw the two of them.

3.2.s:
tasya darśanamātreṇa nṛpaterjñānamāgatam ..
vinayāvanato rājā dharmaṃ papraccha cottamam ..4..
3.2.d:
तस्य दर्शनमात्रेण नृपतेर्ज्ञानमागतम् ॥
विनयावनतो राजा धर्मं पप्रच्छ चोत्तमम् ॥4॥
3.2.m: At the mere sight of him, wisdom arose in the king. / Bowing low with modesty, the king inquired about the highest righteousness.

3.2.s:
tamuvāca munirddhīmāndayādharmaprapoṣaṇam .. .
nirbhayasya samaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..5..
3.2.d:
तमुवाच मुनिर्द्धीमान्दयाधर्मप्रपोषणम् ॥ ।
निर्भयस्य समं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥5॥
3.2.m: The wise sage said to him: “Compassion is the nourishment of righteousness. / Equal to the gift of fearlessness, there has never been nor will there ever be [any gift].

3.2.s:
anarhāndaṇḍamādadyādarhapūjāphalaṃ bhajet ..
mitratā godvije nityaṃ samatā daṃḍanigrahe .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
अनर्हान्दण्डमादद्यादर्हपूजाफलं भजेत् ॥
मित्रता गोद्विजे नित्यं समता दंडनिग्रहे ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: He should punish the undeserving and enjoy the fruit of honouring the deserving; / constant friendliness toward cows and twice-born, impartiality in administering punishment;

3.2.s:
satyatā surapūjāyāṃ damatā gurupūjane ..
mṛdutā dānasamaye saṃtuṣṭirniṃdyakarmaṇi ..7..
3.2.d:
सत्यता सुरपूजायां दमता गुरुपूजने ॥
मृदुता दानसमये संतुष्टिर्निंद्यकर्मणि ॥7॥
3.2.m: truthfulness in worshipping the gods, self-restraint in worshipping the guru, / gentleness at the time of giving, and contentment in blameless conduct.”

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa muniḥ putrīṃ tasmai dattvā gṛhaṃ yayau..
rājāpi ca tayā sārddhaṃ vaṭamūle'śayiṣṭa vai ..8..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स मुनिः पुत्रीं तस्मै दत्त्वा गृहं ययौ॥
राजापि च तया सार्द्धं वटमूलेऽशयिष्ट वै ॥8॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, that sage gave his daughter to him and went home. / And the king lay down to sleep with her at the root of a banyan tree.

3.2.s:
tadā tu rākṣasaḥ kaścittatpatnībhakṣaṇotsukaḥ ..
bodhayāmāsa nṛpatiṃ baliṃ tasmai sa bhūpatiḥ ..9..
3.2.d:
तदा तु राक्षसः कश्चित्तत्पत्नीभक्षणोत्सुकः ॥
बोधयामास नृपतिं बलिं तस्मै स भूपतिः ॥9॥
3.2.m: Then a certain rākṣasa, eager to devour his wife, / woke the king. That ruler of the earth, in order to give him an offering,

3.2.s:
dānārthaṃ caiva kravyāde saptavarṣātmakaṃ dvijam ..
samayaṃ kṛtavānrājā satyena svagṛhaṃ yayau ..3.2.19.1 0..
3.2.d:
दानार्थं चैव क्रव्यादे सप्तवर्षात्मकं द्विजम् ॥
समयं कृतवान्राजा सत्येन स्वगृहं ययौ ॥3.2.19.1 0॥
3.2.m: a twice-born boy seven years of age for the flesh-eater, / made an agreement; and by his truthfulness, the king went to his own home.

3.2.s:
amātyaiḥ saṃmataṃ kṛtvā svarṇalakṣaṃ dadau dvije ..
madhyaṃ bālaṃ puraskṛtya rākṣasāya baliṃ dadau..11..
3.2.d:
अमात्यैः संमतं कृत्वा स्वर्णलक्षं ददौ द्विजे ॥
मध्यं बालं पुरस्कृत्य राक्षसाय बलिं ददौ॥11॥
3.2.m: Having obtained the consent of his ministers, he gave a hundred thousand pieces of gold to a twice-born, / placed the middle son before him, and gave him as an offering to the rākṣasa.

3.2.s:
mṛtyukāle dvijasuto vihasyoccai ruroda ha ..
kathaṃ hāsyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena tatpaścādrodanaṃ katham ..12..
3.2.d:
मृत्युकाले द्विजसुतो विहस्योच्चै रुरोद ह ॥
कथं हास्यं कृतं तेन तत्पश्चाद्रोदनं कथम् ॥12॥
3.2.m: At the time of death, the twice-born son laughed and wept loudly. / Why did he laugh, and why did he weep after that?”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā nṛpaḥ prāha śṛṇu vaitālika dvija ..
jyeṣṭhaputraṃ piturhṛdyaṃ mātṛhṛdyamavaryakam..13..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा नृपः प्राह शृणु वैतालिक द्विज ॥
ज्येष्ठपुत्रं पितुर्हृद्यं मातृहृद्यमवर्यकम्॥13॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the king said: “Listen, O twice-born vetāla! / The eldest son is dear to the father’s heart; the youngest is dear to the mother’s heart.

3.2.s:
jñātvā sa madhyamaḥ putro rājānaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau..
nirdayī rūpasenaśca patnīkalyāṇabhikṣukaḥ ..14..
3.2.d:
ज्ञात्वा स मध्यमः पुत्रो राजानं शरणं ययौ॥
निर्दयी रूपसेनश्च पत्नीकल्याणभिक्षुकः ॥14॥
3.2.m: Knowing this, that middle son sought refuge with the king. / But Rūpasena was merciless, begging for his wife’s welfare.

3.2.s:
khaṅgahastaṃ nṛpaṃ jñātvā jahāsa śivatatparaḥ ..
rākṣasāya śarīraṃ me prāptamasmādruroda ha ..15..
tulanīya - vetālapañcaviṃśatiḥ 20
kathopari ṭippaṇī
3.2.d:
खङ्गहस्तं नृपं ज्ञात्वा जहास शिवतत्परः ॥
राक्षसाय शरीरं मे प्राप्तमस्माद्रुरोद ह ॥15॥
तुलनीय - वेतालपञ्चविंशतिः 20
कथोपरि टिप्पणी
3.2.m:
Seeing the king with sword in hand, devoted to Śiva, he laughed; / and because he thought, ‘My body has been given to a rākṣasa,’ he wept.”
To be compared with: Vetālapañcaviṃśati 20.
Note on the story.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā sa vaitālo nṛpaṃ prāha punaḥ kathām ..
viśālanagare ramye vipuleśo mahīpatiḥ ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा स वैतालो नृपं प्राह पुनः कथाम् ॥
विशालनगरे रम्ये विपुलेशो महीपतिः ॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Having heard this, that vetāla told the king another story: / “In the charming city of Viśālā, there was a king named Vipuleśa.

3.2.s:
tasya grāmevasadvaiśyorthadattovipaṇe rataḥ ..
anaṃgamaṃjarī kanyā tasya jātā manoramā..2..
3.2.d:
तस्य ग्रामेवसद्वैश्योर्थदत्तोविपणे रतः ॥
अनंगमंजरी कन्या तस्य जाता मनोरमा॥2॥
3.2.m: In his village lived a vaiśya named Arthadatta, devoted to trade. / A charming daughter was born to him, named Anaṅgamañjarī.

3.2.s:
suvarṇanāmne vaiśyāya pitā vai dattavānsvayam..
kadācitkamalagrāmātsuvarṇo dvīpamāgamat..
dravyalābhāya nyavasacciraṃ kālaṃ sa lubdhavān ..3..
3.2.d:
सुवर्णनाम्ने वैश्याय पिता वै दत्तवान्स्वयम्॥
कदाचित्कमलग्रामात्सुवर्णो द्वीपमागमत्॥
द्रव्यलाभाय न्यवसच्चिरं कालं स लुब्धवान् ॥3॥
3.2.m: Her father himself gave her [in marriage] to a vaiśya named Suvarṇa. / Once Suvarṇa went from Kamalagrāma to an island; / greedy for gain of wealth, he dwelled there for a long time.

3.2.s:
anaṃgamaṃjarīgehe daivayogāddvijottamaḥ ..
kamalākaranāmāsau kṛtyayogātsamāgataḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
अनंगमंजरीगेहे दैवयोगाद्द्विजोत्तमः ॥
कमलाकरनामासौ कृत्ययोगात्समागतः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: By the workings of fate, an excellent twice-born / named Kamalākara came to Anaṅgamañjarī's house for the sake of an errand.

3.2.s:
homāṃte sundarī nārī mārjanārthe sutā gatā ..
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ kāmakalikāṃ mumoha dvijasattamaḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
होमांते सुन्दरी नारी मार्जनार्थे सुता गता ॥
दृष्ट्वा तां कामकलिकां मुमोह द्विजसत्तमः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: At the conclusion of the fire sacrifice, the beautiful woman, his daughter, went to sweep; / seeing that budding flower of love, the best of the twice-born was infatuated.

3.2.s:
sutāpi madaghūrṇākṣī viprāya samayaṃ dadau ..
niśīthe tamaudbhūte tvaṃ māṃ prāpya sukhī bhava .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
सुतापि मदघूर्णाक्षी विप्राय समयं ददौ ॥
निशीथे तमौद्भूते त्वं मां प्राप्य सुखी भव ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: The daughter too, her eyes rolling with passion, made an appointment with the brāhmaṇa: / "When deep darkness arises at midnight, obtain me and be happy."

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā dvijo vākyaṃ tasyā dhyānaṃ tadākarot ..
kāmāgninā ciraṃ taptaḥ suṣvāpa paramāsane .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा द्विजो वाक्यं तस्या ध्यानं तदाकरोत् ॥
कामाग्निना चिरं तप्तः सुष्वाप परमासने ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this speech, the twice-born then meditated upon her; / long burning with the fire of passion, he fell asleep on his fine couch.

3.2.s:
arddharātre tu sā nārī dvijāgamanatatparā ..
mārgamanveṣamāṇā sā priyasya smarapīḍitā.. .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
अर्द्धरात्रे तु सा नारी द्विजागमनतत्परा ॥
मार्गमन्वेषमाणा सा प्रियस्य स्मरपीडिता॥ ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: At midnight, that woman, intent on the arrival of the twice-born, / searching the path of her beloved, afflicted by love,

3.2.s:
nāgataḥ sa dvijo daivāttadā sā maraṇaṃ gatā ..
kamalākara evāśu samayānte samāyayau .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
नागतः स द्विजो दैवात्तदा सा मरणं गता ॥
कमलाकर एवाशु समयान्ते समाययौ ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Since that twice-born did not come by fate, then met her death. / Kamalākara indeed arrived quickly at the end of the appointed time.

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuvaśāṃ subhrūṃ svayaṃ maraṇamāgataḥ ..
prabhāte cārthadatto vai dāhayāmāsa tāṃ śucā .. 3.2.20.10 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा मृत्युवशां सुभ्रूं स्वयं मरणमागतः ॥
प्रभाते चार्थदत्तो वै दाहयामास तां शुचा ॥ 3.2.20.10 ॥
3.2.m: Seeing that fair-browed woman subject to death, he himself met his death. / And in the morning, Arthadatta indeed had her cremated in grief.

3.2.s:
suvarṇaśca tadāgatya vilalāpa priyāṃ prati ..
citāyāṃ bhasmasādbhūtvā svargaloke tu sā yayau.. .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
सुवर्णश्च तदागत्य विललाप प्रियां प्रति ॥
चितायां भस्मसाद्भूत्वा स्वर्गलोके तु सा ययौ॥ ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: And Suvarṇa, having arrived then, lamented for his beloved. / Having been reduced to ashes on the pyre, she indeed went to heaven.

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo nṛpatiṃ prāha vikramam ..
kasya sneho'dhikasteṣāṃ kutaḥ svargapuraṃ yayau .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो नृपतिं प्राह विक्रमम् ॥
कस्य स्नेहोऽधिकस्तेषां कुतः स्वर्गपुरं ययौ ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: Having said this, that vetāla said to King Vikrama: / "Whose love was the greatest among them? Whence did she go to the city of heaven?"

3.2.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
pati snehodhikasteṣāṃ madhyamau nāriviprakau ..
dvijasnehena sā nārī mṛtā svargapuraṃ yayau .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
॥ राजोवाच ॥ ॥
पति स्नेहोधिकस्तेषां मध्यमौ नारिविप्रकौ ॥
द्विजस्नेहेन सा नारी मृता स्वर्गपुरं ययौ ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: The king said: / "Among them, the husband's love was the greatest; the woman and the brāhmaṇa were middling. / Out of love for the twice-born, that woman died and went to the city of heaven.

3.2.s: vaiśyavarṇaiḥ sadā pūjyo brāhmaṇo brahmamūrtimān .. .. 14 ..
3.2.d: वैश्यवर्णैः सदा पूज्यो ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्ममूर्तिमान् ॥ ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: A brāhmaṇa, the embodiment of Brahman, is always to be worshipped by the vaiśya class.

3.2.s:
dvijo'pi nāptavānnārīṃ tadā svargagatiṃ harim ..
hṛdi kṛtvā ca nidhanaṃ prāpto hyasmāttriviṣṭapam .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
द्विजोऽपि नाप्तवान्नारीं तदा स्वर्गगतिं हरिम् ॥
हृदि कृत्वा च निधनं प्राप्तो ह्यस्मात्त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: The twice-born too, not having obtained the woman, holding in his heart / Hari, the way to heaven, met his death, and thus indeed [attained] heaven.

3.2.s:
suvarṇo hṛdi saṃjñāya matpriyā brahmavatsalā ..
māṃ tyaktā tu divaṃ yātā vahnidāhaprabhāvataḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
सुवर्णो हृदि संज्ञाय मत्प्रिया ब्रह्मवत्सला ॥
मां त्यक्ता तु दिवं याता वह्निदाहप्रभावतः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Suvarṇa, knowing in his heart, 'My beloved was devoted to brāhmaṇas; / having abandoned me, she went to heaven by the power of burning in the fire [of the funeral pyre].'"

3.2.s:
iti śrībhīviṣye mahāpurāṇe pratisargaparvaṇi caturyugakhaṇḍāparaparyāye kaliyu gīyetihāsamuccaye viṃśo'dhyāya .. 20 ..
tulanīya - vetālapañcaviṃśatiḥ 21
kathāyāḥ saṃbhāvita vivecanam
3.2.d:
इति श्रीभीविष्ये महापुराणे प्रतिसर्गपर्वणि चतुर्युगखण्डापरपर्याये कलियु गीयेतिहासमुच्चये विंशोऽध्याय ॥ 20 ॥
तुलनीय - वेतालपञ्चविंशतिः 21
कथायाः संभावित विवेचनम्
3.2.m:
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the Collection of Historical Tales of the Kali Age, in the Section on the Four Ages, in the Pratisargaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Compare: Vetālapañcaviṃśati 21.
Probable Analysis of the Story

3.2.s:
sūta uvāca..
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo rājānaṃ prāha namradhīḥ..
jayasthalapure ramye vardhamāno nṛpobhavat..1..
3.2.d:
सूत उवाच॥
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालो राजानं प्राह नम्रधीः॥
जयस्थलपुरे रम्ये वर्धमानो नृपोभवत्॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, that vetāla, humble-minded, said to the king: / "In the charming city of Jayasthala, Vardhamāna became king.

3.2.s:
tasya grāmevasadvipro vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ..
viṣṇusvāmīti vikhyāto rādhākṛṣṇaparāyaṇaḥ..2..
3.2.d:
तस्य ग्रामेवसद्विप्रो वेदवेदांगपारगः॥
विष्णुस्वामीति विख्यातो राधाकृष्णपरायणः॥2॥
3.2.m: In his village lived a brāhmaṇa who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, / celebrated as Viṣṇusvāmin, devoted to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

3.2.s:
catvāraścātmajāstasya caturbhāgaparāyaṇāḥ ..
dyūtakarmā ca kulaṭo viṣayī nāstikaḥ śrutaḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
चत्वारश्चात्मजास्तस्य चतुर्भागपरायणाः ॥
द्यूतकर्मा च कुलटो विषयी नास्तिकः श्रुतः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: He had four sons, each devoted to one of four parts [of life]: / one engaged in gambling, one a debauchee, one sensual, and one known as an atheist.

3.2.s:
kadāciddaivayogena nirddhanatvaṃ ca te gatāḥ ..
pitaraṃ viṣṇuśarmāṇaṃ nemuste vinayānvitāḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
कदाचिद्दैवयोगेन निर्द्धनत्वं च ते गताः ॥
पितरं विष्णुशर्माणं नेमुस्ते विनयान्विताः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: Once, by the workings of fate, they fell into poverty. / Filled with humility, they bowed down to their father, Viṣṇuśarman,

3.2.s:
ūcū ramā kathaṃ naṣṭā tadvadasva pitaḥ priya ..
pitovāca tu tacchrutvā dyūtakarmanniśāmaya .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
ऊचू रमा कथं नष्टा तद्वदस्व पितः प्रिय ॥
पितोवाच तु तच्छ्रुत्वा द्यूतकर्मन्निशामय ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: And said, 'How has our fortune been lost? Tell us that, dear father.' / Hearing that, the father said, 'Listen, Gambler!

3.2.s:
dyūto dhanavyayakaraḥ pāpamūlo mahākhalaḥ ..
vyabhicārastathā cauryaṃ nirdayatvamato bhavet ..
dyūtakarmaprabhāveṇa tvadīyadravyasaṃkṣayaḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
द्यूतो धनव्ययकरः पापमूलो महाखलः ॥
व्यभिचारस्तथा चौर्यं निर्दयत्वमतो भवेत् ॥
द्यूतकर्मप्रभावेण त्वदीयद्रव्यसंक्षयः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Gambling causes the expenditure of wealth, is the root of sin, and is greatly wicked; / from it arise unfaithfulness, theft, and cruelty. / By the power of gambling, your wealth has been destroyed.

3.2.s:
dhanopāyena bhoḥ pitrorvākyaṃ kuru matiṃ prati ..
tīrthavrataprabhāveṇa tvatpāpaṃ saṃkṣayaṃ vrajet .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
धनोपायेन भोः पित्रोर्वाक्यं कुरु मतिं प्रति ॥
तीर्थव्रतप्रभावेण त्वत्पापं संक्षयं व्रजेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: O you, set your mind on the words of your parents regarding the means of wealth; / by the power of sacred fords and votive observances, your sin will be destroyed.

3.2.s:
he putra kulaṭa tvaṃ vai veśyāsaṃgaṃ mahāśubham ..
tyaktvā brahmaparo bhūtvā brahmacarye matiṃ kuru .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
हे पुत्र कुलट त्वं वै वेश्यासंगं महाशुभम् ॥
त्यक्त्वा ब्रह्मपरो भूत्वा ब्रह्मचर्ये मतिं कुरु ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: O son, Debauchee, having abandoned the company of prostitutes, [which is] exceedingly inauspicious, / be devoted to Brahman and set your mind on celibacy.

3.2.s:
viṣayinmāṃsamadire nityapāpavivardhike ..
ataḥ prāpsyati cauryatvamato vai nirayastathā .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
विषयिन्मांसमदिरे नित्यपापविवर्धिके ॥
अतः प्राप्स्यति चौर्यत्वमतो वै निरयस्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: O Sensualist, meat and liquor always increase sin; / from this one will acquire thievery, and from that, hell.

3.2.s:
tasmāttvaṃ prabhumīśānaṃ viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ jagatpatim ..
nivedya sarvathā dravyaṃ bhuñjīthā vāgyataḥ svayam .. 3.2.21.10 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मात्त्वं प्रभुमीशानं विष्णुं जिष्णुं जगत्पतिम् ॥
निवेद्य सर्वथा द्रव्यं भुञ्जीथा वाग्यतः स्वयम् ॥ 3.2.21.10 ॥
3.2.m: Therefore, having offered all your wealth to the Lord, Īśāna, Viṣṇu, the victorious lord of the universe, / you should yourself eat with restraint of speech.

3.2.s:
nāstikatvaṃ devaniṃdā parityajya matiṃ kuru ..
ātmā sarvābhayo nityamātmaśaktiśca caṃḍikā .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
नास्तिकत्वं देवनिंदा परित्यज्य मतिं कुरु ॥
आत्मा सर्वाभयो नित्यमात्मशक्तिश्च चंडिका ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: Having completely abandoned atheism and reviling the gods, direct your mind [aright]; / the self is ever free from all fear, and the power of the self is Caṇḍikā.

3.2.s:
ātmanoṃgāni devāśca sarvajīvaguhāśayāḥ ..
tāñjñātvā pūjanaṃ teṣāṃ kuru tvaṃ pāpaśāntaye .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
आत्मनोंगानि देवाश्च सर्वजीवगुहाशयाः ॥
ताञ्ज्ञात्वा पूजनं तेषां कुरु त्वं पापशान्तये ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: The gods are the limbs of the self, dwelling in the cave of all living beings; / knowing them, worship them for the pacification of sin.'

3.2.s:
iti te vacanaṃ śrutvā gatāstīrthāntaraṃ prati ..
śivamārādhayāmāsurvidyārthe sarvarūpiṇam .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
इति ते वचनं श्रुत्वा गतास्तीर्थान्तरं प्रति ॥
शिवमाराधयामासुर्विद्यार्थे सर्वरूपिणम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing these words of his, they went to another sacred ford; / for the sake of sacred knowledge they worshipped Śiva, who has all forms.

3.2.s:
varṣāṃte ca mahādevo vidyāṃ saṃjīvanīṃ dadau ..
te prāpya vanamāgatya parīkṣārthe samudyatāḥ .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
वर्षांते च महादेवो विद्यां संजीवनीं ददौ ॥
ते प्राप्य वनमागत्य परीक्षार्थे समुद्यताः ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: At the end of a year, Mahādeva gave them the saṃjīvanī lore; / having obtained it, they went into the forest, ready to test it.

3.2.s:
mṛtavyāghrāsthini śreṣṭhaṃ maṃtrapūtāṃbu cākṣipat ..
tena maṃtraprabhāveṇa paṃjaratvamupāgatam .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
मृतव्याघ्रास्थिनि श्रेष्ठं मंत्रपूतांबु चाक्षिपत् ॥
तेन मंत्रप्रभावेण पंजरत्वमुपागतम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: The eldest threw water consecrated with mantras upon the bones of a dead tiger; / by the power of that mantra, they attained the state of a skeleton.

3.2.s:
tasyoparyyeva kulaṭo maṃtrapūtaṃ payo'kṣipat ..
ghanamāṃsaṃ ca rudhiraṃ tena maṃtreṇa cābhavat .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
तस्योपर्य्येव कुलटो मंत्रपूतं पयोऽक्षिपत् ॥
घनमांसं च रुधिरं तेन मंत्रेण चाभवत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Upon that very [skeleton], the debauchee threw milk consecrated with mantras; / and by that mantra, dense flesh and blood came into being.

3.2.s:
viṣayī cākṣipaccaiva tasyopari jalaṃ śubham ..
tena mantraprabhāveṇa tvakprāṇatvamupāgatam .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
विषयी चाक्षिपच्चैव तस्योपरि जलं शुभम् ॥
तेन मन्त्रप्रभावेण त्वक्प्राणत्वमुपागतम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: And the sensualist threw auspicious water upon it; / by the power of that mantra, it attained skin and vital breath.

3.2.s:
suptaṃ vyāghraṃ ca saṃjñāya nāstikastu jalaṃ dadau ..
maṃtreṇa bodhito vyāghrastāṃśca viprānakhādayat..18..
3.2.d:
सुप्तं व्याघ्रं च संज्ञाय नास्तिकस्तु जलं ददौ ॥
मंत्रेण बोधितो व्याघ्रस्तांश्च विप्रानखादयत्॥18॥
3.2.m: And knowing the tiger to be asleep, the atheist gave water; / awakened by the mantra, the tiger devoured those brāhmaṇas.

3.2.s:
sūta uvāca ..
ityuktvā sa tu vetālo rājānamidamabravīt ..
rājanmūrkho hi kasteṣāṃ śrutvā rājābravīdidam .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वेतालो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
राजन्मूर्खो हि कस्तेषां श्रुत्वा राजाब्रवीदिदम् ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, that vetāla said this to the king: / 'O King, which of them was indeed a fool?' Hearing this, the king said:

3.2.s:
bodhito yena sa vyāghraḥ sa mūrkhastvadhiko mataḥ ..
iti śrutvā dvijaśreṣṭho vaitālaḥ punarabravīt .. 3.2.21.20 ..
tulanīya - kathāsaritsāgare vetālapaṃcaviṃśati
3.2.d:
बोधितो येन स व्याघ्रः स मूर्खस्त्वधिको मतः ॥
इति श्रुत्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठो वैतालः पुनरब्रवीत् ॥ 3.2.21.20 ॥
तुलनीय - कथासरित्सागरे वेतालपंचविंशति
3.2.m:
'He by whom that tiger was awakened is considered the greatest fool.' / Hearing this, the vetāla, best of the twice-born, spoke again.
Compare: Vetālapañcaviṃśati in the Kathāsaritsāgara.

3.2.s:
.. vaitāla uvāca .. ..
bho rājanbilvatīgrāme gaṃgāyāmunamadhyage ..
ahaṃ pūrvabhave cāsaṃ kṣatrasiṃho mahīpatiḥ .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ वैताल उवाच ॥ ॥
भो राजन्बिल्वतीग्रामे गंगायामुनमध्यगे ॥
अहं पूर्वभवे चासं क्षत्रसिंहो महीपतिः ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: The vetāla said: / 'O King, in the village of Bilvatī, situated between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, / in a previous birth I was King Kṣatrasiṃha.

3.2.s:
tasya grāme vasadvipro vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ ..
śaṃbhudatta iti khyāto rudrabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य ग्रामे वसद्विप्रो वेदवेदांगपारगः ॥
शंभुदत्त इति ख्यातो रुद्रभक्तिपरायणः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: In his village lived a brāhmaṇa who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, / known as Śambhudatta, devoted to the worship of Rudra.

3.2.s:
ubhakau tanayau tasya sarvavidyāviśāradau ..
viṣṇubhaktaḥ smṛto jyeṣṭho nāmnā līlādharo balī ..
śākto'bhavattadanujo mohano nāma śrutaḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
उभकौ तनयौ तस्य सर्वविद्याविशारदौ ॥
विष्णुभक्तः स्मृतो ज्येष्ठो नाम्ना लीलाधरो बली ॥
शाक्तोऽभवत्तदनुजो मोहनो नाम श्रुतः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: He had two sons, skilled in all branches of knowledge. / The elder was known as a devotee of Viṣṇu, strong, named Līlādhara; / his younger brother was a Śākta, known by the name Mohana.

3.2.s:
kadācitkṣatrasiṃhastu yajñārthī yajñahetave ..
śaṃbhudattaṃ samāhūya sasutaṃ dharmakovidam ..
svayaṃ ca kārayāmāsa cchāgamedhaṃ surapriyam .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
कदाचित्क्षत्रसिंहस्तु यज्ञार्थी यज्ञहेतवे ॥
शंभुदत्तं समाहूय ससुतं धर्मकोविदम् ॥
स्वयं च कारयामास च्छागमेधं सुरप्रियम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: Once, Kṣatrasiṃha, desirous of a sacrifice, for the sake of the sacrifice / summoned Śambhudatta, skilled in dharma, together with his sons, / and himself had performed a goat-sacrifice pleasing to the gods.'

3.2.s:
śaṃbhudattastu vṛddhātmā śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ ..
catuścakrāṃśca saṃsthāpya kalaśaṃ kāryasiddhidam .. 5..
3.2.d:
शंभुदत्तस्तु वृद्धात्मा शिवभक्तिपरायणः ॥
चतुश्चक्रांश्च संस्थाप्य कलशं कार्यसिद्धिदम् ॥ 5॥
3.2.m: Śambhudatta, an aged man devoted to the worship of Śiva, / set up the four circles and the pitcher that grants the accomplishment of undertakings.

3.2.s:
havyaiḥ susaṃskṛtai ramyaiścakāra havanaṃ mudā ..
chāgamāhūya vidhivatpūjayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
हव्यैः सुसंस्कृतै रम्यैश्चकार हवनं मुदा ॥
छागमाहूय विधिवत्पूजयामास भूपतिः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: With properly consecrated and charming sacrificial substances he gladly performed the oblation. / Having summoned the goat according to rule, the king worshipped it.

3.2.s:
līlādharastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā chāgaṃ ca maraṇonmukham ..
dayālurveṣṇavo dhīmānabravīdvacanaṃ ruṣā .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
लीलाधरस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा छागं च मरणोन्मुखम् ॥
दयालुर्वेष्णवो धीमानब्रवीद्वचनं रुषा ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Seeing that goat facing death, / the compassionate and wise Vaiṣṇava Līlādhara spoke words in anger:

3.2.s:
dāruṇaṃ narakaṃ yogyamanayā jīvahiṃsayā ..
sarveśo bhagavānviṣṇuhiṃsāyajñena duṣyati .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
दारुणं नरकं योग्यमनया जीवहिंसया ॥
सर्वेशो भगवान्विष्णुहिंसायज्ञेन दुष्यति ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: “A terrible hell is deserved on account of this injury to living beings. / The Lord Viṣṇu, master of all, is displeased by a sacrifice involving injury.”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya jyeṣṭhabaṃdhośca mohanaḥ ..
mṛdupūrvaṃ jahāsoccairvacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य ज्येष्ठबंधोश्च मोहनः ॥
मृदुपूर्वं जहासोच्चैर्वचनं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing these words of his elder brother, Mohana / first laughed softly and then loudly, and with a humble mind spoke these words:

3.2.s:
purā satyayuge bhrātarbrāhmaṇā yajñatatparāḥ ..
ajenaiva hi yaṣṭavyamiti jñātvā parāṃ śrutim ..3.2.22.1 0..
3.2.d:
पुरा सत्ययुगे भ्रातर्ब्राह्मणा यज्ञतत्पराः ॥
अजेनैव हि यष्टव्यमिति ज्ञात्वा परां श्रुतिम् ॥3.2.22.1 0॥
3.2.m: “Formerly in the Golden Age, O brother, brāhmaṇas intent on sacrifice, / knowing the supreme revelation that one should sacrifice with an 'aja',

3.2.s:
tilādhikamajaṃ matvā havye te tu mano dadhuḥ ..
tadā śakrādayo devā vahnimadhye samāgatāḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
तिलाधिकमजं मत्वा हव्ये ते तु मनो दधुः ॥
तदा शक्रादयो देवा वह्निमध्ये समागताः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: construed 'aja' to mean sesamum and the like, and fixed their minds on [such] an offering. / Then the gods, Śakra and the others, arrived in the midst of the fire,

3.2.s:
ūcuste madhuraṃ vākyaṃ tvanmataṃ niṣphalapradam ..
ajacchāgaḥ smṛto vedaistena yaṣṭavyamantaram .. 12 ...
3.2.d:
ऊचुस्ते मधुरं वाक्यं त्वन्मतं निष्फलप्रदम् ॥
अजच्छागः स्मृतो वेदैस्तेन यष्टव्यमन्तरम् ॥ 12 ॥।
3.2.m: and spoke sweet words: ‘Your view yields no fruit. / By 'aja', a he-goat is recorded in the Vedas; therefore one should sacrifice with it internally.’

3.2.s:
śrutveti vacanaṃ teṣāṃ vismitā munayo'bhavan ..
etasminnaṃtare tatra pitṛyoniramāvasuḥ .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
श्रुत्वेति वचनं तेषां विस्मिता मुनयोऽभवन् ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र पितृयोनिरमावसुः ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing their words, the sages were amazed. / In the meantime, Amāvasu, an ancestral spirit,

3.2.s:
vimānaṃ paramāruhya munīnprovāca nirbhayaḥ ..
chāga medhena yaṣṭavyaṃ surāṇāṃ tṛptihetave .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
विमानं परमारुह्य मुनीन्प्रोवाच निर्भयः ॥
छाग मेधेन यष्टव्यं सुराणां तृप्तिहेतवे ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: mounted an excellent celestial chariot and fearlessly addressed the sages: / ‘One should sacrifice with a goat-offering for the satisfaction of the gods.’

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya tathā kṛtvā śivaṃ yayuḥ ..
tasmāttvaṃ ca mayā sārddhaṃ yajñaṃ kuru mahāmate .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य तथा कृत्वा शिवं ययुः ॥
तस्मात्त्वं च मया सार्द्धं यज्ञं कुरु महामते ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing his words and acting accordingly, they attained auspiciousness. / Therefore, O high-minded one, perform the sacrifice together with me.”

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ līlādhara udāradhīḥ ..
mohanaṃ prāha dharmātmā yajñastretāyuge'bhavat .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचो घोरं लीलाधर उदारधीः ॥
मोहनं प्राह धर्मात्मा यज्ञस्त्रेतायुगेऽभवत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing these dreadful words, the noble-minded and righteous Līlādhara / said to Mohana: “Sacrifice [with animals] arose in the Tretā age.

3.2.s:
rajoguṇamayo lokastretāyāṃ saṃbabhūva ha ..
hiṃsā satyayuge nāsīddharmastatra catuṣpadaḥ ..17..
3.2.d:
रजोगुणमयो लोकस्त्रेतायां संबभूव ह ॥
हिंसा सत्ययुगे नासीद्धर्मस्तत्र चतुष्पदः ॥17॥
3.2.m: The world came to be dominated by the quality of passion in the Tretā age. / There was no injury in the Golden Age; dharma was four-footed there.

3.2.s:
havyena tarpitā devā na māṃse raktasaṃbhavaiḥ..
iti śrutvā kṣatrasiṃhastyaktvā chāgaṃ bhayāturam ..18..
3.2.d:
हव्येन तर्पिता देवा न मांसे रक्तसंभवैः॥
इति श्रुत्वा क्षत्रसिंहस्त्यक्त्वा छागं भयातुरम् ॥18॥
3.2.m: The gods were gratified with sacrificial oblations, not with meats produced from blood.” / Hearing this, Kṣatrasiṃha released the fear-stricken goat.

3.2.s:
phalā'dyaiḥ kārayāmāsa tadā pūrṇāhutīrnṛpa ..
etasminnantare devī tāmasī krodhamūrchitā ..
nagaraṃ dāhayāmāsa naranārīsamanvitam .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
फलाऽद्यैः कारयामास तदा पूर्णाहुतीर्नृप ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवी तामसी क्रोधमूर्छिता ॥
नगरं दाहयामास नरनारीसमन्वितम् ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: Then the king had the final oblations performed with fruits and other such things, O king. / In the meantime, the dark Goddess, swooning with anger, / burned down the city together with its men and women.

3.2.s:
mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa śaṃbhudattaḥ śivapriyaḥ ..
sa bhūtvā ca mahonmādī tyaktvā dehaṃ divaṃ yayau .. 3.2.22.20 ..
3.2.d:
महामायाप्रभावेण शंभुदत्तः शिवप्रियः ॥
स भूत्वा च महोन्मादी त्यक्त्वा देहं दिवं ययौ ॥ 3.2.22.20 ॥
3.2.m: By the power of Mahāmāyā, Śambhudatta, the beloved of Śiva, / became deeply maddened, abandoned his body, and went to heaven.

3.2.s:
tadā līlādharo vipro daśaputropajīvakaḥ ..
bālānadhyāpayāmāsa grāme padmapure śubhe .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
तदा लीलाधरो विप्रो दशपुत्रोपजीवकः ॥
बालानध्यापयामास ग्रामे पद्मपुरे शुभे ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: Then the brāhmaṇa Līlādhara, who was supported by ten sons, / taught boys in the auspicious village of Padmapura.

3.2.s:
kṣatrasiṃhastu nṛpatirmohanāntikamāyayau ..
prasādaṃ kārayāmāsa devamāturanugraham .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
क्षत्रसिंहस्तु नृपतिर्मोहनान्तिकमाययौ ॥
प्रसादं कारयामास देवमातुरनुग्रहम् ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: King Kṣatrasiṃha came into the presence of Mohana, / and sought the favour and grace of the Mother of the gods.

3.2.s:
.. mohana uvāca .. ...
bījamantrajapādbrahmā brāhmīṃ śaktimavāptavān ..
tadaṃbāyai namastubhyaṃ mahāvīrāyai namonamaḥ .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
॥ मोहन उवाच ॥ ॥।
बीजमन्त्रजपाद्ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मीं शक्तिमवाप्तवान् ॥
तदंबायै नमस्तुभ्यं महावीरायै नमोनमः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: Mohana said: / “By reciting the seed-mantra Brahmā obtained the power of Brahmā; / salutations to that Mother, salutations again and again to the greatly heroic one!

3.2.s:
japtvā saptaśatīṃ viṣṇurvaiṣṇavīṃ śaktimāptavān ..
tadaṃbāyai namastubhyaṃ mahālakṣmyai namonamaḥ .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
जप्त्वा सप्तशतीं विष्णुर्वैष्णवीं शक्तिमाप्तवान् ॥
तदंबायै नमस्तुभ्यं महालक्ष्म्यै नमोनमः ॥ 24 ॥
