3.2.m: By reciting the Saptaśatī Viṣṇu obtained the power of Viṣṇu; / salutations to that Mother, salutations again and again to Mahālakṣmī!

3.2.s:
praṇavāstanayā yasyāsturīyapuruṣapriyā ..
tadaṃbāyai namastubhyaṃ praṇavāyai namonamaḥ .. 25 ...
3.2.d:
प्रणवास्तनया यस्यास्तुरीयपुरुषप्रिया ॥
तदंबायै नमस्तुभ्यं प्रणवायै नमोनमः ॥ 25 ॥।
3.2.m: She whose daughter is the Praṇava, who is beloved of the fourth Person; / salutations to that Mother, salutations again and again to the Praṇava!

3.2.s:
yayā dṛśyamidaṃ jātaṃ yayā vai pālyate jagat ..
yasyā dehe sthitaṃ viśvaṃ tadaṃbāyai namonamaḥ .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
यया दृश्यमिदं जातं यया वै पाल्यते जगत् ॥
यस्या देहे स्थितं विश्वं तदंबायै नमोनमः ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: By whom this visible world was born, by whom indeed the universe is protected, / in whose body the universe is established; salutations to that Mother again and again!

3.2.s:
śacī siddhistathā mṛtyuḥ prabhā gīrvāṇasainikāḥ ..
svāhā ca nirṛtī rātrirṛddhirbhuktistvadudbhavā ..
lokapālapriyā tvaṃ hi lokamātarnamonamaḥ .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
शची सिद्धिस्तथा मृत्युः प्रभा गीर्वाणसैनिकाः ॥
स्वाहा च निरृती रात्रिरृद्धिर्भुक्तिस्त्वदुद्भवा ॥
लोकपालप्रिया त्वं हि लोकमातर्नमोनमः ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: Śacī, accomplishment, death, splendour, the armies of the gods, / Svāhā, Nirṛti, night, prosperity, and enjoyment originate from you; / you are beloved of the world protectors, salutations again and again to the Mother of the worlds!

3.2.s:
tṛṣṇā tṛptī ratirnnītirhiṃsā kṣāṃtirmatirgatiḥ ..
niṃdā stutistatherṣyā ca lajjā tvaṃ hi namonamaḥ .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
तृष्णा तृप्ती रतिर्न्नीतिर्हिंसा क्षांतिर्मतिर्गतिः ॥
निंदा स्तुतिस्तथेर्ष्या च लज्जा त्वं हि नमोनमः ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: Craving, satisfaction, pleasure, policy, injury, forbearance, intellect, movement, / censure, praise, jealousy, and modesty are indeed you; salutations again and again!”

3.2.s:
ityaṣṭakaprabhāveṇa kṣatrasiṃho mahīpatiḥ ..
śivalokaṃ gataḥ sādhu rvaitālatvamavāptavān .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
इत्यष्टकप्रभावेण क्षत्रसिंहो महीपतिः ॥
शिवलोकं गतः साधु र्वैतालत्वमवाप्तवान् ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: By the power of this eight-verse hymn, the pious king Kṣatrasiṃha / went to the world of Śiva and attained the state of a vetāla.

3.2.s:
tasmāttvaṃ vikramāditya bhaja durgāṃ sanātanīm ..
śivājñayā tvahaṃ prāptastvatsamīpe mahīpate .. 3.2.22.30 ..
3.2.d:
तस्मात्त्वं विक्रमादित्य भज दुर्गां सनातनीम् ॥
शिवाज्ञया त्वहं प्राप्तस्त्वत्समीपे महीपते ॥ 3.2.22.30 ॥
3.2.m: “Therefore, O Vikramāditya, worship eternal Durgā. / By the command of Śiva I have arrived in your presence, O king.

3.2.s:
praśnottareṇa bhūpāla mayā tvaṃ saṃparīkṣitaḥ ..
bhujayoste sthitirme syājjahi sarvaripūnbhuvi .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
प्रश्नोत्तरेण भूपाल मया त्वं संपरीक्षितः ॥
भुजयोस्ते स्थितिर्मे स्याज्जहि सर्वरिपून्भुवि ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: By means of question and answer you have been tested by me, O ruler of the earth. / May my abode be in your two arms; slay all enemies on earth!

3.2.s:
dasyunaṣṭāḥ purīḥ sarvāḥ kṣetrāṇi vividhāni ca ..
śāstramānena saṃsthāpya samayaṃ kuru bho nṛpa .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
दस्युनष्टाः पुरीः सर्वाः क्षेत्राणि विविधानि च ॥
शास्त्रमानेन संस्थाप्य समयं कुरु भो नृप ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: Re-establishing in accordance with the standard of scripture all the cities / and various holy places destroyed by bandits, establish an era, O king.

3.2.s:
yo nṛpaḥ sarvatīrthāni punaruddhārayiṣyati ..
sa hi matsthāpitaṃ saṃvadviparītaṃ kariṣyati .. .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
यो नृपः सर्वतीर्थानि पुनरुद्धारयिष्यति ॥
स हि मत्स्थापितं संवद्विपरीतं करिष्यति ॥ ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: A king who will restore all the sacred fords / will overturn the era established by me.

3.2.s:
vikramākhyānakālo'yaṃ punardharmaṃ karoti hi ..
dvādaśābdaśataṃ varṣaṃ dvāparo hi pravartate .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
विक्रमाख्यानकालोऽयं पुनर्धर्मं करोति हि ॥
द्वादशाब्दशतं वर्षं द्वापरो हि प्रवर्तते ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: This period known as the Vikramāditya era indeed restores righteousness. / A Dvāpara age indeed operates for twelve hundred years.

3.2.s:
tadante bhuvi kṛṣṇāṃśo bhaviṣyati mahā balī ..
kaleruddharaṇārthāya mlecchavaṃśavivṛddhaye .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
तदन्ते भुवि कृष्णांशो भविष्यति महा बली ॥
कलेरुद्धरणार्थाय म्लेच्छवंशविवृद्धये ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: At its end, a mighty portion of Kṛṣṇa will appear on earth / for the deliverance of the Kali age and the augmentation of the mleccha lineages.

3.2.s:
sūtādyā munayaḥ sarve naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ ..
viśālāyāṃ samāgatya cakratīrthanivāsinaḥ ..
bhaviṣyaṃti mahārāja purāṇaśravaṇe ratāḥ .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
सूताद्या मुनयः सर्वे नैमिषारण्यवासिनः ॥
विशालायां समागत्य चक्रतीर्थनिवासिनः ॥
भविष्यंति महाराज पुराणश्रवणे रताः ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m: All the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest, headed by Sūta, / having arrived in Viśālā and dwelling at Cakratīrtha, / will be devoted to listening to the Purāṇas, O great king.”

3.2.s:
ityuktvā sa tu vaitālastatraivāntaradhīyata ..
nṛpatirvikramādityaḥ paramānaṃdamāptavān ..37..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स तु वैतालस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
नृपतिर्विक्रमादित्यः परमानंदमाप्तवान् ॥37॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, that vetāla vanished right there. / King Vikramāditya attained supreme joy.

3.2.s:
tasmādyūyaṃ muniśreṣṭhā jñātvā saṃdhyāṃ samāgatām ..
śivaṃ bhajata sarveśaṃ dhyānaniṣṭhāsamanvitāḥ .. 38 .. ..
3.2.d:
तस्माद्यूयं मुनिश्रेष्ठा ज्ञात्वा संध्यां समागताम् ॥
शिवं भजत सर्वेशं ध्याननिष्ठासमन्विताः ॥ 38 ॥ ॥
3.2.m: Therefore, O best of sages, knowing that twilight has arrived, / worship Śiva, the lord of all, endowed with devotion to meditation.

3.2.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā tu munayo viśālānagarīsthitāḥ ..
snātvā kedārakuṇḍe te manasā pūjayañchivam .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तु मुनयो विशालानगरीस्थिताः ॥
स्नात्वा केदारकुण्डे ते मनसा पूजयञ्छिवम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Vyāsa said: / Having heard this, the sages residing in the city of Viśālā, / having bathed in the Kedāra pool, mentally worshipped Śiva.

3.2.s: samādhiniṣṭhāste sarve varṣamekaṃ vyatītayan .. 2 ..
3.2.d: समाधिनिष्ठास्ते सर्वे वर्षमेकं व्यतीतयन् ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: Absorbed in concentration, they all spent one year.

3.2.s:
etasminnaṃtare rājā vikramādityabhūpatiḥ ..
natvā munīnsamādhisthāṃstuṣṭāva parayā girā .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे राजा विक्रमादित्यभूपतिः ॥
नत्वा मुनीन्समाधिस्थांस्तुष्टाव परया गिरा ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: In the meantime, the king, King Vikramāditya, / having bowed to the sages seated in concentration, praised them with excellent speech.

3.2.s:
uṣitvā te tu munayaḥ sūtaṃ gatvā'bruvannidam ..
so'yaṃ rājā samāyāto yasyaivaṃ varṇitā kathā .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
उषित्वा ते तु मुनयः सूतं गत्वाऽब्रुवन्निदम् ॥
सोऽयं राजा समायातो यस्यैवं वर्णिता कथा ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: Those sages, having dwelt [there], went to Sūta and said this: / “This is that king whose story has been described in this manner.

3.2.s:
vājimedhaṃ ca nṛpateḥ kārayāmastvadājñayā ..
bhavānhi cakratīrthe ca sthitvā dhyānaparo bhavet .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
वाजिमेधं च नृपतेः कारयामस्त्वदाज्ञया ॥
भवान्हि चक्रतीर्थे च स्थित्वा ध्यानपरो भवेत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: By your command we shall have the king perform a horse sacrifice. / You should remain at Cakratīrtha and be intent on meditation.”

3.2.s:
tathetyuktvā tu sūtastaiḥ sārdhaṃ ca punarāgamat ..
vidhinā kārayāmāsa hayamedhaṃ mahāmakham ..6..
3.2.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा तु सूतस्तैः सार्धं च पुनरागमत् ॥
विधिना कारयामास हयमेधं महामखम् ॥6॥
3.2.m: Saying “So be it,” Sūta returned along with them / and duly had him perform the horse sacrifice, the great rite.

3.2.s:
pūrve tu kapilasthānaṃ dakṣiṇe setubandhanam ..
paścime siṃdhunadyantaṃ cottare badarīvanam .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
पूर्वे तु कपिलस्थानं दक्षिणे सेतुबन्धनम् ॥
पश्चिमे सिंधुनद्यन्तं चोत्तरे बदरीवनम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: In the east, up to the place of Kapila; in the south, up to the Bridge; / in the west, up to the river Sindhu; and in the north, up to the Badarī forest;

3.2.s:
hayo jagāma tarasā tataḥ kṣiprāṃ nadīṃ gataḥ ..
tyaktvā kalevaraṃ vahnau svargalokamato yayau .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
हयो जगाम तरसा ततः क्षिप्रां नदीं गतः ॥
त्यक्त्वा कलेवरं वह्नौ स्वर्गलोकमतो ययौ ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: the horse went swiftly, and then went to the river Kṣiprā. / Abandoning its body in the fire, it then departed to the heavenly world.

3.2.s:
nṛpayajñe surāḥ sarve sapatnīkāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
caṃdramāstatra nāyāto bhūpatirvimanā abhūt ..9..
3.2.d:
नृपयज्ञे सुराः सर्वे सपत्नीकाः समागताः ॥
चंद्रमास्तत्र नायातो भूपतिर्विमना अभूत् ॥9॥
3.2.m: All the gods came with their wives to the king’s sacrifice. / Candramas did not come there, [and] the king became dejected.

3.2.s:
yajñāṃte vividhaṃ dānaṃ dattvā vaitālasaṃyutaḥ ..
caṃdralokaṃ gato rājā caṃdramāḥ sukhito'bhavat ..3.2.23.1 0..
3.2.d:
यज्ञांते विविधं दानं दत्त्वा वैतालसंयुतः ॥
चंद्रलोकं गतो राजा चंद्रमाः सुखितोऽभवत् ॥3.2.23.1 0॥
3.2.m: Having given various gifts at the conclusion of the sacrifice, accompanied by a vetāla, / the king went to Candraloka, and Candramas was pleased.

3.2.s:
bhobho rājanmahābhāga kalau prāpte bhayaṃkare ..
madgatirbhūtale nāsti tasmānnāyāmi te'ntikam .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
भोभो राजन्महाभाग कलौ प्राप्ते भयंकरे ॥
मद्गतिर्भूतले नास्ति तस्मान्नायामि तेऽन्तिकम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: “O illustrious king, now that the terrible Kali [age] has arrived, / I have no course upon the earth; therefore I do not come into your presence.”

3.2.s:
dattvā sudhāmayaṃ toyaṃ caṃdraścāntardadhe punaḥ ..
jñātvendrastatra saṃprāpya dvijarūpī hyayācayat ..12..
3.2.d:
दत्त्वा सुधामयं तोयं चंद्रश्चान्तर्दधे पुनः ॥
ज्ञात्वेन्द्रस्तत्र संप्राप्य द्विजरूपी ह्ययाचयत् ॥12॥
3.2.m: Having given water full of nectar, Candra disappeared once more. / Indra, learning of it, arrived there in the form of a twice-born and begged [for it].

3.2.s:
dattaṃ rājñā tadamṛtaṃ śakraḥ svargamumupāgataḥ ..
tena tasya phalaṃ jātamāyurlakṣa samaṃ hyabhūt..13..
3.2.d:
दत्तं राज्ञा तदमृतं शक्रः स्वर्गमुमुपागतः ॥
तेन तस्य फलं जातमायुर्लक्ष समं ह्यभूत्॥13॥
3.2.m: That nectar was given by the king, [and] Śakra went to heaven. / Through that, its fruit arose: his lifespan indeed became equal to a hundred thousand [years].

3.2.s:
tasminkāle dvijaḥ kaścijjayanto nāma viśrutaḥ ..
tatphalaṃ tapasā prāptaḥ śakrataḥ svargṛhaṃ yayau ..14..
3.2.d:
तस्मिन्काले द्विजः कश्चिज्जयन्तो नाम विश्रुतः ॥
तत्फलं तपसा प्राप्तः शक्रतः स्वर्गृहं ययौ ॥14॥
3.2.m: At that time a certain twice-born, celebrated by the name Jayanta, / having obtained that fruit from Śakra by asceticism, went to his own home.

3.2.s:
jayanto bhartṛharaye lakṣasvarṇena varṇayan ..
bhuktvā bhartṛharistatra yogārūḍho vanaṃ yayau ..15..
3.2.d:
जयन्तो भर्तृहरये लक्षस्वर्णेन वर्णयन् ॥
भुक्त्वा भर्तृहरिस्तत्र योगारूढो वनं ययौ ॥15॥
3.2.m: Jayanta, describing it to Bhartṛhari for a hundred thousand gold coins— / Bhartṛhari, having partaken of it there, ascended to yoga and went to the forest.

3.2.s:
vikramāditya evāsya rājyamakaṃṭakam..
śatavarṣaṃ mudāyukto jagāma maraṇe divam .. ..16..
3.2.d:
विक्रमादित्य एवास्य राज्यमकंटकम्॥
शतवर्षं मुदायुक्तो जगाम मरणे दिवम् ॥ ॥16॥
3.2.m: Vikramāditya alone [ruled] his thornless kingdom. / Endowed with joy for a hundred years, at his death he went to heaven.

3.2.s:
śaunakādyāstu ṛṣayo jñātvā bhūpasya svargatim ..
gatvā sūtaṃ praṇamyocurdharmaṃ mukhyaṃ vadādhunā .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
शौनकाद्यास्तु ऋषयो ज्ञात्वा भूपस्य स्वर्गतिम् ॥
गत्वा सूतं प्रणम्योचुर्धर्मं मुख्यं वदाधुना ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: The sages led by Śaunaka, learning of the king's departure to heaven, / went, bowed to the Sūta, and said: “Now tell [us] the foremost dharma.”

3.2.s:
tebhyaḥ sūtaḥ purāṇāni śrāvayāmāsa vai punaḥ ..
śatavarṣaṃ pañcalakṣaślokamadhyāpayanmudā ..
te śrutvā munayaḥ sarve jagmurhṛṣṭāḥ svamālayam .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
तेभ्यः सूतः पुराणानि श्रावयामास वै पुनः ॥
शतवर्षं पञ्चलक्षश्लोकमध्यापयन्मुदा ॥
ते श्रुत्वा मुनयः सर्वे जग्मुर्हृष्टाः स्वमालयम् ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: To them the Sūta indeed recited the Purāṇas again, / joyfully teaching five hundred thousand verses over a hundred years. / Having heard [them], all those sages departed rejoiced to their own abode.

3.2.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
ekadā naimiṣāraṇye ṛṣayaḥ śaunakādayaḥ ..
pṛcchanti vinayenaiva sūtaṃ paurāṇikaṃ khalu .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
एकदा नैमिषारण्ये ऋषयः शौनकादयः ॥
पृच्छन्ति विनयेनैव सूतं पौराणिकं खलु ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Vyāsa said: / Once in the Naimiṣa forest, the sages led by Śaunaka / indeed asked the Sūta, well-versed in the Purāṇas, with great humility:

3.2.s:
bhagavanbrūhi lokānāṃ hitārthāya caturyuge ..
kaḥ pūjyaḥ sevitavyaśca vāṃcchitārthapradāyakaḥ ..2..
3.2.d:
भगवन्ब्रूहि लोकानां हितार्थाय चतुर्युगे ॥
कः पूज्यः सेवितव्यश्च वांच्छितार्थप्रदायकः ॥2॥
3.2.m: “O venerable one, tell [us], for the benefit of the worlds in the four yugas: / Who is to be worshipped and served, the bestower of desired ends,

3.2.s:
vināyāsena vai kāmaṃ prāpnuyurmānavāḥ śubham ..
satyaṃ brahmanvadopāyaṃ narāṇāṃ kīrtikārakam ..3..
3.2.d:
विनायासेन वै कामं प्राप्नुयुर्मानवाः शुभम् ॥
सत्यं ब्रह्मन्वदोपायं नराणां कीर्तिकारकम् ॥3॥
3.2.m: by which men may obtain their auspicious desire without effort? / Truly, O holy one, tell the means that brings renown to men.”

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
navāṃbhojanetraṃ ramākelipātraṃ caturbāhucāmīkarācārugātram ..
jagattrāṇahetuṃ ripau dhūmraketuṃ sadā satyanārāyaṇaṃ staumi devam .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
नवांभोजनेत्रं रमाकेलिपात्रं चतुर्बाहुचामीकराचारुगात्रम् ॥
जगत्त्राणहेतुं रिपौ धूम्रकेतुं सदा सत्यनारायणं स्तौमि देवम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: The Sūta said: / “Whose eyes are like new lotuses, who is the vessel for Ramā’s amorous play, / with four arms and a body lovely as gold, / the cause of the world's protection, a comet of destruction to enemies— / I ever praise the god Satyanārāyaṇa.

3.2.s:
śrīrāmaṃ sahalakṣmaṇaṃ sakaruṇaṃ sītānvitaṃ
sāttvikaṃ vaidehīmukhapadmalubdhamadhupaṃ paulastyasaṃhārakam ..
vande vandyapadāṃbujaṃ suravaraṃ bhaktānukampākaraṃ
śatrughnena hanūmatā ca bharatenāsevitaṃ rāghavam .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
श्रीरामं सहलक्ष्मणं सकरुणं सीतान्वितं
सात्त्विकं वैदेहीमुखपद्मलुब्धमधुपं पौलस्त्यसंहारकम् ॥
वन्दे वन्द्यपदांबुजं सुरवरं भक्तानुकम्पाकरं
शत्रुघ्नेन हनूमता च भरतेनासेवितं राघवम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: I venerate glorious Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa, compassionate, accompanied by Sītā, / of sattva nature, a bee longing for the lotus-face of the Vaidehī, the destroyer of Pulastya’s descendant; / the supreme god whose lotus-feet are worthy of reverence, who shows mercy to his devotees, / the descendant of Raghu served by Śatrughna, Hanumat, and Bharata.

3.2.s:
kalikaluṣavināśaṃ kāmasiddhiprakāśaṃ suravaramukhabhāsaṃ bhūsureṇa prakāśam ..
vibudhabudhavilāsaṃ sādhucaryāviśeṣaṃ nṛpa tivaracaritraṃ bhoḥ śṛṇuṣvetihāsam .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
कलिकलुषविनाशं कामसिद्धिप्रकाशं सुरवरमुखभासं भूसुरेण प्रकाशम् ॥
विबुधबुधविलासं साधुचर्याविशेषं नृप तिवरचरित्रं भोः शृणुष्वेतिहासम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Which destroys the impurities of Kali, manifests the attainment of desires, / reflects the radiance of the foremost gods, and is revealed through the brahmins; / which is the delight of the learned and wise, a model of righteous conduct, / the history of the deeds of the best of kings—listen to this tale, O listener!”

3.2.s:
ekadā nārado yogī parānugrahavāṃcchayā ..
paryaṭanvividhām̐llokānmartyalokamupāgamat .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
एकदा नारदो योगी परानुग्रहवांच्छया ॥
पर्यटन्विविधाम्̐ल्लोकान्मर्त्यलोकमुपागमत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Once, the yogin Nārada, desiring to bestow grace on others, / wandering through various worlds, came to the world of mortals.

3.2.s:
tatra dṛṣṭvā janānsarvānnānākleśasamanvitān ..
ādhivyādhiyutānārtānpacyamānānsvakarmabhiḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा जनान्सर्वान्नानाक्लेशसमन्वितान् ॥
आधिव्याधियुतानार्तान्पच्यमानान्स्वकर्मभिः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: There he saw all people afflicted with manifold sufferings, / beset by mental and physical illnesses, distressed, cooking in [the fruits of] their own deeds.

3.2.s:
kenopāyena caiteṣāṃ duḥkhanāśo bhaveddhruvam..
iti sañciṃtya manasā viṣṇulokaṃ gatastadā .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
केनोपायेन चैतेषां दुःखनाशो भवेद्ध्रुवम्॥
इति सञ्चिंत्य मनसा विष्णुलोकं गतस्तदा ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: “By what means may their sorrow be surely destroyed?” / Thinking thus in his mind, he then went to the world of Viṣṇu.

3.2.s:
tatra nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ śuklavarṇaṃ caturbhujam ..
śaṃkhacakragadāpadmavanamālāvibhūṣitam .. 3.2.24.10 ..
3.2.d:
तत्र नारायणं देवं शुक्लवर्णं चतुर्भुजम् ॥
शंखचक्रगदापद्मवनमालाविभूषितम् ॥ 3.2.24.10 ॥
3.2.m: There [he saw] the god Nārāyaṇa, white in complexion, four-armed, / adorned with conch, discus, mace, lotus, and a garland of forest flowers,

3.2.s:
prasannavadanaṃ śāṃtaṃ sanakādyairabhiṣṭutam ..
dṛṣṭvā taṃ devadeveśaṃ stotuṃ samupacakrame .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
प्रसन्नवदनं शांतं सनकाद्यैरभिष्टुतम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा तं देवदेवेशं स्तोतुं समुपचक्रमे ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: with a gracious face, tranquil, praised by Sanaka and the other sages. / Seeing that lord of the gods, he began to praise him.

3.2.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
namo vāṅmanasātītarūpāyānaṃtaśaktaye ..
nādi madhyāntadevāya nirguṇāya mahātmane .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
॥ नारद उवाच ॥ ॥
नमो वाङ्मनसातीतरूपायानंतशक्तये ॥
नादि मध्यान्तदेवाय निर्गुणाय महात्मने ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: Nārada said: / “Obeisance to the one whose form transcends speech and mind, of boundless power, / the god who has no beginning, middle, or end, devoid of gunas, the Great Self,

3.2.s:
sarveṣāmādibhūtāya lokānāmupakāriṇe ..
apāraparimāṇāya tapodhāmne namonamaḥ .. 13 .. ..
3.2.d:
सर्वेषामादिभूताय लोकानामुपकारिणे ॥
अपारपरिमाणाय तपोधाम्ने नमोनमः ॥ 13 ॥ ॥
3.2.m: the source of all beings, the benefactor of the worlds, / of limitless measure, the abode of austerity—obeisance, obeisance [to you]!”

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā stutiṃ viṣṇurnāradaṃ pratyabhāṣata ..
kimarthamāgato'si tvaṃ ki te manasi vartate ..14..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा स्तुतिं विष्णुर्नारदं प्रत्यभाषत ॥
किमर्थमागतोऽसि त्वं कि ते मनसि वर्तते ॥14॥
3.2.m: The Sūta said: / Hearing this hymn of praise, Viṣṇu replied to Nārada: / “For what purpose have you come? What is in your mind?

3.2.s:
kathayasva mahābhāga tatsarvaṃ kathayāmi te ..
śrutvā tu nārado viṣṇumuktavānsarvakāraṇam .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
कथयस्व महाभाग तत्सर्वं कथयामि ते ॥
श्रुत्वा तु नारदो विष्णुमुक्तवान्सर्वकारणम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Speak, O illustrious one! I shall tell you all of that.” / Having heard [him], Nārada explained the entire reason to Viṣṇu.

3.2.s:
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sādhusādhvityapūjayat ..
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi vratamekaṃ sanātanam..16..
3.2.d:
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा साधुसाध्वित्यपूजयत् ॥
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि व्रतमेकं सनातनम्॥16॥
3.2.m: Hearing Nārada’s words, he commended them, saying, “Well done! Well done!” / “Listen, Nārada, I shall declare a single eternal vrata.

3.2.s:
kṛte tretāyuge viṣṇurdvāpare'nekarūpadhṛk ..
kalau pratyakṣaphaladaḥ satyanārāyaṇo vibhuḥ .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
कृते त्रेतायुगे विष्णुर्द्वापरेऽनेकरूपधृक् ॥
कलौ प्रत्यक्षफलदः सत्यनारायणो विभुः ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: In the Kṛta, Tretā, and Dvāpara yugas, Viṣṇu assumed manifold forms; / in the Kali [age], the all-pervading Satyanārāyaṇa bestows visible fruits.

3.2.s:
catuṣpādo hi dharmaśca tasya satyaṃ prasādhanam ..
satyena dhāryate lokaḥ satye brahma pratiṣṭhitam .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
चतुष्पादो हि धर्मश्च तस्य सत्यं प्रसाधनम् ॥
सत्येन धार्यते लोकः सत्ये ब्रह्म प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Dharma indeed has four feet, and truth is its adornment; / by truth the world is sustained; in truth Brahman is established.

3.2.s:
satyanārāyaṇavratamataḥ śreṣṭhatamaṃ smṛtam ..
iti śrutvā harervākyaṃ nāradaḥ punarabravīt .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यनारायणव्रतमतः श्रेष्ठतमं स्मृतम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा हरेर्वाक्यं नारदः पुनरब्रवीत् ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: Therefore the Satyanārāyaṇa vrata is regarded as the most excellent.” / Hearing this word of Hari, Nārada spoke again:

3.2.s:
kiṃ phalaṃ kiṃ vidhānaṃ ca satyanārāyaṇārcane ..
tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā deva kathayasva kṛpānidhe .. 3.2.24.20 ..
3.2.d:
किं फलं किं विधानं च सत्यनारायणार्चने ॥
तत्सर्वं कृपया देव कथयस्व कृपानिधे ॥ 3.2.24.20 ॥
3.2.m: “What is the fruit, and what is the procedure in worshipping Satyanārāyaṇa? / O god, treasure of compassion, kindly tell all that [to me].”

3.2.s:
.. bhagavānuvāca .. ..
nārāyaṇārcane vaktuṃ phalaṃ nālaṃ caturmukhaḥ ..
śṛṇu saṃkṣepato hyetatkathayāmi tavāgrataḥ .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
॥ भगवानुवाच ॥ ॥
नारायणार्चने वक्तुं फलं नालं चतुर्मुखः ॥
शृणु संक्षेपतो ह्येतत्कथयामि तवाग्रतः ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “Even the four-faced [Brahmā] is not capable of stating the fruit of worshipping Nārāyaṇa; / listen, I shall indeed declare it in brief before you.

3.2.s:
nirdhanopi dhanāḍhyaḥ syādaputraḥ putravānbhavet ..
bhraṣṭarājyo labhedrājyamandho'pi syātsulocanaḥ .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
निर्धनोपि धनाढ्यः स्यादपुत्रः पुत्रवान्भवेत् ॥
भ्रष्टराज्यो लभेद्राज्यमन्धोऽपि स्यात्सुलोचनः ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: Even a poor man would become wealthy; a childless man would obtain a son; / one who has lost his kingdom would regain his kingdom; even a blind man would have good sight.

3.2.s:
mucyate baṃdhanādbaddho nirbhayaḥ syādbhayāturaḥ ..
manasā kāmayedyaṃyaṃ labhate taṃ vidhānataḥ ..23..
3.2.d:
मुच्यते बंधनाद्बद्धो निर्भयः स्याद्भयातुरः ॥
मनसा कामयेद्यंयं लभते तं विधानतः ॥23॥
3.2.m: One who is bound is freed from bondage; one afflicted with fear becomes fearless; / whatever one desires in his mind, he obtains that according to the rule.

3.2.s:
iha janmani bho vipra bhaktyā ca vidhinārcayet ..
labhetkāmaṃ hi tacchīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 24 ..
3.2.d:
इह जन्मनि भो विप्र भक्त्या च विधिनार्चयेत् ॥
लभेत्कामं हि तच्छीघ्रं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 24 ॥
3.2.m: In this birth, O brahmin, should one worship with devotion and according to the rite, / he indeed obtains that desire quickly; no doubt should be entertained here.

3.2.s:
prātaḥsnāyī śucirbhūtvā daṃtadhāvanapūrva kam ..
tulasīmañjarīṃ dhṛtvā dhyāyetsatyasthitaṃ harim .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
प्रातःस्नायी शुचिर्भूत्वा दंतधावनपूर्व कम् ॥
तुलसीमञ्जरीं धृत्वा ध्यायेत्सत्यस्थितं हरिम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: Bathing in the morning and becoming pure, having first cleansed his teeth, / holding a shoot of tulasī, he should meditate on Hari abiding in truth:

3.2.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ sāṃdraghanāvadātaṃ caturbhujaṃ pītamahārhavāsasam ..
prasannavaktraṃ navakaṃjalocanaṃ sanandanādyairupasevitaṃ bhaje .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
नारायणं सांद्रघनावदातं चतुर्भुजं पीतमहार्हवाससम् ॥
प्रसन्नवक्त्रं नवकंजलोचनं सनन्दनाद्यैरुपसेवितं भजे ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: ‘I worship Nārāyaṇa, bright as a dense cloud, four-armed, dressed in precious yellow garments, / with a gracious face, eyes like fresh lotuses, served by Sanandana and the others.

3.2.s:
karomi te vrataṃ deva sāyaṃkāle tvadarcanam ..
śrutvā gāthāṃ tvadīyāṃ hi prasādaṃ te bhajāmyaham .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
करोमि ते व्रतं देव सायंकाले त्वदर्चनम् ॥
श्रुत्वा गाथां त्वदीयां हि प्रसादं ते भजाम्यहम् ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: O god, I undertake your vrata, your worship at eventide; / having heard your story, I partake of your consecrated food.’

3.2.s:
iti saṃkalpya manasā sāyaṃkāle prapūjayet ..
pañcabhiḥ kalaśairjuṣṭaṃ kadalītoraṇānvitam .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
इति संकल्प्य मनसा सायंकाले प्रपूजयेत् ॥
पञ्चभिः कलशैर्जुष्टं कदलीतोरणान्वितम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: Having made such a resolution in his mind, he should worship [him] at eventide / [at an altar] provided with five water jars and furnished with banana-tree arches.

3.2.s:
śālagrāmaṃ svarṇayuktaṃ pūjayedātmasūktakaiḥ ..
pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya candanādibhirarcayet .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
शालग्रामं स्वर्णयुक्तं पूजयेदात्मसूक्तकैः ॥
पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य चन्दनादिभिरर्चयेत् ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m: One should worship the Śālagrāma stone along with gold, using one’s own hymns; / having bathed it with the five nectars, one should worship it with sandalwood and other [offerings].”

3.2.s:
oṃnamo bhagavate nityaṃ satyadevāya dhīmahi ..
catuḥpadārthadātre ca namastubhyaṃ namonamaḥ .. 3.2.24.30 ..
3.2.d:
ओंनमो भगवते नित्यं सत्यदेवाय धीमहि ॥
चतुःपदार्थदात्रे च नमस्तुभ्यं नमोनमः ॥ 3.2.24.30 ॥
3.2.m:
"Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One! May we constantly meditate on the God of Truth,
and on the giver of the four aims of life. Homage to You, homage and homage!"

3.2.s:
japtavyaṣṭottaraśataṃ juhuyāttaddaśāṃśakam ..
tarpaṇaṃ mārjanaṃ kṛtvā kathāṃ śrutvā harerimām ..31..
3.2.d:
जप्तव्यष्टोत्तरशतं जुहुयात्तद्दशांशकम् ॥
तर्पणं मार्जनं कृत्वा कथां श्रुत्वा हरेरिमाम् ॥31॥
3.2.m:
One should recite [this mantra] one hundred and eight times, and offer one-tenth of that as an oblation.
Having performed libations and sprinkling, and having listened to this story of Hari,

3.2.s:
ṣaḍadhyāyīṃ satyamukhyāṃ tatpaścāttatprasādakam ..
samyagvibhajya tatsarvaṃ dāpayecchrotṛkāya ca .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
षडध्यायीं सत्यमुख्यां तत्पश्चात्तत्प्रसादकम् ॥
सम्यग्विभज्य तत्सर्वं दापयेच्छ्रोतृकाय च ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m:
comprising six chapters, foremost in truth, thereafter one should divide
all that consecrated food properly and distribute it to the listeners.

3.2.s:
ācāryāyādibhāgaṃ ca dvitīyaṃ svakulāya saḥ ..
śrotṛbhyaśca tṛtīyaṃ ca caturthaṃ cātmahetave .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
आचार्यायादिभागं च द्वितीयं स्वकुलाय सः ॥
श्रोतृभ्यश्च तृतीयं च चतुर्थं चात्महेतवे ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m:
He should give the first share to the teacher, the second to his own family,
the third to the listeners, and the fourth for his own sake.

3.2.s:
viprebhyo bhojanaṃ dadyātsvayaṃ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ ..
devarṣe'nena vidhinā satyanārāyaṇārcanam ..34..
3.2.d:
विप्रेभ्यो भोजनं दद्यात्स्वयं भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
देवर्षेऽनेन विधिना सत्यनारायणार्चनम् ॥34॥
3.2.m:
He should give food to the brāhmaṇas and eat himself, keeping his speech restrained.
O divine sage, according to this rite, the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa—

3.2.s:
kārayedyadi bhaktyā ca śraddhayā ca samanvitaḥ ..
vratī kāmānavāpnoti vāṃchitāniha janmani .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
कारयेद्यदि भक्त्या च श्रद्धया च समन्वितः ॥
व्रती कामानवाप्नोति वांछितानिह जन्मनि ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m:
if one causes it to be performed endowed with devotion and faith,
the observer of the votive observance attains the desires wished for in this life.

3.2.s:
iha janmakṛtaṃ karma parajanmani padyate ..
parajanmakṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ sarvadā naraiḥ .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
इह जन्मकृतं कर्म परजन्मनि पद्यते ॥
परजन्मकृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं सर्वदा नरैः ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m:
Action done in this life reaches into the next life;
action done in another life must always be experienced by men.

3.2.s:
satyanārāyaṇa vratamiha sarvānkāmāndadāti hi ..
adyaiva jagatīmadhye sthāpayāmi tvadājñayā .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यनारायण व्रतमिह सर्वान्कामान्ददाति हि ॥
अद्यैव जगतीमध्ये स्थापयामि त्वदाज्ञया ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m:
The votive observance of Satyanārāyaṇa indeed grants all desires in this world.
This very day, at your command, I establish it upon the earth.

3.2.s:
ityuktṃvā'tardadhe devo nāradaḥ svargatiṃ yayau ..
svayaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ kāśyāṃ puryāṃ samāgataḥ ..38..
satyanārāyaṇavratasya vaidika dṛṣṭikoṇam
satyanārāyaṇavratopari śrī hariśaṃkarajośīmahodayasya dṛṣṭikoṇam
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्ंवाऽतर्दधे देवो नारदः स्वर्गतिं ययौ ॥
स्वयं नारायणो देवः काश्यां पुर्यां समागतः ॥38॥
सत्यनारायणव्रतस्य वैदिक दृष्टिकोणम्
सत्यनारायणव्रतोपरि श्री हरिशंकरजोशीमहोदयस्य दृष्टिकोणम्
3.2.m:
Having spoken thus, the god vanished; Nārada went to heaven.
Lord Nārāyaṇa Himself came to the city of Kāśī.
The Vedic perspective on the votive observance of Satyanārāyaṇa
The perspective of Śrī Hariśaṅkara Jośī Mahodaya on the votive observance of Satyanārāyaṇa

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
kṛpayā brāhmaṇadvārā prakaṭīkṛtavānsvakam ..
itihāsamimaṃ vakṣye saṃvādaṃ hariviprayoḥ .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
कृपया ब्राह्मणद्वारा प्रकटीकृतवान्स्वकम् ॥
इतिहासमिमं वक्ष्ये संवादं हरिविप्रयोः ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m:
Sūta said:
Out of compassion, through the medium of a brāhmaṇa, He revealed His own
history, which I shall narrate—the dialogue between Hari and the brāhmaṇa.

3.2.s:
kāśīpurīti vikhyātā tatrāsīdbrāhmaṇo varaḥ ..
dīno gṛhāśramī nityaṃ bhikṣuḥ putrakalatravān .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
काशीपुरीति विख्याता तत्रासीद्ब्राह्मणो वरः ॥
दीनो गृहाश्रमी नित्यं भिक्षुः पुत्रकलत्रवान् ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m:
There was a renowned city named Kāśī. An excellent brāhmaṇa lived there,
poor, always a householder, a mendicant having a wife and children,

3.2.s:
śatānaṃda iti khyāto viṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ ..
ekadā pathi bhikṣārthaṃ gacchatastasya śrīpatiḥ .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
शतानंद इति ख्यातो विष्णुव्रतपरायणः ॥
एकदा पथि भिक्षार्थं गच्छतस्तस्य श्रीपतिः ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m:
renowned as Śatānanda, devoted to the votive observances of Viṣṇu.
Once, as he was walking along the path for the sake of alms, the Lord of Śrī,

3.2.s:
vinītasyātiśāṃtasya sa babhūvākṣigocaraḥ ..
vṛddhabrāhmaṇaveṣeṇa papraccha brāhmaṇaṃ hariḥ ..
kva yāsīti dvijaśreṣṭha vṛttiḥ kāmena kathyatām .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
विनीतस्यातिशांतस्य स बभूवाक्षिगोचरः ॥
वृद्धब्राह्मणवेषेण पप्रच्छ ब्राह्मणं हरिः ॥
क्व यासीति द्विजश्रेष्ठ वृत्तिः कामेन कथ्यताम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m:
became visible to the eyes of that humble and very peaceful man.
Assuming the guise of an old brāhmaṇa, Hari asked the brāhmaṇa:
"Where are you going, O best of the twice-born? What is your occupation? Tell me at once."

3.2.s:
.. śatānanda uvāca .. ..
bhikṣāvṛttirahaṃ saumya kalatrāpatyahetave ..
yācituṃ dhanināṃ dvāri vrajāmi dhanamuttamam .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
॥ शतानन्द उवाच ॥ ॥
भिक्षावृत्तिरहं सौम्य कलत्रापत्यहेतवे ॥
याचितुं धनिनां द्वारि व्रजामि धनमुत्तमम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
Śatānanda said:
"Gentle sir, I live by the occupation of begging for the sake of my wife and offspring.
I go to the door of wealthy men to beg for excellent wealth."

3.2.s:
.. nārāyaṇa uvāca .. ..
bhikṣāvṛttistvayā dīrghakālaṃ dvija sadā dhṛtā ..
tadvāraka upāyoyaṃ viśeṣeṇa kalau kila .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
॥ नारायण उवाच ॥ ॥
भिक्षावृत्तिस्त्वया दीर्घकालं द्विज सदा धृता ॥
तद्वारक उपायोयं विशेषेण कलौ किल ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
Nārāyaṇa said:
"The occupation of begging has been maintained by you for a long time, O twice-born.
There is a means to alleviate it, especially in the Kali age, they say.

3.2.s:
mamopadeśato vipra satyanārāyaṇaṃ bhaja ..
dāridryaśokaśamanaṃ saṃtāpaharaṇaṃ hareḥ ..
caraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāhi mokṣadaṃ padmalocanam .. .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
ममोपदेशतो विप्र सत्यनारायणं भज ॥
दारिद्र्यशोकशमनं संतापहरणं हरेः ॥
चरणं शरणं याहि मोक्षदं पद्मलोचनम् ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m:
By my instruction, O brāhmaṇa, worship Satyanārāyaṇa.
Go for refuge to the lotus-eyed Hari's foot, which grants liberation,
soothes poverty and sorrow, and removes distress."

3.2.s:
evaṃ saṃbodhito vipro hariṇā karuṇātmanā ..
punaḥ papraccha viprosau satyanārāyaṇo hi kaḥ .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
एवं संबोधितो विप्रो हरिणा करुणात्मना ॥
पुनः पप्रच्छ विप्रोसौ सत्यनारायणो हि कः ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m:
Thus addressed by compassionate Hari,
that brāhmaṇa asked again: "Who indeed is Satyanārāyaṇa?"

3.2.s:
.. vṛddhabrāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
bahu rūpaḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ sarvavyāpī nirañjanaḥ ..
idānīṃ viprarūpeṇa tava pratyakṣamāgataḥ .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
॥ वृद्धब्राह्मण उवाच ॥ ॥
बहु रूपः सत्यसंधः सर्वव्यापी निरञ्जनः ॥
इदानीं विप्ररूपेण तव प्रत्यक्षमागतः ॥ 9 ॥

3.2.s:
duḥkhodadhinimagnānāṃ taraṇiścaraṇau hareḥ ..
kuśalāḥ śaraṇaṃ yāṃti netare viṣayātmikāḥ .. 3.2.25.10 ..
3.2.d:
दुःखोदधिनिमग्नानां तरणिश्चरणौ हरेः ॥
कुशलाः शरणं यांति नेतरे विषयात्मिकाः ॥ 3.2.25.10 ॥
3.2.m:
The two feet of Hari are a boat for those drowned in the ocean of misery.
The wise take refuge in Him, not others whose nature is engrossed in sense-objects.

3.2.s:
āhṛtya pūjāsaṃbhārānhitāya jagatāṃ dvija ..
arcayaṃstamanudhyāyaṃstvametatprakaṭī kuru .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
आहृत्य पूजासंभारान्हिताय जगतां द्विज ॥
अर्चयंस्तमनुध्यायंस्त्वमेतत्प्रकटी कुरु ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m:
Having collected the worship materials for the welfare of the worlds, O twice-born,
worshipping and constantly meditating upon Him, make this [rite] known."

3.2.s:
iti bruvaṃtaṃ viprosau dadarśa puruṣottamam ..
jaladaśyāmalaṃ cārucaturbāhuṃ gadādibhiḥ .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
इति ब्रुवंतं विप्रोसौ ददर्श पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
जलदश्यामलं चारुचतुर्बाहुं गदादिभिः ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
As he spoke thus, the brāhmaṇa beheld the Supreme Person,
dark as a rain-cloud, charming, with four arms bearing a mace and other [weapons],

3.2.s:
pītāṃbaraṃ navāṃbhojalocanaṃ smitapūrvakam ..
vanamālāmadhuvrāta cuṃbitāṃgrisaroruham .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
पीतांबरं नवांभोजलोचनं स्मितपूर्वकम् ॥
वनमालामधुव्रात चुंबितांग्रिसरोरुहम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m:
wearing yellow garments, with eyes like fresh lotus flowers, smiling,
His lotus-feet kissed by a swarm of bees [attracted to] His woodland garland.

3.2.s:
niśamya pulakāṃgosau premapūrṇasulocanaḥ ..
stuvangadgadayā vācā daṃḍavatpatito bhuvi .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
निशम्य पुलकांगोसौ प्रेमपूर्णसुलोचनः ॥
स्तुवन्गद्गदया वाचा दंडवत्पतितो भुवि ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m:
Having perceived [Him], his limbs bristling with joy, his fair eyes filled with love,
praising Him with a voice faltering with emotion, he fell to the ground like a rod:

3.2.s:
praṇamāmi jagannātha jagatkāraṇakārakam ..
anāthanāthaṃ śivadaṃ śaraṇyamanaghaṃ śucim .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
प्रणमामि जगन्नाथ जगत्कारणकारकम् ॥
अनाथनाथं शिवदं शरण्यमनघं शुचिम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m:
"I bow to the Lord of the universe, the cause of the causes of the universe,
the Lord of the helpless, the bestower of welfare, the refuge, the sinless, the pure,

3.2.s: avyaktaṃ vyaktatāṃ yātaṃ tāpatrayavimocanam .. 16 ..
3.2.d: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ततां यातं तापत्रयविमोचनम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: the unmanifest manifest, the deliverer from the threefold misery!

3.2.s:
namaḥ satya nārāyaṇāyāsya kartre namaḥ śuddhasattvāya viśvasya bhartre ..
karālāya kālāya viśvasya hartre namaste jaganmaṅgalāyātmamūrte .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
नमः सत्य नारायणायास्य कर्त्रे नमः शुद्धसत्त्वाय विश्वस्य भर्त्रे ॥
करालाय कालाय विश्वस्य हर्त्रे नमस्ते जगन्मङ्गलायात्ममूर्ते ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m:
Homage to Satyanārāyaṇa, the creator of this [world]; homage to the embodiment of pure sattva, the maintainer of the universe;
homage to dreadful Time, the destroyer of the universe; homage to You, the auspiciousness of the world, whose form is the self!

3.2.s:
dhanyosmyadya kṛtī dhanyo bhavodya saphalo mama ..
vāṅmanogocaro yastvaṃ mama pratyakṣamāgataḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
धन्योस्म्यद्य कृती धन्यो भवोद्य सफलो मम ॥
वाङ्मनोगोचरो यस्त्वं मम प्रत्यक्षमागतः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m:
Blessed am I today, successful and fortunate; my life has become fruitful today,
in that You, who are beyond speech and mind, have come before my eyes.

3.2.s:
diṣṭaṃ kiṃ varṇayāmyāho na jāne kasya vā phalam ..
kriyāhīnasya mandasya deho'yaṃ phalavānkṛtaḥ .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
दिष्टं किं वर्णयाम्याहो न जाने कस्य वा फलम् ॥
क्रियाहीनस्य मन्दस्य देहोऽयं फलवान्कृतः ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m:
How can I describe my destiny, or indeed whose fruit this is, I know not!
This body of a fool devoid of ritual action has been made fruitful.

3.2.s:
pūjanaṃ ca prakartavyaṃ lokanātha ramāpate ..
vidhinā kena kṛpayā tadājñāpaya māṃ vibho .. .. 3.2.25.20 ..
3.2.d:
पूजनं च प्रकर्तव्यं लोकनाथ रमापते ॥
विधिना केन कृपया तदाज्ञापय मां विभो ॥ ॥ 3.2.25.20 ॥
3.2.m:
And worship is to be performed, O Lord of the world, O Lord of Ramā;
by what rite? Mercifully command me concerning that, O omnipresent Lord!"

3.2.s:
haristamāha madhuraṃ sasmitaṃ viśvamohanaḥ ..
pūjāyāṃ mama viprendra bahu nāpekṣitaṃ dhanam .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
हरिस्तमाह मधुरं सस्मितं विश्वमोहनः ॥
पूजायां मम विप्रेन्द्र बहु नापेक्षितं धनम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m:
Hari, the enchantress of the universe, said to him sweetly and with a smile:
"In My worship, O chief of brāhmaṇas, much wealth is not required.

3.2.s:
anāyāsena labdhena śraddhāmātreṇa māṃ yaja ..
grāhagrastojāmilo vā yathā'bhūnmuktasaṃkaṭaḥ .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
अनायासेन लब्धेन श्रद्धामात्रेण मां यज ॥
ग्राहग्रस्तोजामिलो वा यथाऽभून्मुक्तसंकटः ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
Worship Me with whatever is obtained without strain, merely through faith,
just as [the elephant] seized by the crocodile, or Ajāmila, became freed from distress.

3.2.s:
vidhānaṃ śṛṇu viprendra manasā kāmayetphalam ..
pūjāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ pūjāṃ kuryādyathā vidhi ..23..
3.2.d:
विधानं शृणु विप्रेन्द्र मनसा कामयेत्फलम् ॥
पूजासंभृतसंभारः पूजां कुर्याद्यथा विधि ॥23॥
3.2.m:
Hear the ritual rule, O chief of brāhmaṇas: one should desire the fruit in one's mind;
having assembled the worship materials, one should perform the worship according to rule.

3.2.s:
godhūmacūrṇaṃ pādārddhaṃ seṭakādipramāṇataḥ ..
dugdhena tāvatā yuktaṃ miśritaṃ śarkarādibhiḥ ..24..
3.2.d:
गोधूमचूर्णं पादार्द्धं सेटकादिप्रमाणतः ॥
दुग्धेन तावता युक्तं मिश्रितं शर्करादिभिः ॥24॥
3.2.m:
Wheat flour measuring half of a quarter-part, according to the standard of a seṭaka and so forth,
joined with an equal amount of milk, mixed with sugar and other [sweeteners]—

3.2.s:
taccūrṇaṃ haraye dadyād ghṛtayuktaṃ haripriyam..
godugdhenaiva dadhinā goghṛtena samanvitam .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
तच्चूर्णं हरये दद्याद् घृतयुक्तं हरिप्रियम्॥
गोदुग्धेनैव दधिना गोघृतेन समन्वितम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m:
one should offer to Hari that flour mixed with ghee, dear to Hari;
provided with cow's milk itself, curd, and cow's ghee,

3.2.s:
gaṃgājalena madhunā yuktaṃ pañcāmṛtaṃ priyam ..
pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya śālagrāmodbhavāṃ śilām .. .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
गंगाजलेन मधुना युक्तं पञ्चामृतं प्रियम् ॥
पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य शालग्रामोद्भवां शिलाम् ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m:
joined with Ganges water and honey, making the beloved fivefold nectar.
Having bathed the stone originating from the Śālagrāma with the fivefold nectar,

3.2.s:
gandhapuṣpādinaivedyairvedavādairmanoharaiḥ ..
dhūpairdīpaiśca naivedyaistāṃbūlādibhirarcayet .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिनैवेद्यैर्वेदवादैर्मनोहरैः ॥
धूपैर्दीपैश्च नैवेद्यैस्तांबूलादिभिरर्चयेत् ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m:
one should worship it with sandal, flowers, and the like, with food-offerings, with delightful Vedic recitations,
with incenses, lamps, food-offerings, and betel and other [presents].

3.2.s:
miṣṭānnapānasanmānairbhakṣyairbhojyaiḥ phalaistathā ..
ṛtukālodbhavaiḥ puṣpaiḥ pūjayedbhaktitatparaḥ .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
मिष्टान्नपानसन्मानैर्भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैः फलैस्तथा ॥
ऋतुकालोद्भवैः पुष्पैः पूजयेद्भक्तितत्परः ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m:
With honors of sweet food and drink, with edibles, foodstuffs, and fruits,
and with seasonal flowers, devoted to devotion, one should worship [Him].

3.2.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ svajanaiścaiva veṣṭitaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
tvayā sārddhaṃ mama kathāṃ śṛṇuyātparamādarāt .. .. 29 ..
3.2.d:
ब्राह्मणैः स्वजनैश्चैव वेष्टितः श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
त्वया सार्द्धं मम कथां शृणुयात्परमादरात् ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
3.2.m:
Surrounded by brāhmaṇas and one's own kinsmen, endowed with faith,
one should listen with supreme reverence to My story along with you,

3.2.s:
itihāsaṃ tathā rājño bhillānāṃ vaṇijo'sya ca ..
kathāṃte praṇamedbhaktyā prasādaṃ vibhajettataḥ .. 3.2.25.30 ..
3.2.d:
इतिहासं तथा राज्ञो भिल्लानां वणिजोऽस्य च ॥
कथांते प्रणमेद्भक्त्या प्रसादं विभजेत्ततः ॥ 3.2.25.30 ॥
3.2.m:
and also the history of the king, the Bhillas, and this merchant.
At the end of the story, one should bow with devotion, and then distribute the consecrated food.

3.2.s:
labdhaṃ prasādaṃ bhuṃjīta mānayanna vicārayet ..
dravyādibhirna me śāṃtirbhaktyā kevalayā yathā .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
लब्धं प्रसादं भुंजीत मानयन्न विचारयेत् ॥
द्रव्यादिभिर्न मे शांतिर्भक्त्या केवलया यथा ॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m:
One should consume the consecrated food obtained, honoring it without hesitation.
My satisfaction does not come through material goods and the like as it does through pure devotion."

3.2.s:
vidhi?nānena viprendra pūjayaṃti ca ye narāḥ ..
putrapautradhanairyuktā bhuktvā bhogāna nuttamān .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
विधि?नानेन विप्रेन्द्र पूजयंति च ये नराः ॥
पुत्रपौत्रधनैर्युक्ता भुक्त्वा भोगान नुत्तमान् ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: And whatever men worship according to this rite, O best of brahmins, / endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth, having enjoyed the highest pleasures,

3.2.s:
ante sānnidhyamāsādya modante te mayā saha ..
yaṃyaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ suvratī taṃtamāpnuyāt .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
अन्ते सान्निध्यमासाद्य मोदन्ते ते मया सह ॥
यंयं कामयते कामं सुव्रती तंतमाप्नुयात् ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: in the end they attain proximity and rejoice with me. / Whatever desire the observer of good vows desires, that he shall obtain.

3.2.s:
ityuktvāntardadhe viṣṇurvipropi sukhamāptavān ..
praṇamyāgādyathādiṣṭaṃ manasā kautukākulaḥ .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे विष्णुर्विप्रोपि सुखमाप्तवान् ॥
प्रणम्यागाद्यथादिष्टं मनसा कौतुकाकुलः ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu vanished, and the brahmin too found happiness. / Having bowed, he went away as instructed, his mind full of wonder.

3.2.s:
adya bhaikṣyeṇa labhyena pūjyo nārāyaṇo mayā ..
iti niścitya manasā bhikṣārthī nagaraṃ gataḥ .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
अद्य भैक्ष्येण लभ्येन पूज्यो नारायणो मया ॥
इति निश्चित्य मनसा भिक्षार्थी नगरं गतः ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: “Today Nārāyaṇa must be worshipped by me with the alms I obtain.” / Having resolved thus in his mind, he went to the city seeking alms.

3.2.s:
vinā dehīti vacanaṃ labdhā ca vipulaṃ dhanam ..
kautukāyāsamanasā jagāma nijamālayam .. 36..
3.2.d:
विना देहीति वचनं लब्धा च विपुलं धनम् ॥
कौतुकायासमनसा जगाम निजमालयम् ॥ 36॥
3.2.m: Without even saying the word “give,” he obtained abundant wealth. / With a mind free of weariness and full of wonder, he went to his own home.

3.2.s:
vṛttāṃtaṃ sarvamācakhyau brāhmaṇī sānvamodata ..
sādaraṃ dravyasaṃbhāramāhṛtya bharturājñayā .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
वृत्तांतं सर्वमाचख्यौ ब्राह्मणी सान्वमोदत ॥
सादरं द्रव्यसंभारमाहृत्य भर्तुराज्ञया ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m: He related the whole incident, and his brahmin wife agreed. / Respectfully gathering the collection of materials by her husband's command,

3.2.s:
āhūya bandhumitrāṇi tathā sānnidhyavartinaḥ ..
satyanārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ yajāmi svagaṇairvṛtaḥ .. 38 ..
3.2.d:
आहूय बन्धुमित्राणि तथा सान्निध्यवर्तिनः ॥
सत्यनारायणं देवं यजामि स्वगणैर्वृतः ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: and calling relatives, friends, as well as those living nearby, [he said:] / “Surrounded by my own folk, I worship the god Satyanārāyaṇa.”

3.2.s:
bhaktyā tutoṣa bhagavānsatyanārāyaṇaḥ svayam ..
kāmaṃ ditsuḥ prādurāsītkathāṃte bhaktavatsalaḥ .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
भक्त्या तुतोष भगवान्सत्यनारायणः स्वयम् ॥
कामं दित्सुः प्रादुरासीत्कथांते भक्तवत्सलः ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m: The Lord Satyanārāyaṇa was himself pleased by his devotion. / Wishing to grant his desire, he who is fond of his devotees became manifest at the end of the story.

3.2.s:
vavre vipro'bhilaṣitamihāmutra sukhapradam ..
bhaktiṃ parāṃ bhagavati tathā tatsaṃgināṃ vratam .. 3.2.25.40 ..
3.2.d:
वव्रे विप्रोऽभिलषितमिहामुत्र सुखप्रदम् ॥
भक्तिं परां भगवति तथा तत्संगिनां व्रतम् ॥ 3.2.25.40 ॥
3.2.m: The brahmin chose what he desired, which grants happiness in this world and the next: / supreme devotion to the Lord, and likewise the vow for his companions.

3.2.s:
rathaṃ kuñjaraṃ maṃjulaṃ mandiraṃ ca hayaṃ cāru cāmī karālaṃ kṛtaṃ ca ..
dhanaṃ dāsadāsīgaṇaṃ gāṃ mahīṃ ca lulāyāḥ sadugdhā hare dehi dāsyam ..41..
3.2.d:
रथं कुञ्जरं मंजुलं मन्दिरं च हयं चारु चामी करालं कृतं च ॥
धनं दासदासीगणं गां महीं च लुलायाः सदुग्धा हरे देहि दास्यम् ॥41॥
3.2.m: “A chariot, an elephant, a charming palace, a beautiful horse adorned with gold, / wealth, a host of male and female slaves, cattle, land, and milch buffaloes—O Hari, give me servitude [to you]!”

3.2.s:
tathāstviti hariḥ prāha tataścāṃtardadhe prabhuḥ ..
vipro'pikṛta kṛtyo'bhūtsarve lokā visismire ..42..
3.2.d:
तथास्त्विति हरिः प्राह ततश्चांतर्दधे प्रभुः ॥
विप्रोऽपिकृत कृत्योऽभूत्सर्वे लोका विसिस्मिरे ॥42॥
3.2.m: “So be it,” said Hari, and then the Lord vanished. / The brahmin too achieved his goal, and all the people were astonished.

3.2.s:
praṇamya bhuvi kāyena prasādaṃ prāpurādarāt ..
svaṃsvaṃ dhāma samājagmurdhanyadhanyeti vādinaḥ .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
प्रणम्य भुवि कायेन प्रसादं प्रापुरादरात् ॥
स्वंस्वं धाम समाजग्मुर्धन्यधन्येति वादिनः ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m: Bowing on the ground with their bodies, they respectfully received the prasāda. / They went to their respective homes, crying, “Blessed! Blessed!”

3.2.s:
pracacāra tato loke satyanārāyaṇārcanam ..
kāmasiddhipradaṃ muktibhuktidaṃ kaluṣāpaham ..44..
3.2.d:
प्रचचार ततो लोके सत्यनारायणार्चनम् ॥
कामसिद्धिप्रदं मुक्तिभुक्तिदं कलुषापहम् ॥44॥
3.2.m: Thenceforth the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa became widespread in the world, / granting the accomplishment of desires, giving liberation and worldly enjoyment, and removing sins.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
rājāsīddhārmikaḥ kaścitkedāramaṇipūrake ..
candracūḍa iti khyātaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
राजासीद्धार्मिकः कश्चित्केदारमणिपूरके ॥
चन्द्रचूड इति ख्यातः प्रजापालनतत्परः ॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / There was a righteous king in Kedāramaṇipūraka, / known as Candracūḍa, dedicated to the protection of his subjects.

3.2.s:
śāṃto madhuravāgdhīro nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ..
babhūvuḥ śatravastasya mlecchā viṃdhyanivāsinaḥ ..2..
3.2.d:
शांतो मधुरवाग्धीरो नारायणपरायणः॥
बभूवुः शत्रवस्तस्य म्लेच्छा विंध्यनिवासिनः ॥2॥
3.2.m: He was tranquil, gentle of speech, steadfast, and devoted to Nārāyaṇa. / His enemies were the Mlecchas dwelling in the Vindhya mountains.

3.2.s:
tasya tairavabhavadyuddhamatiprabaladāruṇaiḥ..
bhuśuṃḍīyuddhanipuṇaiḥ kṣepaṇaiḥ parighāyudhaiḥ ..3..
3.2.d:
तस्य तैरवभवद्युद्धमतिप्रबलदारुणैः॥
भुशुंडीयुद्धनिपुणैः क्षेपणैः परिघायुधैः ॥3॥
3.2.m: A battle took place between him and those extremely powerful and fierce [foes], / who were skilled in fighting with bhuśuṇḍīs, with sling-stones, and armed with iron clubs.

3.2.s:
candracūḍasya mahatī senā yamapure gatā..
śataṃ rathāstathā nāgāsahasraṃ tu hayāstathā..4..
3.2.d:
चन्द्रचूडस्य महती सेना यमपुरे गता॥
शतं रथास्तथा नागासहस्रं तु हयास्तथा॥4॥
3.2.m: Candracūḍa's great army went to Yama's abode: / a hundred chariots, likewise elephants, and a thousand horses.

3.2.s:
pattayaḥ paṃcasāhasrā mṛtāḥ svargapuraṃ yayuḥ ..
dasyavaḥ paṃcasāhasrā mṛtāḥ kaitavayodhinaḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
पत्तयः पंचसाहस्रा मृताः स्वर्गपुरं ययुः ॥
दस्यवः पंचसाहस्रा मृताः कैतवयोधिनः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: Five thousand foot-soldiers died and went to heaven; / five thousand bandits fighting deceitfully died.

3.2.s:
ākrāṃtaḥ sa mahābhāgastairmlecchairdaṃbhayodhibhiḥ ..
tyaktvā rāṣṭraṃ ca nagaraṃ saikākī vanamāyayau .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
आक्रांतः स महाभागस्तैर्म्लेच्छैर्दंभयोधिभिः ॥
त्यक्त्वा राष्ट्रं च नगरं सैकाकी वनमाययौ ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Overpowered by those Mlecchas fighting with deceit, / that fortunate king abandoned his realm and city and went alone to the forest.

3.2.s:
tīrthavyājena sa nṛpaḥ purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgataḥ ..
tatra nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ vaṃdyaṃ sarvagṛhegṛhe .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
तीर्थव्याजेन स नृपः पुरीं काशीं समागतः ॥
तत्र नारायणं देवं वंद्यं सर्वगृहेगृहे ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Under the pretext of a pilgrimage, the king arrived at the city of Kāśī. / There the god Nārāyaṇa was worshipped in every house.

3.2.s:
dadarśa nagarīṃ caiva dhanadhānyasamanvitām ..
yathā dvārāvatī jñeyā tathā sā ca purī śubhā .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
ददर्श नगरीं चैव धनधान्यसमन्विताम् ॥
यथा द्वारावती ज्ञेया तथा सा च पुरी शुभा ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: And he saw a city endowed with wealth and grain; / just as Dvārāvatī is known, so too was that auspicious city.

3.2.s:
vismitaścaṃdracūḍaśca dṛṣṭvāścaryamanuttamam ..
satyena rodhitāṃ lakṣmīṃ śīladharmasamanvitām.. 9 ..
3.2.d:
विस्मितश्चंद्रचूडश्च दृष्ट्वाश्चर्यमनुत्तमम् ॥
सत्येन रोधितां लक्ष्मीं शीलधर्मसमन्विताम्॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: And Candracūḍa was astonished, having seen this matchless wonder: / fortune restrained by truth, accompanied by good conduct and righteousness.

3.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā śrutvā sadānaṃdaṃ satyadevaprapūjakam ..
patitvā taccaraṇayoḥ praṇanāma mudā yutaḥ .. 3.2.26.10 ..
3.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा सदानंदं सत्यदेवप्रपूजकम् ॥
पतित्वा तच्चरणयोः प्रणनाम मुदा युतः ॥ 3.2.26.10 ॥
3.2.m: Having seen and heard of Sadānanda, a devout worshipper of the true God, / he fell at his feet and bowed down, filled with joy:

3.2.s:
dvijarāja namastubhyaṃ sadānaṃda mahāmate ..
bhraṣṭarājyaṃ ca māṃ jñātvā kṛpayā māṃ samuddhara .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
द्विजराज नमस्तुभ्यं सदानंद महामते ॥
भ्रष्टराज्यं च मां ज्ञात्वा कृपया मां समुद्धर ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: “O best of the twice-born, homage to you, O noble-minded Sadānanda! / Knowing me to have fallen from my kingdom, graciously deliver me!

3.2.s:
yathā prasanno bhagavām̐llakṣmīkānto janārdanaḥ ..
tathā tadvada yadyogyaṃ vrataṃ pāpapraṇāśanam .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
यथा प्रसन्नो भगवाम्̐ल्लक्ष्मीकान्तो जनार्दनः ॥
तथा तद्वद यद्योग्यं व्रतं पापप्रणाशनम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: Explain that proper vow which destroys sins, / in such a way that the blessed Janārdana, the beloved of Lakṣmī, may be pleased.”

3.2.s:
.. sadānaṃda uvāca .. ..
duḥkhaśokādiśamanaṃ dhanadhānyapravardhanam ..
saubhāgyasaṃtatikaraṃ sarvatra vijayapradam .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सदानंद उवाच ॥ ॥
दुःखशोकादिशमनं धनधान्यप्रवर्धनम् ॥
सौभाग्यसंततिकरं सर्वत्र विजयप्रदम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Sadānanda said: / “The vow of Satyanārāyaṇa alleviates grief, sorrow, and the like, increases wealth and grain, / brings good fortune and offspring, and grants victory everywhere;

3.2.s:
satyanārāyaṇavrataṃ śrīpatestuṣṭikārakam ..
yasminkasmindine bhūpa yajeccaiva niśāmukhe .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यनारायणव्रतं श्रीपतेस्तुष्टिकारकम् ॥
यस्मिन्कस्मिन्दिने भूप यजेच्चैव निशामुखे ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: it causes satisfaction to the Lord of Śrī. / On whatever day, O king, one should worship [him] at nightfall.

3.2.s:
toraṇādi prakartavyaṃ kadalīstaṃbhamaṃḍitam ..
paṃcabhiḥ kalaśairyuktaṃ dhvajapaṃcasamanvitam ..15..
3.2.d:
तोरणादि प्रकर्तव्यं कदलीस्तंभमंडितम् ॥
पंचभिः कलशैर्युक्तं ध्वजपंचसमन्वितम् ॥15॥
3.2.m: An archway and the like should be constructed, adorned with plantain trunks, / furnished with five water-pots, and provided with five banners.

3.2.s:
tanmadhye vedikāṃ ramyāṃ kārayetsa vratī dvijaiḥ ..
tatra sthāpya śilārūpaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ svarṇa samanvitam ..16..
3.2.d:
तन्मध्ये वेदिकां रम्यां कारयेत्स व्रती द्विजैः ॥
तत्र स्थाप्य शिलारूपं कृष्णं स्वर्ण समन्वितम् ॥16॥
3.2.m: In the middle of that, the observer of the vow should have a charming altar made by brahmins; / having installed there Kṛṣṇa in the form of a [śālagrāma] stone, accompanied by gold,

3.2.s:
kuryādgaṃdhādibhiḥ pūjāṃ premabhaktisamanvitaḥ..
bhūmiśāyī hariṃ dhyāyansaptarātraṃ vyatītayet ..17..
3.2.d:
कुर्याद्गंधादिभिः पूजां प्रेमभक्तिसमन्वितः॥
भूमिशायी हरिं ध्यायन्सप्तरात्रं व्यतीतयेत् ॥17॥
3.2.m: he should perform worship with fragrances and the like, endowed with loving devotion. / Sleeping on the ground and meditating on Hari, he should spend seven nights.

3.2.s:
iti śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ kāśyāṃ devamapūjayat ..
rātrau prasanno bhagavāndadau rājñe'simuttamam .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
इति श्रुत्वा स नृपतिः काश्यां देवमपूजयत् ॥
रात्रौ प्रसन्नो भगवान्ददौ राज्ञेऽसिमुत्तमम् ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Having heard this, the king worshipped the god in Kāśī. / Pleased at night, the Lord gave an excellent sword to the king.

3.2.s:
śatrupakṣakṣayakaraṃ prāpya khaṅgaṃ nṛpottamaḥ ..
praṇamya ca sadānandaṃ kedāramaṇimā yayau .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
शत्रुपक्षक्षयकरं प्राप्य खङ्गं नृपोत्तमः ॥
प्रणम्य च सदानन्दं केदारमणिमा ययौ ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: Having obtained the sword that destroys the enemy's side, that best of kings / bowed to Sadānanda and went to Kedāramaṇi.

3.2.s:
hatvā dasyūnṣaṣṭiśatāṃsteṣāṃ labdhvā mahaddhanam ..
hariṃ prapūjayāmāsa narmadāyāstaṭe śubhe ..3.2.26.20..
3.2.d:
हत्वा दस्यून्षष्टिशतांस्तेषां लब्ध्वा महद्धनम् ॥
हरिं प्रपूजयामास नर्मदायास्तटे शुभे ॥3.2.26.20॥
3.2.m: Having slain six thousand bandits and obtained their great wealth, / he worshipped Hari on the auspicious bank of the Narmadā.

3.2.s:
paurṇamāsyāṃ vidhānena māsimāsi nṛpottamaḥ..
apūjayatsatyadevaṃ premabhaktisamanvitaḥ..21..
3.2.d:
पौर्णमास्यां विधानेन मासिमासि नृपोत्तमः॥
अपूजयत्सत्यदेवं प्रेमभक्तिसमन्वितः॥21॥
3.2.m: According to the injunctions, on the full-moon day month after month, that best of kings / worshipped the true God, endowed with loving devotion.

3.2.s:
tadvratasya prabhāvena lakṣagrāmādhipo'bhavat..
rājyaṃ kṛtvā sa ṣaṣṭyabdamante viṣṇupuraṃ yayau..22..
3.2.d:
तद्व्रतस्य प्रभावेन लक्षग्रामाधिपोऽभवत्॥
राज्यं कृत्वा स षष्ट्यब्दमन्ते विष्णुपुरं ययौ॥22॥
3.2.m: By the power of that vow he became ruler over a hundred thousand villages. / Having ruled the kingdom for sixty years, in the end he went to Viṣṇu's abode.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
athetihāsaṃ śṛṇuta yathā bhillāḥ kṛtārthinaḥ ..
vicaraṃto vane nityaṃ niṣādāḥ kāṣṭhavāhinaḥ ..1..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
अथेतिहासं शृणुत यथा भिल्लाः कृतार्थिनः ॥
विचरंतो वने नित्यं निषादाः काष्ठवाहिनः ॥1॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Now hear the history of how the Bhillas attained their purpose, / Niṣādas who always roamed in the forest carrying firewood.

3.2.s:
vanātkāṣṭhāni vikretuṃ purīṃ kāśīṃ yayuḥ kvacit..
ekastṛṣākulo yāto viṣṇudāsāśramaṃ tadā ..2..
3.2.d:
वनात्काष्ठानि विक्रेतुं पुरीं काशीं ययुः क्वचित्॥
एकस्तृषाकुलो यातो विष्णुदासाश्रमं तदा ॥2॥
3.2.m: Once they went from the forest to the city of Kāśī to sell firewood. / One of them, overcome by thirst, then went to Viṣṇudāsa's hermitage.

3.2.s:
dadarśa vipulaiśvaryaṃ sevitaṃ ca dvijairharim ..
jalaṃ pītvā vismito'bhūdbhikṣukasya kuto dhanam..3..
3.2.d:
ददर्श विपुलैश्वर्यं सेवितं च द्विजैर्हरिम् ॥
जलं पीत्वा विस्मितोऽभूद्भिक्षुकस्य कुतो धनम्॥3॥
3.2.m: He saw abundant wealth and Hari served by brahmins. / Having drunk water, he was amazed: 'From where does a beggar get wealth?

3.2.s:
yo dṛṣṭo'kiṃcano vipro dṛśyate'dya mahādhanaḥ..
iti saṃciṃtya hṛdaye sa papraccha dvijottamam..4..
3.2.d:
यो दृष्टोऽकिंचनो विप्रो दृश्यतेऽद्य महाधनः॥
इति संचिंत्य हृदये स पप्रच्छ द्विजोत्तमम्॥4॥
3.2.m: The brahmin who was seen as destitute is today seen as very wealthy.' / Reflecting thus in his heart, he questioned the best of brahmins:

3.2.s:
aiśvaryaṃ te kuto brahmandurgatiste kuto gatā ..
ājñāpaya mahābhāga śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
ऐश्वर्यं ते कुतो ब्रह्मन्दुर्गतिस्ते कुतो गता ॥
आज्ञापय महाभाग श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: “From where is your prosperity, O brahmin? Where has your misfortune gone? / Command me, O fortunate one, I wish to hear according to reality.”

3.2.s:
.. sadānaṃda uvāca .. ..
satyanārāyaṇasyāṃga sevayā kiṃ na labhyate ..
na kiṃcitsukhamāpnoti vinā tasyānukaṃpayā .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सदानंद उवाच ॥ ॥
सत्यनारायणस्यांग सेवया किं न लभ्यते ॥
न किंचित्सुखमाप्नोति विना तस्यानुकंपया ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: Sadānanda said: / “Dear one, what is not obtained through the service of Satyanārāyaṇa? / Without his compassion, one attains no happiness whatsoever.”

3.2.s:
..niṣāda uvāca .. ..
aho kimiti māhātmyaṃ satyanārāyaṇārcane ..
vidhānaṃ sopacāraṃ ca hyupadeṣṭuṃ tvamarhasi .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
॥निषाद उवाच ॥ ॥
अहो किमिति माहात्म्यं सत्यनारायणार्चने ॥
विधानं सोपचारं च ह्युपदेष्टुं त्वमर्हसि ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: The Niṣāda said: / Ah, what is the majesty of the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa? / Truly, you ought to teach me the procedure along with its ritual services.

3.2.s:
sādhūnāṃ samacittānāmupakāravatāṃ satām ..
na gopyaṃ vidyate kiṃcidārtānāmārtināśanam .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
साधूनां समचित्तानामुपकारवतां सताम् ॥
न गोप्यं विद्यते किंचिदार्तानामार्तिनाशनम् ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: For virtuous people, even-minded and benevolent, / nothing is to be kept secret from the distressed that removes their distress.

3.2.s:
iti pṛṣṭo vidhiṃ vaktumitihāsamathābravīt ..
candracūḍo mahīpālaḥ kedāramaṇipūrake .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
इति पृष्टो विधिं वक्तुमितिहासमथाब्रवीत् ॥
चन्द्रचूडो महीपालः केदारमणिपूरके ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: Being thus asked to speak of the rite, he then recounted an ancient story: / King Candracūḍa, [dwelling] in Kedāramaṇipūraka,

3.2.s:
mamāśramaṃ samāyātaḥ satyanārāyaṇārcane ..
vidhānaṃ śrotukāmo'sau māmāha sādaraṃ vacaḥ .. 3.2.27.10 ..
3.2.d:
ममाश्रमं समायातः सत्यनारायणार्चने ॥
विधानं श्रोतुकामोऽसौ मामाह सादरं वचः ॥ 3.2.27.10 ॥
3.2.m: came to my hermitage desiring to hear the procedure / for the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa, and addressed respectful words to me.

3.2.s:
mayā yatkathitaṃtasmai tannibodha niṣādaja ..
saṃkalpya manasā kāmaṃ niṣkāmo vā janaḥ kvacit .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
मया यत्कथितंतस्मै तन्निबोध निषादज ॥
संकल्प्य मनसा कामं निष्कामो वा जनः क्वचित् ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: Hear what was told to him by me, O son of a Niṣāda: / Having mentally resolved upon a wish, or even being free of desire, a person at any time,

3.2.s:
godhūmacūrṇaṃ pādārdhaṃ seṭakādyaiḥ sucūrṇakam ..
saṃskṛtaṃ madhugaṃdhājyairnaivedyaṃ vibhave'rpayet .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
गोधूमचूर्णं पादार्धं सेटकाद्यैः सुचूर्णकम् ॥
संस्कृतं मधुगंधाज्यैर्नैवेद्यं विभवेऽर्पयेत् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: [taking] one and a quarter seṭaka of wheat flour, finely ground, / prepared with honey, fragrant substances, and ghee, should offer it as naivedya according to his wealth.

3.2.s:
paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya candanādyaiśca pūjayet ..
pāyasāpūpasaṃyāvadadhikṣīramathoharet .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
पंचामृतेन संस्नाप्य चन्दनाद्यैश्च पूजयेत् ॥
पायसापूपसंयावदधिक्षीरमथोहरेत् ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Having bathed [the deity] with the five nectars, one should worship with sandalwood and the like; / one should then offer pāyasa, apūpa cakes, saṃyāva, curds, and milk.

3.2.s:
uccāvacaḥ phalaiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpaimarnoramaiḥ ..
pūjayetparayā bhaktyā vibhave sati vistaraiḥ .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
उच्चावचः फलैः पुष्पैर्धूपदीपैमर्नोरमैः ॥
पूजयेत्परया भक्त्या विभवे सति विस्तरैः ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: With varied fruits, flowers, incense, and charming lamps, / one should worship with supreme devotion, with elaborations if wealth is available.

3.2.s:
na tuṣyeddravyasaṃbhārairbhaktyā kevalayā yathā ..
bhagavānparitaḥ pūrṇo na mānaṃ vṛṇuyātkvacit .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
न तुष्येद्द्रव्यसंभारैर्भक्त्या केवलया यथा ॥
भगवान्परितः पूर्णो न मानं वृणुयात्क्वचित् ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: He is not pleased by heaps of material goods as He is by devotion alone; / the Lord is completely full on all sides and never seeks outward honour.

3.2.s:
duryodhanakṛtāṃ tyatkvā rājapūjāṃ janārdanaḥ ..
vidurasyāśrame vāsamātithyaṃ jagṛhe vibhuḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
दुर्योधनकृतां त्यत्क्वा राजपूजां जनार्दनः ॥
विदुरस्याश्रमे वासमातिथ्यं जगृहे विभुः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Leaving aside the royal worship performed by Duryodhana, Janārdana, / the Lord, accepted a dwelling and hospitality at the hermitage of Vidura.

3.2.s:
sudāmnastaṃḍulakaṇāñjagdhvā mānuṣyadurlabhāḥ ..
saṃpado'dāddhariḥ prītyā bhaktimātramapekṣyate .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
सुदाम्नस्तंडुलकणाञ्जग्ध्वा मानुष्यदुर्लभाः ॥
संपदोऽदाद्धरिः प्रीत्या भक्तिमात्रमपेक्ष्यते ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: Having eaten the grains of rice from Sudāman, Hari gladly gave / riches difficult for mortals to attain; He looks only for devotion.

3.2.s:
gopo gṛdhro vaṇigvyādho hanumānsavibhīṣaṇaḥ ..
ye'nye pāpātmakā daityā vṛtrakāyādhavādayaḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
गोपो गृध्रो वणिग्व्याधो हनुमान्सविभीषणः ॥
येऽन्ये पापात्मका दैत्या वृत्रकायाधवादयः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: The cowherd, the vulture, the merchant, the hunter, Hanumān along with Vibhīṣaṇa, / and others who were sinful daityas, beginning with Vṛtra and Kayādhu,

3.2.s:
nārāyaṇāntikaṃ prāpya modaṃte'dyāpi yadvaśāḥ ..
iti śrutvā narapatiḥ pūjāsaṃbhāramādarāt .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
नारायणान्तिकं प्राप्य मोदंतेऽद्यापि यद्वशाः ॥
इति श्रुत्वा नरपतिः पूजासंभारमादरात् ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: having reached the presence of Nārāyaṇa, rejoice even today under His control. / Hearing this, the ruler of men reverently [gathered] the worship materials,

3.2.s:
kṛtavānsa dhanaṃ labdhvā modate narmadātaṭe ..
niṣāda tvamapi prītyā satyanārāyaṇaṃ bhaja .. 3.2.27.20 ..
3.2.d:
कृतवान्स धनं लब्ध्वा मोदते नर्मदातटे ॥
निषाद त्वमपि प्रीत्या सत्यनारायणं भज ॥ 3.2.27.20 ॥
3.2.m: performed [the worship], and having obtained wealth, rejoices on the bank of the Narmadā. / O Niṣāda, you too worship Satyanārāyaṇa with love;

3.2.s:
iha loke sukhaṃ prāpya cānte sānnidhyamāpnuyāḥ ..
kṛtakṛtyo niṣādo'bhūtpraṇamya dvijapuṃgavam .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
इह लोके सुखं प्राप्य चान्ते सान्निध्यमाप्नुयाः ॥
कृतकृत्यो निषादोऽभूत्प्रणम्य द्विजपुंगवम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: having attained happiness in this world, at the end you will obtain His presence. / Having bowed to the eminent twice-born, the Niṣāda became fulfilled in his purpose.

3.2.s:
sa gatvā svagaṇānāha māhātmyaṃ harisevane ..
te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve samayaṃ cakrurādṛtāḥ .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
स गत्वा स्वगणानाह माहात्म्यं हरिसेवने ॥
ते हृष्टमनसः सर्वे समयं चक्रुरादृताः ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: Going to his people, he told of the majesty in serving Hari; / with delighted minds, all of them reverently made an agreement:

3.2.s:
satyanārāyaṇe pūjāṃ kāṣṭhalabdhena yāvatā ..
vayaṃ kulaiḥ kariṣyāmaḥ puṇyavṛkṣavidhānataḥ .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यनारायणे पूजां काष्ठलब्धेन यावता ॥
वयं कुलैः करिष्यामः पुण्यवृक्षविधानतः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: "With as much [gain] as is obtained from wood, we, along with our families, / will perform the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa according to the rule of the sacred tree."

3.2.s:
iti niścitya manasā kāṣṭhaṃ vikrīya lebhire ..
caturguṇaṃ dhanaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ svaṃsvaṃ bhavanamāyayuḥ ..24..
3.2.d:
इति निश्चित्य मनसा काष्ठं विक्रीय लेभिरे ॥
चतुर्गुणं धनं हृष्टाः स्वंस्वं भवनमाययुः ॥24॥
3.2.m: Having so resolved in their minds, they sold the wood and obtained / fourfold wealth; delighted, they went each to his own home.

3.2.s:
mudā strībhyassamācakhyurvṛttāṃtaṃ sarvamāditaḥ..
tāḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pūjanaṃ cakrurādarāt ..25..
3.2.d:
मुदा स्त्रीभ्यस्समाचख्युर्वृत्तांतं सर्वमादितः॥
ताः श्रुत्वा हृष्टमनसः पूजनं चक्रुरादरात् ॥25॥
3.2.m: With joy, they reported the entire matter from the beginning to their wives; / hearing it, with delighted minds, they reverently performed the worship.

3.2.s:
kathānte praṇamanbhaktyā prasādaṃ jagṛhustataḥ ..
svajātibhyaḥ parebhyaśca dadustaccūrṇamuttamam .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
कथान्ते प्रणमन्भक्त्या प्रसादं जगृहुस्ततः ॥
स्वजातिभ्यः परेभ्यश्च ददुस्तच्चूर्णमुत्तमम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: At the end of the narrative, bowing with devotion, they then took the prasāda; / they gave that excellent flour-preparation to their own kin and to others.

3.2.s:
pūjāprabhāvato bhillāḥ putradārādibhiryutāḥ ..
labdhvā bhūmitale dravyaṃ jñānacakṣurmahottamam .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
पूजाप्रभावतो भिल्लाः पुत्रदारादिभिर्युताः ॥
लब्ध्वा भूमितले द्रव्यं ज्ञानचक्षुर्महोत्तमम् ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: By the power of the worship, the Bhillas, accompanied by sons, wives, and others, / having obtained wealth upon the earth and the supreme eye of knowledge,

3.2.s:
bhuktvā bhogānyatheṣṭante daridrāndhā dvijottama ..
jagmuste vaiṣṇavaṃ dhāma yogināmapi durlabham .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
भुक्त्वा भोगान्यथेष्टन्ते दरिद्रान्धा द्विजोत्तम ॥
जग्मुस्ते वैष्णवं धाम योगिनामपि दुर्लभम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: and having enjoyed worldly pleasures to their heart's content, O best of the twice-born, those formerly poor and blind / went to the realm of Viṣṇu, difficult even for yogins to reach.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha te varṇayiṣyāmi kathāṃ sādhūpacāritām ..
nṛpopadeśataḥ sādhuḥ kṛtārtho'bhūdvaṇigyathā.. .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ ते वर्णयिष्यामि कथां साधूपचारिताम् ॥
नृपोपदेशतः साधुः कृतार्थोऽभूद्वणिग्यथा॥ ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Now I shall relate to you the story celebrated by good people, / how, through the instruction of the king, the merchant Sādhu achieved his purpose.

3.2.s:
maṇipūrapatī rājā candracūḍo mahāyaśāḥ ..
saha prajābhirānarca satyanārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
मणिपूरपती राजा चन्द्रचूडो महायशाः ॥
सह प्रजाभिरानर्च सत्यनारायणं प्रभुम् ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: The renowned King Candracūḍa, lord of Maṇipūra, / along with his subjects, worshipped the Lord Satyanārāyaṇa.

3.2.s:
atha ratnapurasthāyī sādhurlakṣapatirvaṇik ..
dhanairāpūrya taraṇīḥ saha gacchannadītaṭe .. 3 ..
3.2.d:
अथ रत्नपुरस्थायी साधुर्लक्षपतिर्वणिक् ॥
धनैरापूर्य तरणीः सह गच्छन्नदीतटे ॥ 3 ॥
3.2.m: Then the merchant Sādhu, residing in Ratnapura, a possessor of hundreds of thousands, / having filled boats with wealth, travelling along the riverbank,

3.2.s:
dadarśa bahulaṃ lokaṃ nānāgrāmavilāsinam ..
maṇimuktāviracitairvitānaissamalaṃkṛtam .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
ददर्श बहुलं लोकं नानाग्रामविलासिनम् ॥
मणिमुक्ताविरचितैर्वितानैस्समलंकृतम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: saw a vast gathering of people from various villages revelling, / adorned with canopies made of jewels and pearls.

3.2.s:
vedavādāṃśca śuśrāva gītavāditrasaṃgatān ..
ramyaṃ sthānaṃ samālokya karṇadhāraṃ samādiśat .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
वेदवादांश्च शुश्राव गीतवादित्रसंगतान् ॥
रम्यं स्थानं समालोक्य कर्णधारं समादिशत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: He also heard Vedic recitations accompanied by song and musical instruments. / Looking upon that charming place, he ordered the helmsman:

3.2.s:
viśrāmayātra taraṇīriti paśyāmi kautukam ..
bhartrādiṣṭastathā cakre karṇadhāraḥ sabhṛtyakaiḥ .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
विश्रामयात्र तरणीरिति पश्यामि कौतुकम् ॥
भर्त्रादिष्टस्तथा चक्रे कर्णधारः सभृत्यकैः ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: "Rest the boats here, so that I may see this spectacle." / Commanded by his master, the helmsman did so along with the servants.

3.2.s:
taṭasīmnaḥ samuttīrya mallalīlāvilāsinaḥ ..
karṇadhārā nagā vīrā yuyudhurmallalīlayā .. 7 ..
3.2.d:
तटसीम्नः समुत्तीर्य मल्ललीलाविलासिनः ॥
कर्णधारा नगा वीरा युयुधुर्मल्ललीलया ॥ 7 ॥
3.2.m: Disembarking onto the riverbank, the helmsmen, brave like mountains, / delighting in wrestling sport, fought in wrestling matches.

3.2.s:
svayamuttīrya sāmātyo lokānpapraccha sādaram ..
yajñasthānaṃ samālokya praśastaṃ samudo yayau ..8..
3.2.d:
स्वयमुत्तीर्य सामात्यो लोकान्पप्रच्छ सादरम् ॥
यज्ञस्थानं समालोक्य प्रशस्तं समुदो ययौ ॥8॥
3.2.m: He himself disembarked with his minister and respectfully questioned the people; / looking upon the splendid place of sacrifice, he went filled with joy.

3.2.s:
kimatra kriyate sabhyā bhavadbhirlokapūjitaiḥ ..
sabhyā ūcuśca te sarve satyanārāyaṇo vibhuḥ .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
किमत्र क्रियते सभ्या भवद्भिर्लोकपूजितैः ॥
सभ्या ऊचुश्च ते सर्वे सत्यनारायणो विभुः ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: "O assembly members honoured by the world, what is being done here by you?" / The assembly members all said: "The all-pervading Lord Satyanārāyaṇa

3.2.s:
pūjyate baṃdhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājñā lokānukaṃpinā ..
prāptaṃ niṣkaṭakaṃ rājyaṃ satyanārāyaṇārcanāt .. 3.2.28.10 ..
3.2.d:
पूज्यते बंधुभिः सार्धं राज्ञा लोकानुकंपिना ॥
प्राप्तं निष्कटकं राज्यं सत्यनारायणार्चनात् ॥ 3.2.28.10 ॥
3.2.m: is being worshipped, along with his kinsmen, by the king who is compassionate to the people; / an unobstructed kingdom was obtained through the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa.

3.2.s:
dhanārthī labhate dravyaṃ putrārthī sutamuttamam ..
jñānārthī labhate cakṣurnirbhayaḥ syādbhayāturaḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
धनार्थी लभते द्रव्यं पुत्रार्थी सुतमुत्तमम् ॥
ज्ञानार्थी लभते चक्षुर्निर्भयः स्याद्भयातुरः ॥ 11 ॥
3.2.m: One desiring wealth obtains riches; one desiring a son obtains an excellent son; / one desiring knowledge obtains vision; one afflicted by fear becomes free of fear.

3.2.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti naraḥ satyasurārca nāt ..
vidhānaṃ tu tataḥ śrutvā cailaṃ baddhvā gale'sakṛt .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति नरः सत्यसुरार्च नात् ॥
विधानं तु ततः श्रुत्वा चैलं बद्ध्वा गलेऽसकृत् ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: A person attains all desires through the worship of the God of Truth." / Then, hearing the ritual procedure, binding a cloth around his neck repeatedly,

3.2.s:
daṃḍavatpraṇipatyāha kāmaṃ sabhyānamodayat ..
anapatyo'smi bhagavanvṛthaiśvaryo vṛthodyamaḥ .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
दंडवत्प्रणिपत्याह कामं सभ्यानमोदयत् ॥
अनपत्योऽस्मि भगवन्वृथैश्वर्यो वृथोद्यमः ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: prostrating like a stick, he spoke his desire and gladdened the assembly members: / "O Lord, I am childless; my wealth is in vain and my effort is in vain.

3.2.s:
putraṃ vā yadi vā kanyāṃ labheyaṃ tvatprasādataḥ ..
patākāṃ kāṃcanīṃ kṛtvā pūjayiṣye kṛpānidhim .. 14 ..
3.2.d:
पुत्रं वा यदि वा कन्यां लभेयं त्वत्प्रसादतः ॥
पताकां कांचनीं कृत्वा पूजयिष्ये कृपानिधिम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.2.m: If by your grace I should obtain a son or even a daughter, / having made a golden banner, I will worship that ocean of compassion."

3.2.s:
śrutvā sabhyā abruvaṃste kāmanāsiddhirastu te ..
hariṃ praṇamya sabhyāśca prasādaṃ bhuktavāṃstadā .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
श्रुत्वा सभ्या अब्रुवंस्ते कामनासिद्धिरस्तु ते ॥
हरिं प्रणम्य सभ्याश्च प्रसादं भुक्तवांस्तदा ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Hearing this, the assembly members said to him: "May your wish be fulfilled." / Having bowed to Hari and the assembly members, he then ate the prasāda.

3.2.s:
jagāma svālayaṃ sādhurmanasā ciṃtayanharim..
svagṛhe hyāgate tasminnāryo maṃgalapāṇayaḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
जगाम स्वालयं साधुर्मनसा चिंतयन्हरिम्॥
स्वगृहे ह्यागते तस्मिन्नार्यो मंगलपाणयः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: The merchant went to his own home, contemplating Hari in his mind. / When he arrived at his own house, the noble women with auspicious articles in their hands

3.2.s:
maṃgalāni vicitrāṇi yathocitamakārayan ..
viveśāṃtaḥpure sādhurmahākautukamaṃgalaḥ .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
मंगलानि विचित्राणि यथोचितमकारयन् ॥
विवेशांतःपुरे साधुर्महाकौतुकमंगलः ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: performed diverse auspicious rites as was fitting; / the merchant entered the inner apartments amidst great festivities and auspicious rites.

3.2.s:
ṛtusnātā satī līlāvatī paryacaratpatim ..
garbhaṃ dhṛtavatī sādhvī samaye suṣuve tu sā .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
ऋतुस्नाता सती लीलावती पर्यचरत्पतिम् ॥
गर्भं धृतवती साध्वी समये सुषुवे तु सा ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: Having bathed after her menstrual period, the virtuous Līlāvatī attended upon her husband; / the chaste woman conceived, and in due time she gave birth

3.2.s:
kanyāṃ kamalalolākṣīṃ bāṃdhavāmodakāriṇīm ..
sādhuḥ parāṃ mudaṃ lebhe vitatāra dhanaṃ bahu .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
कन्यां कमललोलाक्षीं बांधवामोदकारिणीम् ॥
साधुः परां मुदं लेभे विततार धनं बहु ॥ 19 ॥
3.2.m: to a daughter with unsteady eyes like lotus petals, who brought joy to her kin. / The merchant attained supreme joy and distributed much wealth.

3.2.s:
viprānāhūya vedajñānkārayāmāsa maṃgalam ..
lekhayitvā janmapatrīṃ nāma cakre kalāvatīm .. 3.2.28.20 ..
3.2.d:
विप्रानाहूय वेदज्ञान्कारयामास मंगलम् ॥
लेखयित्वा जन्मपत्रीं नाम चक्रे कलावतीम् ॥ 3.2.28.20 ॥
3.2.m: Summoning brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas, he had the auspicious rites performed; / having had her horoscope written, he named her Kalāvatī.

3.2.s:
kalānidhikale vāsau vavṛdhe sā kalāvatī ..
aṣṭavarṣā bhavedgaurī navavarṣā ca rohiṇī .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
कलानिधिकले वासौ ववृधे सा कलावती ॥
अष्टवर्षा भवेद्गौरी नववर्षा च रोहिणी ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: Like a digit of the moon, she, Kalāvatī, grew. / At eight years of age she would be a Gaurī, and at nine years a Rohiṇī.

3.2.s:
daśavarṣā bhavetkanyā tataḥ prauḍhā rajasvalā ..
prauḍhāṃ kālena tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vivāhārthamacintayat .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
दशवर्षा भवेत्कन्या ततः प्रौढा रजस्वला ॥
प्रौढां कालेन तां दृष्ट्वा विवाहार्थमचिन्तयत् ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m: At ten years old she is a kanyā; thereafter, mature, having her menses. / Seeing that she had matured in time, he thought of marriage for her.

3.2.s:
nagare kāṃcanapure vaṇikchaṃkhapatiḥ śrutaḥ ..
kulīno rūpasaṃpattiśīlaudāryaguṇānvitaḥ .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
नगरे कांचनपुरे वणिक्छंखपतिः श्रुतः ॥
कुलीनो रूपसंपत्तिशीलौदार्यगुणान्वितः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: In the city of Kāñcanapura, a merchant named Śaṅkhapati was renowned, / noble-born, endowed with abundant beauty, good conduct, and generous qualities.

3.2.s:
varayāmāsa taṃ sādhurduhituḥ sadṛśaṃ varam ..
śubhe lagne bahuvidhairmaṃgalairagnisannidhau ..24..
3.2.d:
वरयामास तं साधुर्दुहितुः सदृशं वरम् ॥
शुभे लग्ने बहुविधैर्मंगलैरग्निसन्निधौ ॥24॥
3.2.m: The merchant chose him, a groom worthy of his daughter. / At an auspicious moment, with diverse blessings before the sacred fire,

3.2.s:
vedavāditraninadairdadau kanyāṃ yathāvidhi ..
maṇimuktāpravālāni vasanaṃ bhūṣaṇāni ca .. 25 ..
3.2.d:
वेदवादित्रनिनदैर्ददौ कन्यां यथाविधि ॥
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानि वसनं भूषणानि च ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: with the sounds of the Vedas and musical instruments, he gave away his maiden according to the rule, / and gems, pearls, coral, garments, and ornaments.

3.2.s:
mahāmodamanāḥ sādhurmaṃgalārthaṃ dadau ca ha ..
premṇā nivāsayāmāsa gṛhe jāmātaraṃ tataḥ .. 26 ..
3.2.d:
महामोदमनाः साधुर्मंगलार्थं ददौ च ह ॥
प्रेम्णा निवासयामास गृहे जामातरं ततः ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: With great joy in his heart, the merchant gave them for the sake of blessing, / and out of affection he made his son-in-law reside in his house.

3.2.s:
taṃ mene putravatsādhuḥ sa ca taṃ pitṛvatsudhīḥ ..
atīte bhūyasaḥ kāle satyanārāyaṇārcanam .. 27 ..
3.2.d:
तं मेने पुत्रवत्साधुः स च तं पितृवत्सुधीः ॥
अतीते भूयसः काले सत्यनारायणार्चनम् ॥ 27 ॥
3.2.m: The merchant regarded him like a son, and that wise man regarded him like a father. / When much time had passed, the worship of Satyanārāyaṇa

3.2.s:
vismṛtya saha jāmātrā vāṇijyāya yayau punaḥ ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha sādhuḥ samādāya ratnāni vividhāni ca .. 28 ..
3.2.d:
विस्मृत्य सह जामात्रा वाणिज्याय ययौ पुनः ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ साधुः समादाय रत्नानि विविधानि च ॥ 28 ॥
3.2.m: he forgot, and went again with his son-in-law to engage in trade. / Sūta said: / Then the merchant, taking diverse gems,

3.2.s:
naukāḥ saṃsthāpya sa yayau deśāddeśāntaraṃ prati ..
nagaraṃ narmadātīre tatra vāsaṃ cakāra saḥ ..29..
3.2.d:
नौकाः संस्थाप्य स ययौ देशाद्देशान्तरं प्रति ॥
नगरं नर्मदातीरे तत्र वासं चकार सः ॥29॥
3.2.m: and outfitting boats, journeyed from country to country. / There was a city on the bank of the Narmadā, and there he made his abode.

3.2.s:
kurvankrayaṃ vikrayaṃ ca ciraṃ tasthau mahāmanāḥ ..
karmaṇā manasā vācā na kṛtaṃ satyasevanam .. 3.2.28.30 ..
3.2.d:
कुर्वन्क्रयं विक्रयं च चिरं तस्थौ महामनाः ॥
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा न कृतं सत्यसेवनम् ॥ 3.2.28.30 ॥
3.2.m: Buying and selling, the great-minded man stayed for a long time. / In deed, mind, and speech, no service to Satya was performed [by him].

3.2.s:
tataḥ karmavipākena tāpamāpācirādvaṇik ..
kasmiṃściddivase rātrau rājño gehe tamovṛteḥ.. 31 ..
3.2.d:
ततः कर्मविपाकेन तापमापाचिराद्वणिक् ॥
कस्मिंश्चिद्दिवसे रात्रौ राज्ञो गेहे तमोवृतेः॥ 31 ॥
3.2.m: Then, through the fruition of his past deeds, the merchant soon incurred suffering. / On a certain day, in a night enveloped in darkness, in the king's house,

3.2.s:
jñātvā nidrāgatānsarvānhṛtaṃ caurairmahādhanam ..
prabhāte vācito rājā sūtamāgadhabaṃdibhiḥ .. .. 32 ..
3.2.d:
ज्ञात्वा निद्रागतान्सर्वान्हृतं चौरैर्महाधनम् ॥
प्रभाते वाचितो राजा सूतमागधबंदिभिः ॥ ॥ 32 ॥
3.2.m: knowing that everyone had gone to sleep, great wealth was stolen by thieves. / At dawn, the king was awakened by sūtas, māgadhas, and bards.

3.2.s:
prātaḥkṛtyaṃ nṛpaḥ kṛtvā sadaḥ saṃprāviśacca saḥ ..
tatastatra samāyātaḥ kiṃkaro rājavallabhaḥ .. 33 ..
3.2.d:
प्रातःकृत्यं नृपः कृत्वा सदः संप्राविशच्च सः ॥
ततस्तत्र समायातः किंकरो राजवल्लभः ॥ 33 ॥
3.2.m: Having performed his morning duties, the king entered the assembly hall. / Then an attendant, dear to the king, arrived there

3.2.s:
uvāca sa tadā vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ dharā pate ..
muktāmālāśca bahudhā ratnāni vividhāni ca .. 34 ..
3.2.d:
उवाच स तदा वाक्यं शृणुष्व त्वं धरा पते ॥
मुक्तामालाश्च बहुधा रत्नानि विविधानि च ॥ 34 ॥
3.2.m: and spoke these words at that time: "Listen, lord of the earth! / Many pearl necklaces and diverse jewels,

3.2.s:
mumuṣuścaurā gatāssarve na jānīmo vayaṃ nṛpa ..
iti vijñāpito rājā puṇyaśloka śikhāmaṇiḥ .. 35 ..
3.2.d:
मुमुषुश्चौरा गतास्सर्वे न जानीमो वयं नृप ॥
इति विज्ञापितो राजा पुण्यश्लोक शिखामणिः ॥ 35 ॥
3.2.m: thieves stole, and all have fled; we do not know [where], O king!" / Thus informed, the king, a crest-jewel among the righteous,

3.2.s:
uvāca krodhatāmrākṣo yūyaṃ saṃyāta mā ciram ..
sacauraṃ dravyamādāya matpārśvaṃ tvamupānaya .. 36 ..
3.2.d:
उवाच क्रोधताम्राक्षो यूयं संयात मा चिरम् ॥
सचौरं द्रव्यमादाय मत्पार्श्वं त्वमुपानय ॥ 36 ॥
3.2.m: spoke, his eyes copper-red with rage: "Go forth! Do not delay! / Recovering the wealth along with the thief, bring [them] before me!

3.2.s:
no ceddhaniṣye sagaṇāniti dūtānsamādiśat ..
nṛpavākyaṃ samākarṇya prajagmuste ca kiṃkarāḥ .. 37 ..
3.2.d:
नो चेद्धनिष्ये सगणानिति दूतान्समादिशत् ॥
नृपवाक्यं समाकर्ण्य प्रजग्मुस्ते च किंकराः ॥ 37 ॥
3.2.m: Otherwise, I shall slay you along with your retinue!" Thus he commanded the messengers. / Hearing the king's words, those servants departed.

3.2.s:
bahuyatnairna saṃśodhya dravyaṃ corasamanvitam ..
ekībhūtvā niśi tadā mahāciṃtāturo'bhavat .. 38 ..
3.2.d:
बहुयत्नैर्न संशोध्य द्रव्यं चोरसमन्वितम् ॥
एकीभूत्वा निशि तदा महाचिंतातुरोऽभवत् ॥ 38 ॥
3.2.m: Having failed to find the wealth together with the thief despite many efforts, / coming together at night, [their leader] became deeply distressed with worry:

3.2.s:
hantā māṃ sagaṇaṃ rājā kiṃ karomi kutaḥ sukham ..
nṛpadaṃḍācca me mṛtyuḥ pretatvāya bhavediha .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
हन्ता मां सगणं राजा किं करोमि कुतः सुखम् ॥
नृपदंडाच्च मे मृत्युः प्रेतत्वाय भवेदिह ॥ 39 ॥
3.2.m: "The king will kill me along with my retinue! What shall I do? Whence can happiness come? / If I die by the king's punishment, it would lead to existence as a preta in this world;

3.2.s:
narmadāyāṃ ca maraṇaṃ śivalokapradāyakam ..
ityevaṃ saṃmataṃ kṛtvā narmadāyāstaṭaṃ yayuḥ .. 3.2.28.40 ..
3.2.d:
नर्मदायां च मरणं शिवलोकप्रदायकम् ॥
इत्येवं संमतं कृत्वा नर्मदायास्तटं ययुः ॥ 3.2.28.40 ॥
3.2.m: but death in the Narmadā bestows the world of Śiva!" / Having agreed on this, they went to the bank of the Narmadā.

3.2.s:
videśino'sya vaṇijo dadarśa vipulaṃ dhanam ..
muktāhāraṃ gale tasya luṃṭhitaṃ vaṇijo'sya ca .. 41 ..
3.2.d:
विदेशिनोऽस्य वणिजो ददर्श विपुलं धनम् ॥
मुक्ताहारं गले तस्य लुंठितं वणिजोऽस्य च ॥ 41 ॥
3.2.m: He saw the vast wealth of this foreign merchant; / a pearl necklace was around his neck, and [the wealth] of this merchant was plundered.

3.2.s:
cauro'yamiti niścitya tau babaṃdhātmarakṣaṇāt ..
sadhanaṃ saha jāmātrā nṛpāntikamupānayat .. 42 ..
3.2.d:
चौरोऽयमिति निश्चित्य तौ बबंधात्मरक्षणात् ॥
सधनं सह जामात्रा नृपान्तिकमुपानयत् ॥ 42 ॥
3.2.m: Deciding, "This is the thief," to save himself he bound the two of them, / and brought [the merchant] with his wealth, along with his son-in-law, before the king.

3.2.s:
pratikūle harau tasminrājñāpi na vicāritam ..
dhanāgāre dhanaṃ nītvā badhnīta tau sudurmatī .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
प्रतिकूले हरौ तस्मिन्राज्ञापि न विचारितम् ॥
धनागारे धनं नीत्वा बध्नीत तौ सुदुर्मती ॥ 43 ॥
3.2.m: Since Hari was displeased with him, the king also did not investigate: / "Taking the wealth to the treasury, bind those two very wicked men

3.2.s:
kārāgāre lohamayaiḥ śṛṃkhalairaṃgapādayoḥ ..
iti rājājñayā dūtāstathā cakrurnibaṃdhanam .. 44 ..
3.2.d:
कारागारे लोहमयैः शृंखलैरंगपादयोः ॥
इति राजाज्ञया दूतास्तथा चक्रुर्निबंधनम् ॥ 44 ॥
3.2.m: in the prison, with iron shackles upon their limbs and feet!" / By the king's command, the messengers bound them accordingly.

3.2.s:
jāmātrā sahitaḥ sādhurvilalāpa bhṛśaṃ muhuḥ ..
hā putra tāta tāteti jāmātaḥ kva dhanaṃ gatam .. 45 ..
3.2.d:
जामात्रा सहितः साधुर्विललाप भृशं मुहुः ॥
हा पुत्र तात तातेति जामातः क्व धनं गतम् ॥ 45 ॥
3.2.m: Together with his son-in-law, the merchant wailed exceedingly, again and again: / "Alas, son! Father! Father! O son-in-law, where has our wealth gone?

3.2.s:
kva sthitā ca sutā bhāryā paśya dhāturviparyayam ..
nimagnau duḥkhajaladhau ko vāṃ pāsyati saṃkaṭāt .. 46 ..
3.2.d:
क्व स्थिता च सुता भार्या पश्य धातुर्विपर्ययम् ॥
निमग्नौ दुःखजलधौ को वां पास्यति संकटात् ॥ 46 ॥
3.2.m: Where are my daughter and wife? Behold the adverse turn of fate! / Plunged into an ocean of sorrow, who will protect you both from distress?

3.2.s:
mayā bahutaraṃ dhāturvipriyaṃ hi purākṛtam ..
tatkarmaṇaḥ prabhāvo'yaṃ na jāne kasya vā phalam .. 47 ..
3.2.d:
मया बहुतरं धातुर्विप्रियं हि पुराकृतम् ॥
तत्कर्मणः प्रभावोऽयं न जाने कस्य वा फलम् ॥ 47 ॥
3.2.m: Indeed, I did much that was displeasing to the Creator in the past; / this is the power of that karma, or whose fruit is it? I do not know!"

3.2.s: samaṃ śvaśurajāmātrau dvādaśeṣu viṣādinau .. 48 ..
3.2.d: समं श्वशुरजामात्रौ द्वादशेषु विषादिनौ ॥ 48 ॥
3.2.m: Together, father-in-law and son-in-law, sorrowful, [remained] for twelve [years].

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tāpatrayaharaṃ viṣṇoścaritaṃ tasya te śivam ..
śṛṇvaṃti sudhiyo nityaṃ te vasaṃti hareḥ padam .. .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
तापत्रयहरं विष्णोश्चरितं तस्य ते शिवम् ॥
शृण्वंति सुधियो नित्यं ते वसंति हरेः पदम् ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m: Sūta said: / The auspicious conduct of that Viṣṇu removes the threefold suffering; / the wise who listen to it constantly dwell in Hari's abode.

3.2.s:
pratikūle harau tasminyāsyanti nirayānbahūn ..
tatpriyā kamalā devī catvārastasya cātmajāḥ .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
प्रतिकूले हरौ तस्मिन्यास्यन्ति निरयान्बहून् ॥
तत्प्रिया कमला देवी चत्वारस्तस्य चात्मजाः ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: When Hari is displeased with someone, they will go to many hells. / His beloved goddess Kamalā has four sons:

3.2.s:
dharmo yajño nṛpaścauraḥ sarve lakṣmīpriyaṃkarāḥ ..
viprebhyaścātithibhyaśca yaddānaṃ dharma ucyate..3 ..
3.2.d:
धर्मो यज्ञो नृपश्चौरः सर्वे लक्ष्मीप्रियंकराः ॥
विप्रेभ्यश्चातिथिभ्यश्च यद्दानं धर्म उच्यते॥3 ॥
3.2.m: dharma, sacrifice, the king, and the thief; all of them please Lakṣmī. / That gift which is given to Brahmins and guests is called dharma.

3.2.s:
mātṛbhyo devatābhyaśca svadhā svāheti vai makhaḥ ..
dharmasyaiva makhasyaiva rakṣako nṛpatiḥ smṛtaḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
मातृभ्यो देवताभ्यश्च स्वधा स्वाहेति वै मखः ॥
धर्मस्यैव मखस्यैव रक्षको नृपतिः स्मृतः ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: What is offered to the ancestors with svadhā and to the deities with svāhā is indeed sacrifice; / the protector of dharma and of sacrifice is known to be the king.

3.2.s:
dvayorhantā hi coraḥ sa te sarve dharmakiṃkarāḥ ..
yatra satyaṃ tato dharmastatra lakṣmīḥ sthirā bhavet ..5..
3.2.d:
द्वयोर्हन्ता हि चोरः स ते सर्वे धर्मकिंकराः ॥
यत्र सत्यं ततो धर्मस्तत्र लक्ष्मीः स्थिरा भवेत् ॥5॥
3.2.m: The thief is the destroyer of both; yet they all serve dharma. / Where truth is, there is dharma; where dharma is, Lakṣmī remains steadfast.

3.2.s:
satyahīnasya tatsādhordhanaṃ yattadgrahe sthitam ..
hṛtavānavanīpālaḥ caurairbhāryātiduḥkhitā .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
सत्यहीनस्य तत्साधोर्धनं यत्तद्ग्रहे स्थितम् ॥
हृतवानवनीपालः चौरैर्भार्यातिदुःखिता ॥ 6 ॥
